title: revdep does not support Bioconductor repositories beyond the software one
description: **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** When working with Bioconductor packages, `revdep()` only extracts the information from the Bioconductor software packages. However, there are more types: annotation, experiment data, workflows, and books. So those dependencies are missed. See ```R > devtools::revdep("SpatialExperiment", recursive = TRUE, bioconductor = TRUE) 'getOption("repos")' replaces Bioconductor standard repositories, see '?repositories' for details replacement repositories: CRAN: https://cloud.r-project.org/ [1] "ExperimentSubset" "mistyR" ``` which misses several packages: **Describe the solution you'd like** I wrote the following code going by what `devtools` already does. I can modify it and submit it as a PR if you think that's ok. ```R packages_all <- function() { repos <- BiocManager::repositories() views <- paste(repos[grepl("BioC", names(repos))], "VIEWS", sep = "/") views <- views[!grepl("books", views)] all_pkgs <- c(lapply(views, devtools:::bioc_packages), list("CRAN" = devtools:::cran_packages())) Reduce(function(...) merge(..., all = TRUE), all_pkgs) } revdep_all <- function(pkg, dependencies = c("Depends", "Imports", "Suggests", "LinkingTo"), recursive = FALSE, ignore = NULL, bioconductor = FALSE) { if (missing(pkg)) pkg <- as.package(".")$package all <- if (bioconductor) packages_all() else devtools:::cran_packages() deps <- tools::dependsOnPkgs(pkg, dependencies, recursive, installed = all) deps <- setdiff(deps, ignore) devtools:::sort_ci(deps) } ``` The end result is this one: ```R > revdep_all("SpatialExperiment", recursive = TRUE, bioconductor = TRUE) 'getOption("repos")' replaces Bioconductor standard repositories, see '?repositories' for details replacement repositories: CRAN: https://cloud.r-project.org/ [1] "BayesSpace" "ExperimentSubset" "miloR" [4] "mistyR" "MouseGastrulationData" "SingleCellMultiModal" [7] "spatialLIBD" "STexampleData" "TENxVisiumData" ``` **Describe alternatives you've considered** In my `packages_all()` code there's a little detail that "books" is a new Bioconductor repository and it doesn't have the `VIEWS` that others do have. Another option would be to use `tryCatch()` and test all the `views` instead of dropping `books`. **Additional context** I'm trying to list at https://github.com/lmweber/OSTA-book all the software related to `SpatialExperiment` that readers might want to check out. Thanks!

title: add function to check if package names are single quoted
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The CRAN policy states that the user should single quote package names in the title as well in the description section of the DESCRIPTION file. See [Checklist for CRAN submissions](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/submission_checklist.html)

'Put non-English usage, including names of other packages and external software, in single quotes. Example: 'OpenSSL'. '

**Describe the solution you'd like**
```

# Alert User to remind CRAN policy for package mentioning

pcks <- utils::available.packages() # get all packages in CRAN
package_names <- base::rownames(pcks) # extract just the package names


# sample string from a Description file
# can be also a Title or the Description section itself.
# for real usage, one has to find a way to read both section from DESCRIPTION file as a string. One per section.
s <- "I use the 'ggplot2' package for plotting awesome plots.
      I also use 'tidyverse' a lot." 

s <- gsub(".,;\"?!", "",s)
s <- base::unlist(base::strsplit(s," ")) 
findings <- base::intersect(s,package_names)

if (base::length(findings) > 0 ){
base::stop(base::paste("change:",
            paste0(findings," --> ","'",findings,"' ")))
}
# prints no error, as the packages are referred correctly with single quotes.

s <- "I use the ggplot2 package for plotting awesome plots.
      I also use tidyverse a lot" 

s <- gsub(".,;\"?!", "",s)
s <- base::unlist(base::strsplit(s," ")) 
findings <- base::intersect(s,package_names)

if (base::length(findings) > 0 ){
base::stop(base::paste("change:",
            paste0(findings," --> ","'",findings,"' ")))
}
```

The basic idea is to retive the known package names and map those with each word of the DESCRIPTION file.
it should return the names of the packages that are not single quoted. Also double quoted packages should be printed as error, as it is different to single quotes.

title: copy vignettes to inst/doc after calling document?
description:
This is related to https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/1766.

In RStudio, the default package workflow involves installing the package without building vignettes, which implies that calls to `vignette()` will fail to find your package's vignettes (unless, of course, you run `devtools::load_all()` before your attempt).

However, it's possible for the RStudio install-without-build to work with vignettes if those vignettes are copied to `inst/doc` first. We could do this in RStudio, but it might be reasonable to do this in `devtools` as well.

In this world, the assumption is that the package author only places their vignettes in the `vignettes/` directory, and the `inst/doc/` directory is managed entirely by `devtools`. So, `devtools::document()` would:

1. Remove any old files within `inst/doc/`,
2. Generate documentation + vignettes with `roxygen2` as normal (if the `vignette` roclet is active),
3. Copy the generated vignettes to `inst/doc/`, so they're visible on a later install.

A later call to `R CMD INSTALL` would use the versions of those vignettes copied to `inst/doc/`; if the package author later was preparing a release for CRAN, those older vignettes would be automatically overwritten during build. This implies no extra gunk in `.Rbuildignore` or `.Rinstignore` is required, which is nice.

Let me know if this feels in scope; if not, we'll probably consider a similar strategy in RStudio proper.

title: Issue with multi-line examples
description:
I have been using devtools for a while now, and I have found it has been fantastic. I have found one bug which I think might be worth flagging up.

I have found that there is a problem if you use `#'` to create multi-line comments within your functions, for example:

``` R
#' Title of My Function
#' 
#' Function description
#'
#' @param param1
#' @param param2
#' @param param3
#' 
#'  @return
#'  @export
#' 
#'  @examples
#' 
#'  bar <- "foo"
my_test_function <- function(param1, param2, param3){

#' Multi
#' line
#' comment
print("my test function")

}
```

What I have found is, if I run `devtools::check()`, I will get the following error:

``` 
base::assign(".ptime", proc.time(), pos = "CheckExEnv")
### Name: load_all_db_units
### Title: Load all db units
### Aliases: load_all_db_units
### ** Examples

loop over the possible list of unit conversion csv file names
Error: unexpected symbol in "Multi"
Execution halted
```

This is remedied when I replace `#'` with `#` within the function. 
It's absolutely fine if `#'` is not allowed within function, but it may
be useful to have a warning/error which tells the user that the 
issue is with the type of comment used, and not with the actual
examples they have made.

Thanks so much!

title: submit_cran should check for outdated date fields
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I'm always frustrated when I r-devel check everything for a CRAN submission and I forget to make sure the date field in DESCRIPTION is updated. Unfortunately, I submitted more than once with a date field older than a month and therefore got rejected with everything else fine, causing unnecessary for the CRAN team and frustration for myself. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I thought it would be cool if `submit_cran` would have warned me and prevented me from pushing up to CRAN. 
Something like adding the below code to https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/blob/56875888a507eedb1a92d820ff8c899e065e653c/R/release.R#L270

would do the job. 


```r
# the force submission if clause is entirely optional to the idea 
# and would allow to force pushes from environments with weird Sys.Date()
if(!force_submission){
  desc_date_diff <- as.Date(desc::desc_get_field("Date")) -
    Sys.Date()
  
  if(desc_date_diff > 28){
    message("Date field in DESCRIPTION may be older than a month compared to Sys.Date(). Aborting upload. This may lead to a CRAN rejection.")
    return(NULL)
  }
}

```

Alternatively to checking `Sys.Date()` one could check some online date service. 

If desired I can create a PR, but thought raising the issue first makes sense.

```
│       ├── app.R
│       └── tests

│               ├── repro_test-expected
│               │   └── repro_test.json
│               └── repro_test.R
└── R
    └── repro.R

6 directories, 5 files

$ cat DESCRIPTION

Title: Repro
Description: This is a description.
Author: Author
Maintainer: Maintainer <main@tain.er>
License: GPL-3
Version: 0.0.1

Suggests: shinytest
Encoding: UTF-8
RoxygenNote: 7.1.2

$ cat inst/shiny/app.R
Sys.setlocale("LC_ALL", "en_US.UTF-8")
shinyApp(repro:::repro_ui(), repro:::repro_server)

$ cat inst/shiny/tests/shinytest/repro_test.R
app <- ShinyDriver$new("../../", seed = 0)
app$snapshotInit("repro_test", screenshot = FALSE)
app$snapshot(filename = "repro_test.json")
# Sys.sleep(120)

$ cat inst/shiny/tests/shinytest/repro_test-expected/repro_test.json 
{
  "input": {
    "X_b": "X_b",
    "Xa": "Xa"
  },
  "output": {

  },
  "export": {

  }
}

$ cat R/repro.R 
repro_server <- function(input, output, session) {}

#' @import shiny
repro_ui <- function() {
  fluidPage(
    selectInput("Xa", "Xa", choices = "Xa"),
    selectInput("X_b", "X_b", choices = "X_b"),
  )
}

#' Run tests
#'
#' @examples
#' run_tests()
#' @export

}

```

From this filestructure, run 

```bash
R -e "shinytest::testApp('inst/shiny')"
```
to verify that the test passes. 

(You can also do
```
R -e "devtools::install(); repro::run_tests()"
```
with the same result: pass.)

Then, run
```bash
R -e "devtools::check()"
```
Then, the same test (run as an example) fails.

To see why, uncomment `Sys.sleep(120)` above and re-run `check()`. While `shinytest` is sleeping, check the output using `find /tmp/ | grep current/repro_test.json`:

```json
{
  "input": {
    "Xa": "Xa",
    "X_b": "X_b"
  },
  "output": {

  },
  "export": {

  }
}
```

Note the sort order is different.

On my system, it is expected that collate settings influence the sort order:

```
 version  R version 4.1.1 (2021-08-10)
 os       openSUSE Leap 15.2          
 system   x86_64, linux-gnu           
 ui       X11                         
 language (EN)                        
 collate  en_US.UTF-8                 
 ctype    en_US.UTF-8                 

```

```bash
$ printf "Xa\nX_b" | LC_COLLATE=en_US sort
Xa
X_b
$ printf "Xa\nX_b" | LC_COLLATE=C sort
X_b
Xa
```

However, we are unable to reproduce this within R:
```bash
$ LC_COLLATE=en_US R -e "sort(c('Xa', 'X_b'))"
> sort(c('Xa', 'X_b'))
[1] "X_b" "Xa" 
> 
$ LC_COLLATE=C R -e "sort(c('Xa', 'X_b'))"
> sort(c('Xa', 'X_b'))
[1] "X_b" "Xa" 
> 
```
or
```r
> x <- c('Xa', 'X_b')
> withr::with_collate("C", sort(x))
[1] "X_b" "Xa" 
> withr::with_collate("en_US.UTF-8", sort(x))
[1] "X_b" "Xa" 
> 
```

So the issue is, why is the sort order changing inside `devtools::check()`? And if this is through collate settings, why are we unable to emulate the same effect?

It seems to have something to do with `shiny`/`shinytest`: if I replace `run_tests` simply by

```r
run_tests <- function() {
  stopifnot(all(order(c("X_b", "Xa")) == c(1, 2)))
}
```
then the example code runs fine.

title: check if `.R` directory exists before calling `lint()` with `cache = TRUE`
description:
Thank you for providing this package and the tools beneath. When using `devtools::lint()` to lint the source code of a local package without changing any defaults I got the following error:

```r
.Error in gzfile(file, "wb") : cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In dir.create(path) :
  cannot create dir '/Users/axel/.R/lintr_cache', reason 'No such file or directory'
2: In gzfile(file, "wb") :
  cannot open compressed file '/Users/axel/.R/lintr_cache/638da06b9726522683c05aa11150f6363bbfce89', probable reason 'No such file or directory'
```

This was confusing to me first as `lintr::lint_package()` succeeds (without changing any defaults).  After checking my user directory and seeing that there is no `.R` directory i figured out that the difference between `devtools::lint()` and `lintr::lint()` is the default value of `cache`, which is `TRUE` in `devtools` and `FALSE` in `lintr`.

Therefore it might be a good idea (if the difference in defaults is intended) to check the existence of the `.R` directory before trying to use it for the cache and provide the user with a more meaningful cli-warning or even create it if it does not exist (creating the directory manually did solve the problem).

Let me know if I should provide any additional info or create a pull request to fix this (for which your advise on the intended behaviour would be needed).

title: `install()` errors when `pkgbuild` is updated (lazy-load database is corrupt, internal error -3 in R_decompress1)
description:
I am aware that issues related to package installation should be filed against `remotes`, but the issue in question appears exclusively with `devtools`, so I am posting here first.

Basically, I am getting the following error when `install()`ing a (local) package having an outdated version of `pkgbuild` installed.

> Error in devtools::install("pkg", force = TRUE) : 
  lazy-load database '/tmp/tmp.Gt6EyQF3cJ/lib/pkgbuild/R/pkgbuild.rdb' is corrupt
In addition: Warning message:
In devtools::install("pkg", force = TRUE) :
  internal error -3 in R_decompress1
Execution halted

To reproduce the problem, set up a clean library and a fake package depending on `pkgbuild`, and install `devtools`. Then, downgrade `pkgbuild` and install the fake package:

```shell
cd `mktemp -d`

mkdir lib
export R_LIBS_USER=lib

mkdir pkg
echo "Package: aaadeleteme" > pkg/DESCRIPTION
echo "Version: 0.0.0.9000" >> pkg/DESCRIPTION
echo "Imports: pkgbuild" >> pkg/DESCRIPTION

R --vanilla -q -s -e 'install.packages("devtools", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")'

# this code errors:
R --vanilla -q -s -e 'devtools::install_version("pkgbuild", "1.2.1", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")'
R --vanilla -q -s -e 'devtools::install("pkg", force = TRUE)'

# this code does not:
R --vanilla -q -s -e 'devtools::install_version("pkgbuild", "1.2.1", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")'
R --vanilla -q -s -e 'devtools::install_local("pkg", force = TRUE)'

# this code does not, either:
R --vanilla -q -s -e 'devtools::install_version("pkgbuild", "1.2.1", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")'
R --vanilla -q -s -e 'remotes::install_local("pkg", force = TRUE)'
```

title: Images in Rd pages not displayed during development (img src mismatch with tmp file path + resources not copied)
description: Thank you for the ever improving goodness of devtools! During development, in the browser the generated file path for a Rd file will be e.g. > file:///private/var/folders/66/wrbb/T/Rtmp/Rtxt.html Paths to images in that Rd file, however, are unchanged (e.g. ``) and the `help` and `figures` folders aren't copied in. So, the image display fails because the folder containing the generated page doesn't contain the `figures` folder and the address is not re-written to match the throw-away url. Not a massive problem, but would be nice if images displayed during development.

title: quit and restart R.app (on MacOS) after each make
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I'm always frustrated when I have to quit and restart R.app (on MacOS) after each make.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
it would be great if devtools had a `restart= T/F` parameter allowing the user to automate build, quit, and execute a delayed call like this (would need tweaking):

```R
system("sleep 2; open -a R.app")
quit()
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
manually watching for make to complete, executing quit, opening R... 10 times a session :-)

**Additional context**
This was not necessary a couple of years ago as builds typically left the package  reloaded correctly. So loving the library/corruption problem would be the ideal solution with this as a workaround..

title: Add a function to install archive packages
description:
Upon upgrading R to 4.0, one of my packages got obsolete (namely {ArgumentCheck}) and has been removed from CRAN repo. However, its archived versions still work efficiently. I then wanted to get a way to install it back. I then used the following function to get it installed:

```
install.archive <- function(url) {
  stopifnot(!missing(url))
  stopifnot(is.character(url) && grepl("^https?://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive", url))
  
  pkgFile <- paste0(tempdir(), gsub("^https?://.*/", "", url))
  download.file(url, pkgFile)
  
  devtools::install_local(pkgFile, dependencies = TRUE, upgrade = "never")
  
  unlink(pkgFile)
}
```

Clearly, this is more a script than a robust solution, but I believe a `install.archive()` function to allow the user to get older version would easily would be helpful. Also, letting a `version` argument could be useful to catch older versions.

title: Problem including a large matrix when using devtools install
description:
I'm trying to use devtools install with a package that I am developing. I do the following after starting R:

library("devtools")                              
library("roxygen2")                               
setwd("./")                                       
install("myPackage")

But I get the error:

*** moving datasets to lazyload DB
Error in lazyLoadDBinsertVariable(vars[i], from, datafile, ascii, compress,  : 
  long vectors not supported yet: connections.c:5984
ERROR: lazydata failed for package ‘myPackage’
* removing ‘/home/phil/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.6/myPackage’
* restoring previous ‘/home/phil/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.6/myPackage’
Error in (function (command = NULL, args = character(), error_on_status = TRUE,  : 
  System command 'R' failed, exit status: 1, stdout & stderr were printed

I think this is caused by a recent addition of a large matrix in the package's data/ directory stored as a  .RData file. If I remove that file, devtools install works fine again. I can load the matrix inside R, although it's big (matrix is 45000x24717).

I found that I can get around this by splitting the matrix into 3 parts to make the vectors/matrices smaller, but I'd still like to know if there is a way that I can use just one file.

I've looked at the devtools install documentation, but I didn't see anything like a parameter that I can set.

When I searched for a solution, I saw some answers for similar problems where cache.lazy = FALSE was recommended for lazyLoadDBinsertVariable.

I tried posting on the Google group for rdevtools but I didn't get a reply.

Thanks very much in advance.

title: Suggestion: check size of tarball/add to list of Qs before release
description:
**Problem:**
Submitted a data package > 5 MB to CRAN

title: get true namespace exports
description:
Because {devtools} hacks the namespace system, `getNamespaceExports()` returns all unexported objects too if `devtools::load_all()` was used.

I'm designing a function to help package development and I'd like to access the list of true exports of the currently developed package.

The following gets me close, except it doesn't include the variables created by `.onLoad()` (and I don't know how to get those)  :  

```
get_namespace_exports <- function(ns) {
  current_pkg <- sub("^Package: (.*)$", "\\1", readLines("DESCRIPTION")[[1]])
  if(is.environment(ns)) ns <- sub("^namespace:", "", environmentName(ns))
  if(ns != current_pkg) return(getNamespaceExports(ns))
  ns_lines <- readLines("NAMESPACE")
  pattern <- "^export\\((.*)\\)$"
  sub(pattern, "\\1", ns_lines)[grepl(pattern, ns_lines)]
}
```

Would it make sense to have such a function in {devtools} ?

title: `devtools::test()` works, but `devtools::check()` does not for `system.file` to locate file with `.yml` extension
description:
I am trying to locate an external file with `.yml` extension for creating unit test with `testthat` while building a R package, the file is placed under `\inst` folder, as mentioned here https://r-pkgs.org/data.html#data-extdata. Am using `system.file()` to load the file with `yaml` package for some unit test (not `base::system.file()`, so that `pkgload:::shim_system.file()` can intercept). The tests passes if I do `devtools::test()`, but it keeps throwing error when I run `devtools::check()`. 

However, interestingly after lots of trials I found out that `devtools::check()` does not throw any error if I save the file with `.txt` extension instead of `.yaml`/`.yml`.

title: `devtools::release()` ignores `release_questions` when package is not loaded
description:
Dear package developers, I recently read on the help page of `devtools::release()` that:

> You can add arbitrary extra questions by defining an (un-exported) function called `release_questions()` that returns a character vector of additional questions to ask.

Hence, I tried to code such a function, but I think that, by default, the extra questions are ignored by `devtools::release()` unless the package itself is loaded (e.g. with `library(something)`). I tried to develop a super small reprex with an R package (no real function but `release_questions`), and it's saved [here](https://github.com/agila5/testpkg). When I run `devtools::release()` inside that project (no package loaded) and answer all questions, I see that the extra question are ignored. Moreover, when I run the function `devtools:::find_release_questions()` inside the project, I get character(0). 

On the other hand, after installing and loading the package, I get the extra question via `devtools::release()` and `devtools:::find_release_questions()`.  Is there a bug in the function? Or do I have to load the package every time before running `devtools::release()` to get the extra questions? If so, is it possible to skip that step? 

Maybe linked to https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/issues/1434

Thanks for your work.

title: devtools::document() fails namespace imports with files which contain no code
description:
Hi! 

I have a problem with `devtools::document()` where it fails to record imports from files which contain no code. I set up a minimal reproducible example over at https://github.com/JSzitas/autodepFailExample. 

In short, as long as any code is present in the file, `devtools::document()` seems to record the imports from the `@importFrom` tags as anticipated (regardless of whether they are used in the code). This would be what I would anticipate would happen. However, if you have a file which contains nothing but `@importFrom` tags (or, I presume, other tags and/or documentation), the imports specified there will not be recorded in the `NAMESPACE` file when running `devtools::document()`.

This led to a bit of confusion for me and I have no idea whether this is intended behavior, so I figured I would ask. 

Thank you for the awesome package!

title: Suggestion: function to build \describe and \items section of oxygen file from a dataset
description:
**Problem**
While it is relatively easy to write an R script to generate a .Rd documentation file for a small dataset with few variables, it is quite painful for a dataset with hundreds of variables, especially when many variables have nonintuitive names, like gene names.

**Possible solution**
A devtools function that would take a dataset as an argument, and build (with glue?) the 
\describe section of the R script to generate and .Rd file
with all of the \items, data type, levels (if factor), range (if numeric), and a spot for a descriptive name (which would have to be hand-edited)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Spending a long time hand-editing these and hunting for typos, missing braces, mismatched variable names, etc.

**Additional context**
It is not essential, but it would be nice and friendly.

title: Suggestion: a function to detect which variables are mismatched when Check fails for a data package because code variables names do not match docs
description:
**Problem**
When variable names in a dataset do not **exactly** match the documentation file, it is relatively easy find the difference in a small dataset with few variables. However, it is quite painful when you have a dataset with hundreds of variables, especially when many variables have similar names, or nonintuitive names, like gene names.

**Suggested solution**
a function that would compare the dataset variables and the documentation variables, and display the mismatches

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
pasting the check output into 2 word documents, one for docs and one for code, and running Compare Documents. This is a hacky workaround, but it works. Just far from elegant. But a lot better than hand-inspecting hundreds of non-adjacent pairs of variable names.

**Additional context**
This is a bit of an edge case. But I do think more folks have large datasets with many variables nowadays.

title: Run test file addin does not find test file on Windows
description:
Here is the issue : 

Running the addin "Run a test file" will run `devtools:::test_active_file()` in R Console in the RStudio IDE. But this error 

```r
> devtools:::test_active_file()
Error: No test files found
Run `rlang::last_error()` to see where the error occurred.
> rlang::last_trace()
<error/rlang_error>
No test files found
Backtrace:
    x
 1. \-devtools:::test_active_file()
 2.   \-devtools:::find_test_file(file)
```

I think this is a Windows specific issue due to the recent switch to **fs** in #2331 mainly due to the fact the **fs** HOME dir on Windows is not the same as the R HOME dir. This means that every unexpanded path started with `~/` will not mean the same for R base function or for **fs**. 

Here is what happens: 

* `devtools:::test_active_file()` => `devtools:::find_active_file()`: This results in a path starting with `~/`. e.g `"~/DEV_R/rmarkdown/tests/testthat/test-render.R"`
* Then `devtools:::find_test_file()` is run on this file and this will error there
https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/blob/f5dc632e7c1e1c6f1743a7288d51cfe3e9a89d18/R/active.R#L8-L25

`fs::file_exists()` is not the same as `file.exists()` on Windows. ([source of change](https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/commit/adbe8382a14161b681f73cb395e60ae1cd5ae155#diff-c7726ac9d315e6cce0ae6befdb86c16cdf6786ef9b6930a616c01d92d7274e69L16-R16))

``` r
file.create(x <- "~/dummy")
#> [1] TRUE
file.exists(x)
#> [1] TRUE
fs::file_exists(x)
#> ~/dummy 
#>   FALSE
unlink(x)
```

<sup>Created on 2021-05-28 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

I think the change to **fs** should take into account this HOME directory difference. It must have for the package internal function that are tested as the tests have passed on Windows. So it may be only an issue for this addin function.

As a workaround, I am changing `R_FS_HOME` for now so that the addin works

title: Building package with vignette deletes local files in inst
description:
Migrated from here: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/9230

**Steps to reproduce:**
* Make an R package project with vignettes (example to use: https://github.com/david-cortes/MatrixExtra).
* Create a sub-folder `inst/doc` and put some files there (e.g. a PDF or alike).
* Run `devtools::build()`

**Expected behavior:** should include the `inst/` files in the package.

**Actual behavior:** ***deletes*** the local files without warning and does not include them in the source build.

**Setup:** devtools 2.3.2.

This is BTW not an issue with R itself since `R CMD build` will not delete local files and will end up including the `inst` folder.

title: devtools (pkgload?) shims cause trouble in .onLoad
description:
My package's `.onLoad()` looks like this:

```
.onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname) {
   
   # load tbb, tbbmalloc
   .tbbDllInfo       <<- loadTbbLibrary("tbb")
   .tbbMallocDllInfo <<- loadTbbLibrary("tbbmalloc")
   
   # load RcppParallel library
   library.dynam("RcppParallel", pkgname, libname)
   
}
```

When I try to call `devtools::document()`, I see:

```
> devtools::document()
ℹ Updating RcppParallel documentation
ℹ Loading RcppParallel
Error in library.dynam("RcppParallel", pkgname, libname) :
  shared object ‘RcppParallel.so’ not found
Calls: <Anonymous> ... <Anonymous> -> run_pkg_hook -> <Anonymous> -> library.dynam
Execution halted
```

And I believe this is because `.onLoad()` receives "shimmed" paths. If I `ls.str()` in my `.onLoad()`:

```
libname :  chr "/Users/kevin/r/pkg"
pkgname :  chr "RcppParallel"
```

I need to manually control the order in which shared libraries are loaded, hence the explicit usages of `dyn.load()` and `library.dynam()`.

What is the correct way out of this hole? How do I avoid the pkgload shims? Does pkgload need its own `library.dynam()` shim?

Separately (and unrelated), if readme.Rmd is located in inst/, should Readme.Rmd be rendered to the package home directory as Readme.md, e.g. by setting `output_dir = path` in the call to `build_rmd` via `...` as default?

title: install_github() needs to tickle gh to cache PAT in env var
description:
I have now removed everything about my GitHub PAT from `.Renviron` and `.Rprofile`, trusting packages like gh and gert to discover the PAT in the Git credential store upon first need. Happily, they both cache the PAT in an env var for the duration of the R session.

The problem is that `devtools::install_github()` sort of assumes the PAT is ambiently available, yet does nothing to trigger its discovery and caching. Which leads to experiences like this:

```
> install_dev_deps()
Skipping 1 packages ahead of CRAN: pkgload
Error: HTTP error 403.
  API rate limit exceeded for 108.172.55.111. (But here's the good news: Authenticated requests get a higher rate limit. Check out the documentation for more details.)

  Rate limit remaining: 0/60
  Rate limit reset at: 2020-11-19 21:42:22 UTC

  To increase your GitHub API rate limit
  - Use `usethis::browse_github_pat()` to create a Personal Access Token.
  - Use `usethis::edit_r_environ()` and add the token as `GITHUB_PAT`.
```

We need to do some combination of these things, here or in ?remotes?:

* Tickle gh to do its thing, perhaps with a `tryCatch()`d and silenced call to `gh::gh_token()`.
* Change the advice above to point people to <https://usethis.r-lib.org/articles/articles/git-credentials.html>

#2253 didn't completely close #2243 because I think devtools or remotes eventually hits GitHub w/o necessarily going through gh (am I right about that?)

cc @hadley

title: test() should support testing frameworks other than testthat
description:
We should keep the existing special case for testthat (since it gives nicer for the interactive case), but we should execute all other files in `tests/` in a new process.

Will also need to set an env var (e.g. `DEVTOOLS_TEST = true`) so that we can opt-out if needed.

title: Avoid rebuilding vignettes in devtools::release()
description:
Some vignettes in some of my packages take very long time to build so I would prefer avoiding to rebuild them when running `devtools::release()` multiple times until CRAN accepts my new package version. Rather, I have prebuilt vignettes saved in `doc` through `devtools::build_vignettes()` that I would like to reuse for the release process. 

In the past I have tried to run `devtools::release(args = "--no-build-vignettes")` but it failed as the vignette index was not built correctly (or at all rather). 

Is it possible to add an argument to `devtools::release()` to reuse existing prebuilt vignettes while still making sure the vignette index (and whatever else might be required for vignettes to function correctly on CRAN) is built correctly?

Many thanks for your efforts on `devtools` and all the related packages! I don't know what I would do without them.

title: `devtools::test()` sources helper files in wrong environment
description:
tl;dr: `devtools::test()` sources helper files in the package environment on the search path, but they should be sourced in the package's namespace.

In a helper file in httpuv (https://github.com/rstudio/httpuv/blob/55c8699d3c811521618e9ce04cacad57c1e89d80/tests/testthat/helper-app.R#L1-L22), we do `library(curl)`, and then call a function from it. The code looks roughly like this:

```R
library(curl)

foo <- function() {
   multi_run()
}
```


When I run `devtools::test()` in new R session, the tests call `foo()`, but it can't find `multi_run()`

```R
> devtools::test()
Loading httpuv
Testing httpuv
✔ |  OK F W S | Context
✖ |   2 3     | basic [0.2 s]                                                                                                      
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Error (test-app.R:30:3): Basic functionality
Error: could not find function "multi_run"
Backtrace:
 1. fetch(local_url("/", s1$getPort())) test-app.R:30:2
 2. curl_fetch_async(url, handle = handle) helper-app.R:83:2
 3. poll() helper-app.R:17:2
```


However, `testthat:test_local()` works:

```R
> testthat::test_local()
✔ |  OK F W S | Context
✔ |  17       | basic [0.4 s]                                                                                                      
✔ |   1       | frame completion                                                                                                   
✔ |   5       | http-parse [0.3 s]                                                                                                 
✔ | 149       | static [2.0 s]                                                                                                     
✔ |   0     8 | traffic                                                                                                            
```

The problem with `devtools::test()` seems to be that the helper is sourced into a sibling of the httpuv package environment (note: this is not the httpuv namespace, but the package env on the search path), and the curl package env is added as a child of the httpuv package env, so it's not visible from the file.

I edited `helper-app.R` so that it prints out parent envs of the current environment and global environment:


```R
library(curl)

cat("Parents of current env ==============================\n")
print(pryr::parenvs())

cat("Parents of global env ==============================\n")
print(pryr::parenvs(globalenv(), all = T))
```

This shows why objects from curl aren't visible from the helper file when using `devtools::test()`:

```
> devtools::test()
Loading httpuv
Parents of current env ==============================
Registered S3 method overwritten by 'pryr':
  method      from
  print.bytes Rcpp
   label                            name               
1  <environment: package:httpuv>    "package:httpuv"   
2  <environment: package:testthat>  "package:testthat" 
3  <environment: package:stats>     "package:stats"    
4  <environment: package:graphics>  "package:graphics"

6  <environment: package:utils>     "package:utils"    
7  <environment: package:datasets>  "package:datasets"

9  <environment: package:methods>   "package:methods"  
10 <environment: 0x7ffd4a2aa400>    "Autoloads"        
11 <environment: base>              ""                 
12 <environment: R_EmptyEnv>        ""                 
Parents of global env ==============================
   label                            name               
1  <environment: R_GlobalEnv>       ""                 
2  <environment: package:promises>  "package:promises" 
3  <environment: package:curl>      "package:curl"     
4  <environment: package:httpuv>    "package:httpuv"
```

title: Don’t add unwanted/overly broad .gitignore entries
description:
`build_vignettes` helpfully adds the entries `doc` and `Meta` to `.gitignore`, if they don’t already exist.

However, more specific, existing entries are ignored. In particular, if the `.gitignore` file contains `/doc/` and `/Mate/`, the (redundant) entries are *still* added.

Unfortunately, my project is actually using a nested `doc` directory, so that project *doesn’t* want to ignore this name.

I’m happy to contribute a patch but I’m not sure how to do this well: ideally the `build_vignettes` should probably be [maximally specific](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore), and attempt to add `/doc/` and `/Meta/` instead of `doc` and `Meta` to avoid falsely matching unrelated directories. But such a change wouldn’t be backwards compatible (i.e. existing ‘devtools’ projects would now get redundant entries added to `.gitignore`) so it doesn’t seem viable. Instead, maybe an option to skip automatic additions to `.gitignore`, for users who rely on such directory names, might be conceivable.

title: library path for `install_github`
description:
I know this has been raised in the past and I have looked at issue #519.
Somebody even asked for a better argument for specifying the library path in the `install_github` function.

Here is a better argument:

In HPC (High-Performance Computing) Clusters, a normal user doesn't have admin privilege to install R packages in /usr/ locations. All a normal user can do is to install in their personal folders assigned to them as per institutions policy and quota.

A lot of researchers in universities and academic institutions rely on HPC to perform computation-intensive jobs and features like this have a lot of advantages.

Currently, I can do the following with `install.packages`:

```
install.packages("RSpectra", lib="/home/username/Rlib")

```

It will really be helpful to imitate a similar function signature, something like:
```
install_github("r-lib/devtools", lib = "/home/username/Rlib")
```

description:

title: object 'is_R_CMD_check' not found
description:
Hi,

I wanted to share an issue that I came across while updating my R-package.
I uploaded my package two months ago to GitHub and today, I wanted to check whether `devtools::check()` ran without problems.
However, I ran into the following issues:

1. When running `devtools::check()` the following error occured: 

```r
creating vignettes (14.9s) 
--- re-building ‘raincloudplots.Rmd’ using rmarkdown
object 'is_R_CMD_check' not found`
Error: Vignette re-building failed.
```

After reading up on some websites, I was able to resolve this error by changing the following in the Vignette YAML: 

```r
%\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
```
into

```r
%\VignetteEngine{rmarkdown::render}
```
Thereafter, the `devtools::check()` ran until the end with the following warning:

```r
checking files in ‘vignettes’ ... WARNING
  Files in the 'vignettes' directory but no files in 'inst/doc':
    ‘raincloudplots.Rmd’
```
My questions:

Why would I now have to change the YAML data, while `devtools::check()` ran perfectly two months ago?
Any suggestions on how to resolve the `inst/doc` warning? 

Both error and warning did not occur previously on the `devtools::check()` when I uploaded the package two months ago.

Many thanks.

title: more meaningful error message for install_github() when branch master doesn't exist
description:
github is planning on "master" no longer being the default branch.

If you try to install_github() from a repo that doesn't have a master branch, you get this error message:

```
Downloading GitHub repo <user>/<repo>@master
Error in utils::download.file(url, path, method = method, quiet = quiet,  : 
  cannot open URL 'https://api.github.com/repos/<user>/<repo>/tarball/master'
```
While the message does contain `@master` which hints at the issue, it still could be more clear. Maybe add something like, "Perhaps this repo uses a different name for the main branch?"

title: check() "no visible binding for global variable" errantly flags subset's subset arguments
description:
With apologies for the confusing titlename!

I think this might be a bug but I'm quite new to `check()`. I got a number of "no visible binding for global variable" notes, which I think were due to the syntax of `subset()`having its 'subset' argument look like a global variable. E.g.:

```
mydataframe$newColumn <- runif(100, 0, 1)
subset(mydataframe, newColumn > 0.5)
```

Would flag `newColumn` for this issue even though it's not a global variable. I presume this is due to the syntax checking algorithm `check()` uses but I'm massively guessing here.

Cheers!

title: load_all() glitch with unexported S3 methods
description:
I'm wondering if I've messed up my installation somehow, as this seems to be a fairly fundamental issue.

I'm using R 4.0.2 on Windows, with devtools 2.3.0. When I run `load_all()` on a package under development, R doesn't find S3 methods that aren't exported (ie, aren't present in the NAMESPACE file).

Reproducible example:

- Create  a new directory, and in that directory, run `devtools::create(".")`
- Create a file `R/file1.R` containing:

```r
func <- function(x, ...)
{
    UseMethod("func")
}

func.cls <- function(x, ...)
{
    x
}

#' @export
make_cls <- function(x)
{
    structure(list(x=x), class="cls")
}
```

- Run `devtools::document()` and `devtools::load_all()`
- Run the following:

```r
obj <- make_cls(42)
func(obj)
```
```
Error in UseMethod("func") : 
  no applicable method for 'func' applied to an object of class "cls"
```

The error goes away if I add `@export` directives to the `func` and `func.cls` functions, redocument and reload. This behaviour wasn't present under R 3.6.x.

description:
Seemingly a duplicate of this issue that I cannot comment on: https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/issues/1956.

Exactly the same behaviour is exhibited. I get the same error message when I try to use `devtools::release()` after the third step.

```r
Error in getOption("repos")[["CRAN"]] : subscript out of bounds
```

But if, as per the locked issue, I set 

```r
options(repos = list(CRAN = "http://cran.us.r-project.org"))
```

it works as expected. I tried installing the version from GitHub as well and it exhibits the same unexpected behaviour.

title: devtools::build() fails to include PDF of help pages when needed
description:
The `rgl` package (https:://github.com/rforge/rgl/pkg/rgl) uses some `\Sexpr` expressions in its help files.  CRAN says this means the tarball should contain the PDF file for the help pages, and `R CMD build rgl` includes it.  However, if I ask to build the source package in RStudio, I get a tarball without the help PDF, and CRAN rejects my submission. 

RStudio is calling `devtools::build()`, and after saving files, it calls `pkgbuild::build` with lots of arguments set, including `manual = FALSE`, coming from a default in `devtools::build()`.  This causes `pkgbuild::build` to use the option `--no-manual` when it calls `R CMD build`.

If I run `R CMD build` on a package that doesn't need the PDF file, I don't get one, so I think the default should leave off any specification of the option.

title: option `porcelain` takes no value
description:
Hi! I rely on this package for CRAN submissions and greatly appreciate it.

I had a new error arise that i don't think is due to a problem with my Git installation. It occurred during a `release()` of a new package, but i can reproduce it with a freshly initiated Git directory—though `reprex()` does not print the message. Here's the reprex:

``` r
library(devtools)
#> Warning: package 'devtools' was built under R version 4.0.2
#> Loading required package: usethis
#> Warning: package 'usethis' was built under R version 4.0.2
setwd(tempdir())
system2("git", "init")
print(devtools:::git_uncommitted())
#> Warning in system2("git", c("status", "--porcelain=v1"), stdout = TRUE): running
#> command ''git' status --porcelain=v1' had status 129
#> [1] FALSE
system2("rm", c("-r", ".git"))
```

<sup>Created on 2020-10-09 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

And here's what i see by executing these lines in the Terminal:

description:

title: R crashes after calling load_all()
description:
I'm writing a package containing `OpenMP` code. When I disable the OpenMP flag when compiling the code, everything works fine, but once I enable the flag, calling `load_all()` lead to segfaults.

To reproduce the error, follow the following steps:

1. Open/Download OpenMP enabled package. For example create R project from github, https://github.com/fstpackage/fstcore
2. Compile the package
3. Run some functions that uses OpenMP. For example
```r
.Call(fstcore:::`_fstcore_fststore`, tempfile(), data.frame(V1=1), 100L, TRUE)
```
4. Add a blank line in src/*.cpp (any file)
5. Run `devtools::load_all(recompile = TRUE)`

These five steps not only crash RStudio, but also R if ran in terminal.

I tried multiple packages that use OpenMP. None of them survives these steps.

title: Reconsider removing `inst()`
description:
The [search](https://github.com/search?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=user%3Acran+%22devtools%3A%3Ainst%22&type=Code) from the original issue #1643 shows four packages using `devtools::inst()` as of now:

 * NlsyLinks, last updated 4 years ago
 * Wats, last updated 5 years ago
 * teachingApps, last updated 2 years ago; [no longer using `devtools::inst()`](https://github.com/cran/teachingApps/blob/master/R/inst.R)
 * IalsaSynthesis, last updated 5 years ago

Since the three remaining packages with an actual dependency only have the dependency in their tests and none of them seem to be actively maintained, I would suggest to remove `devtools::inst()` from the package once again.

The upside of this would be that the auto-complete prefix for `devtools::install()` shortens to "i" instead of "insta", saving a lot of keystrokes for this very frequent function call.
Also, it's less confusing than to have two functions with very similar name but completely different functionality.

title: build only one vignette using dev package version
description:
TL;DR: it would be great to be able to use `build_vignettes` logic for only knitting one vignette.

This is from experiences during tidydevday in SF. Some people were working on documentations in Rmd for vignettes. However, in the Rmd file they have a library call like `library(dplyr)`. When knitting,  it then uses by default the library installed in their library path and not the current dev version they are working on. 

Currently, I see two workflows: 
* Installing the dev version locally then work on the vignette and knit to render
* use `devtools::build_vignettes(..., install = TRUE)` (which is the default) to build the vignettes by building first the current dev package in a temp libpath. 

I find the second one safer, but it builds all the vignettes with `tools::buildVignettes` and not offering to render one Rmd only. 

Maybe there could be an option or a new function to only render one Rmd file when working on a vignette and applying the logic of [`devtools::build_vignettes(..., install = TRUE)`](https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/blob/726c5305b34e7cd76a30064162b3871825733b0e/R/vignettes.R#L47-L65): 
* install the current dev version of the package in a temp library path
* render the vignette using this temp lib path 
* do that in another background using callr session for safety 

Their could also be something to do in the IDE so that knitting can be done with the dev version when in a vignette. Or maybe in `rmarkdown::html_vignette` format so that `rmarkdown::render` can help with that. 

I think this could definitely helped when working on vignettes.

title: suggestion: error message recommending `remotes::install_*` when `devtools::install_*` fails?
description:
hi, thanks for the excellent software.

the problem described below doesn't occur with `remotes::install_github` since it has fewer dependencies, one of the benefits of the https://github.com/r-lib/devtools#conscious-uncoupling

`devtools::install_*` has been the standard way to load packages from repos like github, i'm probably not the only user who didn't realize they should switch to `remotes::install_*`

in the event of an install_* error, does it make sense for the error message to encourage users to switch to `remotes::install_*` which doesn't have the same dependency conflicts?

thanks very much for your time  :-)



	install.packages('devtools')


	# # close console and re-open


	# old version of some package on local machine
	packageurl <- "http://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/rlang/rlang_0.4.0.tar.gz"
	install.packages(packageurl, repos=NULL, type="source")


	# # close console and re-open


	# fails because running a devtools function loads the rlang library
	devtools::install_github("tidyverse/ggplot2",dependencies = TRUE)

	# Error: .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'pkgload', details:
	  # call: loadNamespace(i, c(lib.loc, .libPaths()), versionCheck = vI[[i]])
	  # error: namespace ‘rlang’ 0.4.0 is already loaded, but >= 0.4.1 is required


	# # close console and re-open


	# fails because `rlang` is required by devtools, but it doesn't have the same >= 0.4.1 as ggplot2
	# this step updates dependencies ggplot2 shares with devtools
	install.packages( "devtools" , dependencies = TRUE )
	devtools::install_github("tidyverse/ggplot2" , dependencies = TRUE )


	# # close console and re-open


	# update the problem packages by hand
	install.packages( c( "rlang" , "processx" ) , dependencies = TRUE )
	devtools::install_github("tidyverse/ggplot2" , dependencies = TRUE )
	# works

title: devtools::test_file not working when file name starts with test_
description:
The convention is that the file name starts with `test-`, not `test_`. In the latter case, `test_file` does not work currently.

https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/blob/b166195be72927a003e6937de5c3239881095a9f/R/test.R#L180

In this line, you remove the `test` prefix. On the other hand, in `testthat:::filter_test_scripts`, you remove "test-?" (see https://github.com/r-lib/testthat/blob/de3cff6bb59a957cf4078e127a9ea9a616ca7fea/R/test-files.R#L57).

So a fix would be to replace the quoted line 180  above: `"test" -> "test-?"`

```
3: None                                  
4: ape       (5.3    -> 5.4       ) [CRAN]
5: phangorn  (2.5.5  -> 2.6.0.0   ) [CRAN]
6: TreeTools (1.0.0  -> 1.0.0.9000) [CRAN]
7: bit       (1.1-14 -> 1.1-15.2  ) [CRAN]
```

But the latest version of 'phangorn' and 'TreeTools' on CRAN was 2.5.5 and 1.0.0, which the user already had installed; the proposed updates (v2.6.0.0 & v1.0.0.9000) were hosted on my custom repository.

I would interpret this to suggest that the 'phangorn' and 'TreeTools' updates would be downloaded from CRAN.  This feels like a potential security risk: the user is not given the choice to decide whether or not they trust my personal repo.  Is it possible for the tag to reflect the true source of the linked files?

description:
I knew about this for a while but was surprised to learn that it is apparently not on purpose. As mentioned [here](https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/issues/542#issuecomment-446317144),  `devtools::check()` does not seem to automatically set `Sys.setenv(NOT_CRAN = "true")` while  `Build -> Check Package` in RStudio does.

I created a [minimal test package](https://github.com/JBGruber/test) with a test that is supposed to fail locally but not on CRAN:

```
test_that("multiplication works", {
  skip_on_cran()
  expect_equal(2 * 3, 4)
})
```
However when I run this via `devtools::check()`, it runs without error, presumably because `NOT_CRAN` isn't set. If I use `Sys.setenv(NOT_CRAN = "true")` before `devtools::check()`, everything works as intended.

title: devtools:test() works, but devtools:check() fail on functions with if(class(x) == "type") conditional.
description:
Hi. I and @grlloyd have stumbled across strange behaviour of the `devtools` package using `R-devel (4.0.0)` and the latest `devtools` package.

I am using R command `class` to determine what data structure object belong to. Based on the object type, function is supposed to do different tasks. Small example is shown below or can be accessed from Github repository [devtoolsCheck](https://github.com/andzajan/devtoolsCheck):

```
#' This is example function to demonstrate that devtools:check() can fail.
#'
#' @param object R object
#' @return The class of the object
#' @examples
#' mat <- matrix(1:20, nrow=5, ncol=5)
#' object_class (mat)
#' @export

object_class <- function (object){
    obj_class <- class(object)
    if (obj_class == "matrix"){
        cat ("Object type is matrix!", "\n")
    } else {
        cat ("Object type isn't matrix!", "\n")
    }
}
```
And corresponding `testthat` test looks like this:
```
  
test_that("Object class is returned", {
    mat <- matrix(1:20, nrow=5, ncol=5)
    expect_output(object_class(mat))
})
```

This works fine with `devtools:test()` and `rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck()`, but fails with `devtools:check()` command. Giving error:
```
 --- value of length: 2 type: logical ---
[1]  TRUE FALSE
```
Full Travis report using `r-devel` version:  
[devtools:check() fails](https://travis-ci.org/andzajan/devtoolsCheck/builds/626808086?utm_source=github_status&utm_medium=notification).

The fix is to specifically only to take the first element of `class` command output, `devtools:check()` and Travis will pass. [Travis report with fix](https://travis-ci.org/andzajan/devtoolsCheck/builds/626813214?utm_source=github_status&utm_medium=notification)
```
obj_class <- class(object)[1]
```

But output from a `class` command for `matrix` object is length of 1, why does `devtools:check()` fail?
```
> mat <- matrix(0, ncol=5, nrow =5)
> class(mat)
[1] "matrix"
> length(class(mat))
[1] 1
> 
```

title: Inconsistent documentation of install()
description:
The `install()` option `local` was renamed to `build` in c2850710. Its default value remained `TRUE` although it means the opposite. (It has been defaulted to `build = !quick`, i.e.`TRUE`, since cc368444.)

This situation conflicts with the detail description of `install()`:

> By default, installation takes place using the current package directory.
> If you have compiled code, this means that artefacts of compilation will be
> created in the `src/` directory. If you want to avoid this, you can
> use `build = TRUE` to first build a package bundle and then install
> it from a temporary directory. This is slower, but keeps the source
> directory pristine.

title: Give more detailed explanation of `args` argument to `devtools::check`
description:
I find that `devtools::check(args = c("--no-examples", "--no-tests"))` works fine but devtools::check(args = "--no-examples --no-tests") does not work; instead it warns `Warning: unknown option ‘--no-tests --no-examples’` and carries on and performs the tests and examples. This is surprising behaviour, particularly for someone who is used to running `R CMD CHECK` from the command line. It would be good to make clear in the docs that the spaced approach will not work with `devtools::check()`.

I recently had a PR for this very reason accepted to the `rcmdcheck` package (https://github.com/r-lib/rcmdcheck/pull/125). Are you interested in such a PR for `devtools`? If so how would you like me to do it? Could just `@inheritParams rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck`?

title: If rlang have newer source version for windows, install_github could fail because of locking
description:
I have rlang 0.4.5 binary installed
```r
> install.packages("rlang")
Installing package into ‘D:/Lib/R_user_lib’
(as ‘lib’ is unspecified)

  There is a binary version available but the source version is later:
      binary source needs_compilation
rlang  0.4.5  0.4.6              TRUE

trying URL 'https://cran.rstudio.com/bin/windows/contrib/4.0/rlang_0.4.5.zip'
Content type 'application/zip' length 1112530 bytes (1.1 MB)
downloaded 1.1 MB

package ‘rlang’ successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked
```
while installing a package with `install_github`, I chose to only update CRAN packages, 

```r
> devtools::install_github("ctmm-initiative/ctmmweb")
Downloading GitHub repo ctmm-initiative/ctmmweb@master
These packages have more recent versions available.
It is recommended to update all of them.
Which would you like to update?

1: All                          
2: CRAN packages only           
3: None                         
4: rlang (0.4.5 -> 0.4.6) [CRAN]

Enter one or more numbers, or an empty line to skip updates:
2
rlang        (0.4.5 -> 0.4.6   ) [CRAN]
```
then it will ask me 
>   There is a binary version available (and will be installed) but the source version is later:
      binary source
rlang  0.4.5  0.4.6

I chose Not to install from source, then it will download 0.4.5 and try to install it again, even I already have 0.4.5 installed. In the end the package installation will fail.

```r

trying URL 'https://cran.rstudio.com/bin/windows/contrib/4.0/rlang_0.4.5.zip'
Content type 'application/zip' length 1112530 bytes (1.1 MB)
downloaded 1.1 MB
...
package ‘rlang’ successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked
Error: Failed to install 'ctmmweb' from GitHub:
  (converted from warning) cannot remove prior installation of package ‘rlang’

```

I cannot pass this failure loop unless I chose to install rlang 0.4.6 from source.

I think the problem is, once the process scheduled to install 0.4.6, even user chose not to install from source, it will try to install binary version even there is a same version binary package installed already. Then somehow this will cause problem.

Either don't try to install the same version binary, or fix the problem of installing same version binary again will fix this.

title: [feature request] Create notes/changelog.md from git commits
description:
I am not sure if this is the right place to post this or even if this is possible in R but I figure I would give it a shot and this seems like the best place to request this.

The concept is simple, Git commit messages can be formatted so that all the relevant information needed to generate changelogs is there. I am requesting a feature that would allow for automatically generating a changelog based off these preformatted git commit messages. An example implementation can be found here

https://medium.com/jobtome-engineering/how-to-generate-changelog-using-conventional-commits-10be40f5826c.

These changelogs can possibly be extended with either rmarkdown or roxygen2 comment tags in another file to make into a useful notes file since notes files are preferred in R packages as opposed to simple changelogs.

Thank you for your consideration.

title: DT should not be an imported package
description:
Because DT is an imported package, when you load devtools, it also loads htmltools, which makes it hard to do development on  htmltools, especially on on Windows.

There are also some packages that are listed as Imports in crosstalk's DESCRIPTION but don't load immediately because they're not imported in the NAMESPACE. Even though they're not loaded immediately, these packages do need to be installed when DT (and thus crosstalk) is installed. Two of these packages have a pretty heavy installation footprint: shiny and ggplot2.

So there really two annoying issues: one is that loading devtools causes DT and htmltools to load. That one can be solved by removing `importFrom(DT,datatable)` from NAMESPACE. The other one is the heavy installation footprint. To solve that, DT would have to be removed from the Imports in the DESCRIPTION file. I see in #2085 that it was moved there specifically to cause it to be automatically installed. Maybe it could be changed to a Suggested package again and prompt for installation when it's needed?

title: Refinement of devtools::build error message for invalid pkg path
description:
When specifying an invalid path to the `pkg` option of `devtools::build()`, the following error message is returned (via the call to `pkgbuild::build`): 

> Error: `path` must exist.

This causes some user-confusion because there is a separate, unrelated `path` option for `devtools::build` that is passed to the `dest_path` option of `pkgbuild::build`. Without looking at the traceback, the user would likely assume that their `path` option to `devtools::build` was incorrect, rather than the `pkg` option. 

Two potential solutions are:

- Check the validity of the `pkg` path in `devtools::build` prior to calling `pkgbuild::build` using a similar set of code to [this snippet](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgbuild/blob/master/R/build.R#L69-L71) (swapping in `pkg` instead of `path`)
- Update [the error snippet](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgbuild/blob/master/R/build.R#L69-L71) in `pkgbuild::build` to something like "Error: pkg `path` must exist".

From my perspective, the first option seems preferable, but I'm not sure whether that would fit philosophically with your approach of offloading much of the codebase to functions within the pkgbuild package.

title: add package commit date to DESCRIPTION file when building/installing package
description:
It's often helpful to provide detailed package version information to user for bug report. Manually assigned version number may not be updated frequently like commit date, thus it can be useful to add the commit date time to package DESCRIPTION file.

Right now devtools will add a "Built date", but that is just the time it installing the package from source. There is remote SHA if installed from github which is helpful but not directly usable as a commit date.

Thus when devtools install a package from github or from local source, it will be helpful to add the commit date to DESCRIPTION file.

title: bug in `check()` or `R CMD CHECK`?
description:
`R CMD CHECK` gives a NOTE on my R package:
> checking R code for possible problems ... NOTE  
  Found the following calls to attach():  
  File ‘wfr/R/rmd.util.r’:  
    attach(rImageFn, name = "rImage", pos = 2)  
  See section ‘Good practice’ in ‘?attach’.

Here is the corresponding "Good Practice" section in [`attach`](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/base/versions/3.6.1/topics/attach):
> Good Practice  
`attach` has the side effect of altering the search path and this can easily lead to the wrong object of a particular name being found. People do often forget to `detach` databases.

The NOTE is due to the following three consecutive lines of code in a function in my R package:
```r
        attach(rImageFn,name="rImage", pos=2)
        obj1=get("OBJ2",pos = 2)
        detach(name="rImage", pos=2)
```
Seems the concern from the NOTE is that **People do often forget to detach databases**, which is not the case here. So I wonder if `R CMD CHECK` should issue the NOTE **only if** `attach` is not followed by `detach`?

Meanwhile, any suggestion on how to prevent this NOTE?

title: Alphabetical ordering inconsistent between test() and check() using testthat::expect_known_output()
description:
Hi All

I have written some tests using the testthat framework. I'm working in Rstudio, currently devtools 2.2.0 is installed. When running them with devtools::test() or ctrl + shit + T they pass, running them with devtools::check() or ctrl + shift + E they fail, citing a changed alphabetical order of expected outputs. The failure occurs with "." and "_" being sorted differently, though I have not tried other combinations of symbols/characters.

I have reproduced the issue in the attached minimal package. In essence the code writes a number of variables to an environment and at some point prints all names in that environment. I'm using testthat::expect_known_output() match this printed list with a previous, verified printout stored in "tests/testthat/ref.txt" (produced by running devtools::test() once before).  

I realize that this issue may be caused by a lot of different things along the execution paths up to and including the language settings of the host . But as the devtools are my current entry point I'm posting it here first.

I'm running R3.6.1 on Ubuntu 18.04.3 LTS 64bit.


The files/functions as reference point:
print_env.R:
``` R
print_env <- function() {
  test_env <- new.env()
  assign("a_c", NA, envir = test_env)
  assign("a_b", NA, envir = test_env)
  assign("a.c", NA, envir = test_env)
  env_names <- ls(test_env)
  cat(env_names, sep = "\n")
}
```

tests/testthat/test-print_env.R:
``` R
test_that("print_env_comparison" , {
  expect_known_output(print_env(),
                      file = "ref.txt",
                      update = TRUE)
})
```

Running these commands either from the console or hotkeys:

``` R
devtools::test()
# Loading orderingTest
# Testing orderingTest
# ✔ |  OK F W S | Context
# ✔ |   1       | print_env
#
# ══ Results 
# 
# OK:       1
# Failed:   0
# Warnings: 0
# Skipped:  0
```

``` R 
devtools::check()
# (omited output)
# > test_check("orderingTest")
# ── 1. Failure: print_env_comparison (@test-print_env.R#3)  
# Results have changed from known value recorded in 'ref.txt'.
# 3/3 mismatches
# x[1]: "a.c"
# y[1]: "a_b"
# 
# x[2]: "a_b"
# y[2]: "a_c"
# 
# x[3]: "a_c"
# y[3]: "a.c"
```

Obviously I'd expect the test to produce the same result independently on how it is called. 
Attached is the minimal package, including the reference output file for the testcase.

Thank you and cheers.

[orderingTest.zip](https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/files/3641479/orderingTest.zip)

title: Spell check does not for for two or more languages
description:
I have a package in which the documentation in written in English (functions) and a second language (vignettes). These languages are set in the `Language` field of the `DESCRIPTION` file. This is done following the 'Writing R Extensions' manual:

> A `‘Language’` field can be used to indicate if the package documentation is not in English: this should be a comma-separated list of standard (not private use or grandfathered) IETF language tags as currently defined by RFC 5646 (https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5646, see also https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag), i.e., use language subtags which in essence are 2-letter ISO 639-1 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_639-1) or 3-letter ISO 639-3 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_639-3) language codes.

When running `devtools::spell_check()`, the following error message is issued:

```
Error: Dictionary file not found: pt_BR, EN_US.dic
``` 

I haven't found a way around this.

Obviously, this is very uninformative, especially if the order is different. Instead (or in addition) devtools should provide the specific list of columns that are absent/extra in the documentation. Assuming that devtools just obtains a character vector for both the variables in the dataset, and the variables in the documentation, two calls to %in% would be sufficient to do so.

title: Incomplete package loading for collate files containing UTF-8 characters and missing Encoding in DESCRIPTION
description:
When using `devtools::load_all` and in case of some UTF-8 characters within the collate files but missing `Encoding: UTF-8` in the DESCRIPTION, devtools loads parts of the files (until UTF-8 characters) and does not stop. There is just an indirect warning:

> Warning in readLines(con, warn = FALSE, n = n, ok = ok, skipNul = skipNul) :
>   invalid input found on input connection 'test.R'

Most likely, `Encoding ASCII` is assumed and `pkgload:::read_lines_enc` reads incomplete files. In case the UTF-8 character is found within a roxygen function documentation (or comment), no incomplete code is evaluated and no error is thrown.

The following code from `pkgload:::read_lines_enc` reads files until the first UTF-8 character:
```
file_encoding <- "ASCII"
con <- file("test.R", encoding = file_encoding)
lines <- readLines(con, warn = FALSE, n = -1L, ok = TRUE, skipNul = FALSE)
Encoding(lines) <- "UTF-8"
```
The following replacement reads all lines and seems to be more robust: 
```
lines <- readLines("test.R", warn = FALSE, n = -1L, ok = TRUE, skipNul = FALSE)
Encoding(lines) <- "UTF-8"
```

title: Recommendations re: who and how to use devtools vs. constituent packages
description:
Discussion in group meeting made it clear we don't have a clear consensus and policy re: devtools vs. the constituent packages. The problem is that we haven't fully discussed, recorded, and publicized what we want -- not that there's any real disagreement.

Draft of some principles:

  * devtools is the main "storefront" for this package development toolkit. Most especially for interactive use.
    - In `.Rprofile`, if someone makes this toolkit available to themselves in interactive sessions, it should probably be via `require(devtools)`.
    - In a README, we'd prefer to see `devtools::install_github("OWNER/REPO")` over `remotes::install_github("OWNER/REPO")`.
  * Programmatic use should NOT be of devtools, but of the package where the target function actually lives.
    - "Imports: usethis" + `usethis::use_WHATEVER()` is good and "Imports: devtools" + `devtools::use_WHATEVER()` is bad, even if both "work". The number of packages that depend on devtools should hold steady or, hopefully, decline as a result of breaking devtools into smaller packages.
    - In a CI script, we'd expect to see `remotes::install_github("OWNER/REPO")`, not `devtools::install_github("OWNER/REPO")` (~although, because of devtools' use on both travis and appveyor, you can probably count on its presence~ and we have better ways to install a dev version but whatever).

It would be nice to have a graphical depiction of what devtools is, with respect to the whole set of packages.

```R
mypkgfun()

devtools::install()

# Updating mypkg documentation

# Loading mypkg
# Writing NAMESPACE
mypkgfun()

```

workaround = manual reload
```R
library(mypkg)
mypkgfun()
# "hi"
```

title: install_github() and friends should use ellipsis::check_dots_used()
description:
From @jennybc:

`devtools::install_github()` used to have a `build_vignettes` argument. But its current incarnation, now `remotes::install_github()`, does **not** have this argument. To build vignettes, we're supposed to do this:

```
devtools::install_github("foo/bar", build_opts = c("--no-resave-data", "--no-manual"))
```

as per https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/issues/1896#issuecomment-431834044.

However lots of people still try to do `install_github("foo/bar", build_vignettes = TRUE)` and, no doubt, some of our own material probably shows this, i.e. hasn't been updated yet.

And because the signature of `install_github()` contains `...`, their attempts just silently fail:

```
install_github(repo, ref = "master", subdir = NULL,
  auth_token = github_pat(), host = "api.github.com",
  dependencies = NA, upgrade = c("default", "ask", "always", "never"),
  force = FALSE, quiet = FALSE, build = TRUE,
  build_opts = c("--no-resave-data", "--no-manual",
  "--no-build-vignettes"), repos = getOption("repos"),
  type = getOption("pkgType"), ...)
```

---

`install_github()` needs to give a clear message if you've misspecified the argument names.

(I think this needs to wait until after I've added an option to `check_dots_used()` to throw a warning instead of an error; since `install_github()` is called primarily for its side-effects, I think throwing an error is confusing, since it would occur after the side-effects have taken place)

description:
without `BiocManager` installed for a package with a big dependency network, it can be a second or more before the error occurs:

```
devtools::revdep('data.table', bioconductor = TRUE)
```

> Error in loadNamespace(name) : there is no package called ‘BiocManager’

Any reason not to run the test at the top of the function to save this time?

Happy to file a PR

----

PS as an aside, since the modularization of `devtools`, is it better to file this issue under `devtools` or the upstream package (`tools` in this case IINM)?

title: devtools::document error with shared object
description:
Dear,

I have been using devtools::document() to update .Rd files and NAMESPACE in my package. This package need load a dynamic shared object (specifically a Fortran .f90 file) and have been working accordingly.

To do this I include the .onLoad function and use library.dynam function to inform the dynamic shared object.

.onLoad <- function(lib, pkg) {
	library.dynam("xx_package", pkg, lib)
}

and to inform NAMESPACE via @rawNamespace tag:

@rawNamespace useDynLib(xx_package)

This correct include “useDynLib(xx_package)” in NAMESPACE file. The package can be installed and load.

However, every time that I need update .Rd or NAMESPACE files the function devtools::document() fails.

The following error:

devtools::document()
Updating xx_package documentation
Loading xx_package
Error in library.dynam("xx_package", pkg, lib) : 
  shared object ‘xx_package.so’ not found

To solve this, I need to follow the following steps:
1 - Comment (with #) library.dynam line in .onLoad function
2 - Run devtools::document()
3 - Uncomment library.dynam line in .onLoad function

As I already informed via @rawNamespace tag the existence of dynamic shared object all work accordingly. Could I find a simpler solution to solve this error?


Best, Vanderlei

title: Improvement demand on devtools::check
description:
**CRAN** does not accept packages submitted when version in **DESCRIPTION** file has leading zeros _(e.g. 1.01.004)_. This ends up to be rejected by **CRAN,** and the fix is just to turn 1.01.004 to 1.1.4. 

I wish **devtools::check** to implement such a simple test as it will make all of us avoid this trap and avoid many erroneous submissions on **CRAN**, not currently detected by devtools.

title: Installation instructions for Mac / Mojave
description:
It took me sometime to figure out how to install devtools on my Mojave Mac and I wish there were an instruction section in the README.md.

1. Install Xcode patch by typing following in command line:
```open /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/Packages/macOS_SDK_headers_for_macOS_10.14.pkg```
This is necessary as [Mojave has a different header folder location](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/52702738/stdio-h-not-found-during-r-package-installation)

2. [Install `Omp` library](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25990296/how-to-include-omp-h-in-os-x) required for `px` package dependency:
```brew install libomp```

3. Install `devtools` per se: `install.packages('devtools')`

Done

title: Error in devtools: Incorrect number of arguments (16), expecting 14 for 'processx_exec'
description:
This issue is already, solved. However, see the description as it might be helpful to others.

I've been working on an R package (`"mypackage"`) using `devtools` without any problems for months. Then, one day I attempted to use `devtools::install()` and the error below first appeared:

```r
devtools::install("mypackage")
> Error in rethrow_call(c_processx_exec, command, c(command, args), stdin,  : 
> Incorrect number of arguments (16), expecting 14 for 'processx_exec'
```

After some iterative attempts, I realized that the very same error appeared when I run `devtools::find_rtools()`:

```r
devtools::find_rtools()
> Error in rethrow_call(c_processx_exec, command, c(command, args), stdin,  : 
> Incorrect number of arguments (16), expecting 14 for 'processx_exec'
```

So, I re-installed Rtools 3.5, switched to Rtools version 3.3, re-installed devtools 2.1.0, switched to devtools version 2.0.1, reset my computer a few times, run `find_rtools` with Rtools uninstalled, but the error persisted.

In addition, I got a similar error when I tried to install devtools from GitHub

```r
devtools::install_github("r-lib/devtools")
> Error: Failed to install 'devtools' from GitHub:
>  Incorrect number of arguments (16), expecting 14 for 'processx_exec'
```

Apparently, the problem was `processx` package and the error disappeared when I reinstalled it. 

I don't know what caused the error, but [this forum](https://github.com/tidyverse/reprex/issues/136) helped me solve it.

title: introducing function to check web only vignettes
description:
I have a data visualization package and, as much as I wish to write detailed vignettes with a lot of plots, I constantly run into the issue of package size being bigger than 5MB, which is something `CRAN` doesn't really like.

Of late, one solution I have found is to write vignettes in a subdirectory and host them on the `pkgdown` website articles (e.g., https://github.com/IndrajeetPatil/ggstatsplot/tree/master/vignettes/web_only). But the risk is that the code in this subdirectory is not checked by `devtools` and so some mistakes can slip through.

Is there any possibility to have a function that can also check these vignettes in such a subdirectory?

title: checking `dontrun{}` and recommending `donttest{}`?
description: `CRAN` team now expects `dontrun{}` to be replaced by `donttest{}`. I am not sure if this is actually possible for `devtools` to do given that it's just a wrapper around `R CMD CHECK` but I was wondering if `devtools` can maybe catch all instances of `dontrun{}` and inform the developer that these should be replaced by `donttest{}`.

title: documenting re-exported functions in the manual
description:
This is more of a general question about how to document re-exported function couched in `devtools` settings.

For example, `devtools` re-rexports `session_info` function from the `sessioninfo` package:
https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/blob/f6d0cae9727ebd17b4a8193270bb390dbe5cf0b2/R/session-info.R#L31-L37

And although this function is exported from the package, if one were to simply go by the manual, one would completely miss out on the existence of this function-
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/devtools/devtools.pdf

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11330453/55578932-0dc49f80-56e5-11e9-88af-4dc20f5cd205.png)

Since a lot of users check out available functions by looking at the manual, I was wondering if there is any way to document re-exported function in the `pdf` manual?

title: `devtools::check` doesn't catch invalid file URIs
description:
Although I had 0 `NOTE`, `ERROR`, or `WARNING` on my local machine, this is the `NOTE` I am getting with the development version of R (but not on `R 3.6.0`).
