title: Consider throwing an error when build_manual() fails
description:
Currently, there is no nothing to let you know that something went wrong during compilation of the package manual when `build_manual()` is called. The only difference from a successful call is that the two last lines of output are missing

Successfull call to `build_manual()`:

```r
Hmm ... looks like a package
Creating pdf output from LaTeX ...
Saving output to ‘[some-file-name].pdf’ ...
Done
```

Failing call to `build_manual()`:

```r
Hmm ... looks like a package
Creating pdf output from LaTeX ...
```

May I suggest that, at the very least, the function throws an error saying something went wrong in building the manual.

title: Informative error when on `load_all()` failure due to duplicative Rcpp exports
Print stack trace on error in devtools::document() or devtools::check()
description:
I am trying to get a large codebase with many classes and generics set up as a package. This is a tedious task when using S4 classes and the devtools and roxygen2 packages definitely make it easier. Thanks for that.

However, when I am trying to follow the advice on [this page](http://r-pkgs.had.co.nz/check.html), I run into the following issue: I get back an error from `devtools::document()` or `devtools:check()` that is unspecific as to where the error actually happened (which file and which line). All I seem to get is the error message but no stacktrace, no file or line number.

Is there a way to fix this? Is this a limitation of the way R handles things? For me, just the file where the error occurs would be of great help.

Thanks,
Alexander

title: devtools::install_deps() needs remotes > 2.0.2
description:
The default `upgrade` argument of `devtools::install_deps()` and `devtools::install_dev_deps()`
https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/blob/55f982c6f7a9bef22c659954318a824381d9fdab/R/install.R#L113
has been changed in https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/commit/55f982c6f7a9bef22c659954318a824381d9fdab to accommodate the development version of **remotes**.

However, this changed also needs to increase the minimum required version of **remotes** in the DESCRIPTION of **devtools** to `remotes > 2.0.2`.

Using in-development **devtools**`::install_deps()` with released **remotes** 2.0.2 fails with
```
Error in match.arg(upgrade, c("ask", "always", "never")) : 
  'arg' must be of length 1
```
because at some point, **remotes** 2.0.2 calls
```r
match.arg(upgrade, c("ask", "always", "never"))
```

title: "Would you like to update?" the yes/no options should be in a consistent place
description:
Whenever I install a github package with install_github, I am presented with something like:

```
These packages have more recent versions available.
Which would you like to update?

1:   BH         (1.66.0-1 -> 1.69.0-1) [CRAN]
2:   colorspace (1.3-2    -> 1.4-0   ) [CRAN]
3:   later      (0.7.5    -> 0.8.0   ) [CRAN]
4:   R6         (2.3.0    -> 2.4.0   ) [CRAN]
5:   rlang      (0.3.0.1  -> 0.3.1   ) [CRAN]
6:   CRAN packages only
7:   All
8:   None
```

Let's say I want to update all, so I choose 7.
Next I install another package, and it only has 2 dependencies that can be updated, so now I have to choose 4.

It's a lot of friction to have to scan through the output and choose the right number, and seems like unnecessary adding slowness to the process. I strongly feel that the "CRAN", "All", "None" options should always have the same way to choose them, whether it be 1-2-3 or maybe even "C" "A" "N". Perhaps there's a good argument to doing it the current way that I don't see!

title: devtools and usethis
description:
I'm starting the revision of R Packages.

The relationship of devtools to usethis is a bit awkward. devtools re-exports lots of functions, but also does not re-export many others. I'm adding an early "whole game" chapter that shows the creation of a small toy package. And I can't close the deal without attaching usethis and using it directly.

I think we need to get off this fence:

  1. Admit package devs will probably need to attach both devtools and usethis.
  2. Re-export more usethis stuff from devtools.

If we choose 1., we need to clarify language like this (from v2.0.0 blog post but also the README & pkgdown site):

> devtools will remain the primary package developers will interact with when writing R packages; it will just rely on these other packages internally for most of the functionality.
>
> Generally, you should not need to worry about these different packages, because devtools installs them all automatically. You will need to care, however, if you’re filing a bug because reporting it at the correct place will lead to a speedier resolution.

Honestly, I think we have to do 1. because 2. feels unsustainable / extreme. Would we ever put usethis in Depends 🤔?

Do we have a pithy principle that governs whether devtools will import and re-export a usethis function vs not?

cc @hadley

title: devtools::release seems to handle "NOT_CRAN" in vignettes differently since version 2.0
description:
The computations in the vignettes of my brms package (https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms) take a long time and so I avoid recomputing them on CRAN via the "NOT_CRAN" environment variable. Specifically, I add 

```
params:
  EVAL: !r identical(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN"), "true")
```

to the YAML header of my rmarkdown vignettes. This works as expected.

However, with the release of devtools 2.0, it seems as if `devtools::release(check = FALSE)` seems to be not evaluating the vignettes either so that they are shown unevaluated on CRAN (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/brms/index.html). My question is how to convince the new ` devtools::release` to build the vignettes locally and submit them to CRAN, while using the "NOT_CRAN" environment variable.

Thanks in advance for you help.

Thanks in advance :)

My package, as the title of this issue says, breaks the testthat testing when running `check()` but it works just fine when running `test()`. The use of relative paths is to fetch pictures stored in the `extdata/` folder of the package to run against some tests, I think that the problem is really this because of the following line that is printed when running the check call:

```
R CMD check results
1 error  | 0 warnings | 1 note 
checking tests ... ERROR
  Running ‘testthat.R’
Running the tests in ‘tests/testthat.R’ failed.
Last 13 lines of output:
  [REMOVED LINES]
  7: get_reader(file)(file)
```

Unfortunately, I cannot share the code here due to some concerns about its content. Is there any way that I could debug this by myself trying to find how to fix this? Or allow printing a `getwd()` call inside the function that calls this file -- right now this approach is not working, maybe the output is silent and I don't know how to enable a "debug mode".

Thank you guys for this awesome package :)

title: check_win*() wants to remove vignettes-folder
description:
I guess this one is related to https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/issues/1918 and https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/pull/1824, however, this behaviour is somewhat annoying.

I have vignettes with long computational time to build (Bayesian models), and CRAN policies ask to keep running-time for tests and vignette building short. So I build the vignettes locally and use a switch in the knitr-option that prevents re-building the vignettes on CRAN after submission - so CRAN takes the compiled vignettes from `inst/doc`.

However, this directory is removed each time I run `build_vignettes()` or `check_win*()`. 

My question is, could _removing_ the folder be optional, and not the only and default option? For me, using devtools is now useless to some extent, unfortunately.

title: Can devtools::check() fail on errors?
description:
Hi!
We're developing some R packages using gitlab and gitlab CI. Now it would be very useful if the pipeline could fail in case check() detects errors - unfortunately this seems not possible, yet - or am I maybe missing some setting? For devtools::test() I can set the reporter to "fail", so at least I can use unit tests in the CI process. check(), however, always returns "Job succeeded", independent of the number of errors.

I would appreciate any help in further improving our development processes :-)

Thanks a lot in advance!

title: devtools check new behavior?
devtools check new behavior with folder and archive not cleaned?
description:
Whenn running ctrl+shift+e (check package) in rstudio using devtools::check it creates a folder pkgname.Rcheck and pkgname_version.tar.gz in the upper directory.
If I change some code to alter the check it looks like it uses the old code inside the folder or the archive.

How do I disable this folder creation or at least clean it on fail and success?
There is a Rstudio  option in tools/global options/Packages `cleanup output after successful R CMD check` but it looks like it does not work and it definitely does not clean on failure...

So my workflow used to be 1)run check 2)fix problems and loop but now I have to manually delete this folder and archive to make it work otherwsie it uses old code

Any solution please?

title: check() and test() unstable with system.file()
description:
The `check()` function is unstable with system.file(). When R-studio is started for the first time, `check()` works fine. After executing `check()` a couple of times or after restarting the R session (through the R-studio menu) the function gives the following output:
```
Updating BTL.CJ documentation
Loading BTL.CJ

In addition: Warning message:
In file(file, "rt") :
  file("") only supports open = "w+" and open = "w+b": using the former
Execution halted
```
`test()` provides a similar output.

[Here](https://github.com/SanVerhavert/BTL.CJ/tree/ae04c12008159d677903a150a6c9a79f056abe6b) you can find the repository for the package that gives the issue. title: github_install works with 1.13.6, not with 2.0.0, for a particular repo
description:
I've been trying to troubleshoot a problem installing a package via `install_github`. The following command works with devtools_1.13.6, but not devtools_2.0.0 (Using R 3.5.1)

   devtools::install_github("statgen/SAIGE")

The difference is that there's a fatal error during the build. Specifically the error is

    SAIGE_readDosage_vcf.cpp:1:55: fatal error: ../thirdParty/cget/include/savvy/reader.hpp: No such file or directory

which implies that the file is not in the tar ball. And that's true, with 2.0 I see the message

    installation of package ‘/tmp/RtmpodjtZ7/filebfa461502e93/SAIGE_0.29.4.tar.gz’ had non-zero exit status

and if I go look at that `SAIGE_0.29.4.tar.gz` tarball, I see the file is not there. I also get an error just viewing the table of contents on that file. Specifically using the `-tf` option will say

    tar: Skipping to next header
    tar: Exiting with failure status due to previous errors

So it seems the new version is making an invalid (truncated?) tarball? Is that possible? I didn't see anything in the release notes about there being differences in how tarballs might be generated between versions.

Do you have other suggestions for how to troubleshoot this? I wouldn't be surprised if this ended up being a problem with the repo rather than devtools but it's just odd it works in the other version but not the newer without a clear indication why.

This was run on Ubuntu 16.04.5 LTS and specifically commit 756bbac94144e6e92d9caf0d4a8f428c49377b17 of https://github.com/statgen/SAIGE/. Also note that some of the dependencies will write info to the user's home directory.

description:

I used to be able to install my package from the github repo like this

                                          ,auth_user = "my_git_user" 
                                          ,password = "my_git_password" 
                                          ,ref = "my_branch"

It recently failed with this kind of error

`cannot open URL 'https://my_git_user:my_git_pwd@api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/username/repo/src/my_branch/PathTo/Package1DESCRIPTION'`

It looks to me that a `/` is missing at the end of the url, between the package name and the DESCRIPTION. I could not find a publicly available repository where the packages are located in subdirectories otherwise I would have checked the `subdir` still works. 

Any advice on whether what I am doing is right would be much appreciated :)

Thanks,
Paul

title: reload(".") does not load "."
description:
The behavior of `reload(".")` is a little surprising to me. After unloading `"."`, it tries to load a package with the same name from somewhere in`.libPaths()`. It applies to any case where a path is passed as `pkg` argument. I guess many users expect the package in the given path is loaded by this function even if they know `load_all()` is a more preferable way to reload a package under development.

https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/blob/5bbcac458f7c874e465229c01f07d4ff229d3dfc/R/reload.r#L25-L33

title: spelling: allow use of WORDLIST if found
description:
`devtools` initially used the `spelling` package, which takes advantage of a WORDLIST file if one is found in `inst/`

`hunspell` (the current spelling support) doesn't, and its equivalent mechanism (`ignore`) defaults to an empty vector.

_OBTAINED_: As a result, `devtools:: release` can't use a package-specific dictionary, and catches a big list of false positives each time (or to it simply being turned off by setting to `NULL`).

_DESIRED_: Allow `release()` and `spell_check()` to detect the presence of `inst/WORDLIST` and use it (i.e., read in, parse into a vector of words, and pass to `ignore=`) unless `ignore = NULL`.

https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/issues/1645

title: under test(), cannot detach the package being tested
description:
Within a package named "packagefileprob", which defines and exports a function `bar`, in tests/test-detach.R, I have
```
context('whatever')

test_that('some tests where I detach my package', {
  detach(package:packagefileprob, unload = TRUE, force = TRUE)
  expect_error(bar())
  expect_silent(packagefileprob::bar())
  library(packagefileprob)
})

library(clipr)

test_that('some tests where I detach a different package', {
  detach(package:clipr, unload = TRUE, force = TRUE)
  expect_error(dr_clipr())
  expect_error(clipr::dr_clipr(), NA)
  library(packagefileprob)
})

```

From the command line the `test_that` call runs silently, as expected. It also works if I run `testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat")`. But if I run `devtools::test()`, I get:

```
test-detach.R:6: failure: some tests where I detach my package
`bar()` did not throw an error.
```

title: Github GraphQL API requires Authentication
description:
When `GITHUB_PAT` is not set, devtools's Github functionality ceases to work:

``` r
Sys.unsetenv("GITHUB_PAT")
devtools::update_packages("devtools")
#> condition in stop(github_error(req)): This endpoint requires you to be authenticated. (401)
```

Created on 2018-08-08 by the [reprex package](http://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.0).

```r
> traceback()
9: stop(github_error(req))
8: github_response(req)
7: github_POST("graphql", body = jsonlite::toJSON(auto_unbox = TRUE, 
       list(query = query, variables = list(org = username, repo = repo, 
    ...
6: github_sha(username = remote$username, repo = remote$repo, host = remote$host, 
       ref = remote$ref, pat = remote$auth_token)
5: remote_sha.github_remote(X[[i]], ...)
4: FUN(X[[i]], ...)
3: vapply(remote, remote_sha, character(1))
2: package_deps(pkgs, dependencies = dependencies, repos = repos, 
       type = type)
1: devtools::update_packages("devtools")
```

This is also discussed in:
https://community.rstudio.com/t/devtools-install-github-error-this-endpoint-requires-you-to-be-authenticated-401/11972/13

The issue seems to be that GraphQL always requires authentication: https://developer.github.com/v4/guides/forming-calls/#authenticating-with-graphql

As seen in: https://api.github.com/graphql vs https://api.github.com

Previously `GITHUB_PAT` is only required when working with private repository. We could either revert this change or only use GraphQL API when PAT is detected.

p.s. This issue is not caught in CI because CI has built-in PAT.

Notably, the file `pkg_name-Ex.Rout` (to be stored at `/tests/Examples/pkg_name-Ex.Rout.save`) contains a bunch of line like these which are not in the same file generated by `R CMD check`:
```
base::assign(".ExTimings", "pkg_name-Ex.timings", pos = 'CheckExEnv')
base::cat("name\tuser\tsystem\telapsed\n", file=base::get(".ExTimings", pos = 'CheckExEnv'))
base::assign(".format_ptime",
+ function(x) {
+   if(!is.na(x[4L])) x[1L] <- x[1L] + x[4L]
+   if(!is.na(x[5L])) x[2L] <- x[2L] + x[5L]
+   options(OutDec = '.')
+   format(x[1L:3L], digits = 7L)
+ },
+ pos = 'CheckExEnv')

### * </HEADER>

...

base::assign(".dptime", (proc.time() - get(".ptime", pos = "CheckExEnv")), pos = "CheckExEnv")

...

base::assign(".ptime", proc.time(), pos = "CheckExEnv")

Consequently when the file generated by devtool's check is used as reference output, a lot of differences are found.

title: Installing R package from GitHub Enterprise
description:
I'm trying to install a private R package from my company's GitHub Enterprise. I referred to the instructions in #688 and #892. 

The process appears to be:
1. Create a personal access token inside your company's instance of GitHub Enterprise
2. Create a GITHUB_PAT variable inside your .Renviron file
3. Set the host to the GitHub Enterprise API

I'm surprised to see that `install_github` still calls out to raw.githubusercontent.com (even though I specified a host that points to my company's GitHub Enterprise).

> Sys.getenv('GITHUB_PAT')

When I ran debug, I found that `devtools:::remote_package_name.github_remote` calls out (hard-coded) to https://raw.githubusercontent.com.

}
<environment: namespace:devtools>

state caries between runs of devtools:: build_vignettes()
description:
State caries between runs of `devtools:: build_vignettes()`.  This can cause a problem as side-effects of one vignette run can effect others.  Below is an example where if `devtools:: build_vignettes()` is run in a clean environment everything is fine.  However if `devtools:: build_vignettes()` is then re-run it errors out (due to a value assignment being left behind from the first run).

`````r
---
title: "title"
author: "author"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{example}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

Running `devtools::build_vignettes()` twice in a row with this file as a vignette errors 
out because the assignment "`ChickWeight <- NULL`" stays live between runs and then
obscures the original `datasets::ChickWeight`.

```{r}
ChickWeight <- dplyr::mutate(ChickWeight, Time = Time+1)
ChickWeight <- NULL
```
`````

title: install_github() can fail if installation runs an executable script
description:
On R installations that have `options(unzip = "internal")`, installation of packages can fail.

For example, these will fail on Linux and Mac:

```R
# Most installations have options(unzip = "/usr/bin/unzip"), but we'll set it to
# internal for this example.
options(unzip = "internal")

devtools::install_github("r-lib/fs")

devtools::install_github("rstudio/httpuv@v1.4.3")
```

The error looks like this:

```
(cd libuv \
	&& touch aclocal.m4 \
	&& touch -r aclocal.m4 configure Makefile.in \
&& CC="gcc" CFLAGS="-g -O2  -fpic -fvisibility=hidden" AR="ar" RANLIB="ranlib" LDFLAGS="-L/usr/local/lib" ./configure --quiet)
/bin/bash: line 3: ./configure: Permission denied
Makevars:32: recipe for target 'libuv/Makefile' failed
make: *** [libuv/Makefile] Error 126
ERROR: compilation failed for package ‘fs’
```

The problem is that the internal `unzip` does not preserve execute permissions.

Most installations of R default to `/usr/bin/unzip`, but some do not. With httpuv, we heard about this issue from a few people who had their own builds of R. On rstudio.cloud and rsp.rstudioservices.com, the default for unzip is `internal`, so installation of these packages from GitHub fails. The error is pretty cryptic so we went through a bunch of rounds of communication, asking if there were NFS issues, limits on sudo permissions, or weird filesystems that were used for the temp dir. But it turned out to just be just due to the internal unzip.

@jimhester and I discussed changing `install_github` to download a .tar.gz instead of .zip. Assuming the internal untar preserves execute permissions, this would solve the problem with `install_github()`. However, it wouldn't solve the problem with .zip files in general.

title: SHA1 check false positives with multiple libraries
description:
When `install_github` checks the SHA1 to see if a package actually needs to be updated, it should only check in the library where the package is about to be installed.

Currently it gives a false positive when you try to install a package in a given library, but the package is already available from another library. For example:

```r
devtools::install_github('rwebapps/gitstats')
# Installing gitstats
# ...
# * DONE (gitstats)

my_private_lib <- tempdir()
withr::with_libpaths(my_private_lib, devtools::install_github('rwebapps/gitstats'))
# Skipping install of 'gitstats' from a github remote, the SHA1 (fc578831) has not changed since last install.
#  Use `force = TRUE` to force installation

library("gitstats", lib.loc = my_private_lib)
# Error in library("gitstats", lib.loc = my_private_lib) : 
#  there is no package called ‘gitstats’
```

Not sure if this intended but it is dangerous. When working with many libraries (such as packrat) you want to assume that installing a package in a given library will indeed install or update the package in that library to the latest version. The fact that the package was also available from another lib during installation shouldn't matter.

Error in .C(Cname, t(data), as.integer(k), d, n, nn.index = integer(n *  :

unloadNamespace("clusterExperiment") not successful, probably because another loaded package depends on it.Forcing unload. If you encounter problems, please restart R.

title: Remotes field with `url::` prefix not being installed
description:
The `mcclust.ext` package extends some clustering algorithms and is located (ONLY) in a tarball located at http://wrap.warwick.ac.uk/71934/.  Now this is likely not the best long-term example to use, but it shows how a `url::` in `Remotes` fails to install.

``` r
library(desc)
library(devtools)
```

## Check if Package Installed
Here's a simple test to see if the package `mcclust.ext` is installed.  If it is installed, it is removed.
```r
check_url_installed = function() {
  res = "mcclust.ext" %in% installed.packages()[, "Package"]
  return(res)
}
check_url_installed()
#> [1] TRUE
if (check_url_installed()) {
  remove.packages("mcclust.ext")
}
#> Removing package from '/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.4/Resources/library'
#> (as 'lib' is unspecified)
check_url_installed()
#> [1] FALSE
```

## Fake `DESCRIPTION` file
Here we create a fake `DESCRIPTION` file for the `testurl` package. 
```r
desc <- description$new("!new")
auth = person("Joe", "Schmoe", role = c("aut", "cre"), 
              email = "asdf@gmail.com")
desc$set("Package", "testurl")
desc$add_remotes("url::http://wrap.warwick.ac.uk/71934/1/mcclust.ext_1.0.tar.gz")
desc$set_dep(type = "Suggests", package = "mcclust.ext")
desc$set_authors(auth)
desc$del("URL")
desc$del("BugReports")
desc$set("License", "GPL-2")
desc$set("Maintainer", "Joe Schmoe <asdf@gmail.com>")
desc$set("Description", "This is a test.")
desc$set("Title", "Title of the Package")
```

We write this out to a temporary directory for `devtools` to work with.
```r
tdir = tempfile()
tdir = file.path(tdir, "testurl")
dir.create(tdir, recursive = TRUE)
tfile = file.path(tdir, "DESCRIPTION")
desc$write(file = tfile)
```

## `devtools` functions don't install the package

```r
devtools::package_deps(pkg = tdir, dependencies = "Suggests")
#> Not on CRAN ----------------------------
#>  package                                                                              
#>  /var/folders/1s/wrtqcpxn685_zk570bnx9_rr0000gr/T//Rtmpqq0bk3/file139fdc55edb8/testurl

#>  NA        NA        CRAN

check_url_installed()
#> [1] FALSE
deps = devtools::dev_package_deps(pkg = tdir, dependencies = "Suggests")
res = devtools::install_deps(pkg = tdir, dependencies = "Suggests")
check_url_installed()
#> [1] FALSE
res = devtools::install_deps(pkg = tdir, dependencies = "Suggests")

devtools::install(tdir, dependencies = TRUE)
#> Installing testurl
#> '/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/bin/R' --no-site-file  \
#>   --no-environ --no-save --no-restore --quiet CMD INSTALL  \
#>   '/private/var/folders/1s/wrtqcpxn685_zk570bnx9_rr0000gr/T/Rtmpqq0bk3/file139fdc55edb8/testurl'  \
#>   --library='/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.4/Resources/library'  \
#>   --install-tests
#> 
check_url_installed()
#> [1] FALSE

devtools::install(tdir, dependencies = TRUE)
#> Installing testurl
#> '/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/bin/R' --no-site-file  \
#>   --no-environ --no-save --no-restore --quiet CMD INSTALL  \
#>   '/private/var/folders/1s/wrtqcpxn685_zk570bnx9_rr0000gr/T/Rtmpqq0bk3/file139fdc55edb8/testurl'  \

title: Request: create_citation
description:
(Seems wrong posting a feature request to an issues site but not sure where else to go with this... sorry if wrong...)

Could you have a create_citation()? 

create() makes your package skeleton. That makes DESCRIPTION template using create_description (and build_description). Once the user has updated the DESCRIPTION, they have to make CITATION, but unless they have anything special to document (which tends to come later) that is the manual, and you can extract a preliminary version of that from DESCRIPTION. Adding a create_citation() would save users wanting that minimal CITATION a transpose job and mean even new users would have provisional CITATION in place.    

Guessing you would break it into a create_ and build_citation and use functions available through devtools, but I think the process is do-able, e.g.:

`
create_citation <- function (pkg = ".", overwrite = FALSE) 
{

  #check package, inst and CITATION are useable...
	.pkg <- as.package(pkg)    
	test <- file.path(.pkg$path, c("R", "src", "data"))
	if (!any(file.exists(test))) {
		stop("'", pkg, 
		     "' does not look like a package: no R/, src/ or data directories", 
		     call. = FALSE)
	}
	if (!file.exists(file.path(.pkg$path, "inst"))) 
		dir.create(file.path(.pkg$path, "inst"))
	if (file.exists(file.path(.pkg$path, "inst/CITATION"))) 
	  if(overwrite){
	    file.remove(file.path(.pkg$path, "inst/CITATION"))
	  } else {
		  stop("'", pkg, "' already has CITATION", call. = FALSE)
	}

  #get citation info
  pkg <- .pkg$package #pkg name from description
  #if pkg name in title use as is else pkg: title
  title <- if(length(grep(pkg, .pkg$title))>0) .pkg$title else 
               paste(pkg, ": ", .pkg$title, sep="")
  #if date in decription use that else use this year
  year <- if("date" %in% names(.pkg))
             format(as.Date(.pkg$date), "%Y") else 
                 format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")
  #make manual and text authors records 
  authors <- paste(format(eval(parse(text = .pkg$`authors@r`)),
                          include = c("given", "family")))
  txt.aut <- paste(authors, collapse=", ")
  txt.aut <- paste("         textVersion = paste(\"", txt.aut, " (", year,
                   ") \",", sep ="")
  if(length(authors)>1)
    txt.aut <- gsub(paste(", ", authors[length(authors)], sep=""), 
                    paste(" and ", authors[length(authors)], sep=""), 
                    txt.aut)
  man.aut <- paste("as.person(\"", authors, "\")", sep="")
  man.aut[1] <- paste("         author = personList(", 
                      man.aut[1], ",", sep="")
  if(length(man.aut)>1)
    man.aut[2:length(man.aut)] <- paste("                             ",
                                        man.aut[2:length(man.aut)], ",",
                                        sep="")
  man.aut[length(man.aut)] <- gsub("[)],$", ")),", man.aut[length(man.aut)])
  
  #make a citation template
  #note no longer strictly template
  #pre-formatting authors details...  
  out <- c(
    "citHeader(\"To cite '[packname]' package in publications use:\")",
    "",
    "citEntry(entry=\"Manual\",",
    "         title = \"[packtitle]\",",
    man.aut,
    "         year = \"[year]\",",
    "         note = paste(\"R package version \",",
    "                    packageDescription(\"[packname]\",",
    "                                 fields = c(\"Version\"))[1], sep=\"\"),",
    txt.aut,
    "                    \"[packtitle], \",",
    "                    \"R package version \",",
    "                    packageDescription(\"[packname]\",",
    "                         fields = c(\"Version\"))[1],\".\", sep=\"\"))",
    "",
    "citFooter(\"Please cite both '[packname]' and R \",",
    "          \"when using '[packname]'.\",",
    "          \"For R citation, see \", sQuote(\"citation()\"))"
  )
  
  #update template
  out <- gsub("[[]packname[]]", pkg, out)
  out <- gsub("[[]packtitle[]]", title, out)
  out <- gsub("[[]year[]]", year, out)
  
  #make CITATION  
  fileConn<-file(file.path(.pkg$path, "inst/CITATION"), "at")
  writeLines(out, fileConn)
  close(fileConn)
}
`

title: C:\Program is not recognized as internal or external program
description:
Hi All,

I realize this is probably a bug in R-core, but I figured maybe a workaround can be implemented in devtools, since it shows up because of the way R is invoked from this package.

Basically on Windows, depending on system configuration, `install_github` fails with a message similar to 
``C:\Program is not recognized as internal or external program``

This happens when both of the following conditions are met
- R is installed in a directory that contains whitespace in its name (e.g. "Program Files")
- Short filenames (SFN) are disabled for the volume on which R is installed

The second point can be verified with this command (assuming R is installed on the C drive; requires admin privileges, more info [here](https://technet.microsoft.com/en-us/library/cc785435(v=ws.11).aspx))

 ``fsutil.exe behavior query disable8dot3 C:``

if the output looks like

``
8dot3 name creation is disabled on C:
``

then you are in trouble because R will not be able to handle a path with spaces properly, AND it will not be able to get an SFN-style path because it's disabled on your volume.

A telltale sign of this problem is that you won't be able to start `R.exe` from the command line, even though the RGui will start fine. This does not create a problem for the built-in `install.packages` function because it does not spawn another R process like `devtools` seems to do.

title: CRAN dependencies installation fails on Windows with formal argument "repos" matched by multiple actual arguments
description:
The error comes from line 42 in `install_remote` where `...` also contains argument `repos` passed from `update_packages`:
```R
install_packages(package_name, repos = remote$repos, type = remote$pkg_type, dependencies = NA, ..., quiet = quiet,
                     out_dir = out_dir, skip_if_log_exists = skip_if_log_exists)
```

The following fixes the error, by merging all repositories into a singe `repos` argument:
```R
# merge repos arguments
args <- list(...)
args[['repos']] <- unique(c(remote$repos, args[['repos']]))
# build argument list for install_packages call 
args <- c(list(pkgs = package_name,
                type = remote$pkg_type, dependencies = NA, quiet = quiet,
                out_dir = out_dir, skip_if_log_exists = skip_if_log_exists), 
          args)
do.call(install_packages, args)
```

title: Dependence on R version '3.3.3' not with patchlevel 0
description:
Hi, 

I am using the development version of `devtools` and ran `devtools::check()`, which produced 0 errors, 0 warnings, and 0 notes for my package. So I submitted the package to `CRAN`, but their `R CMD CHECK` threw the following warning and the submission was rejected (full `check.log` provided below). 
```
* checking DESCRIPTION meta-information ... WARNING
Dependence on R version '3.3.3' not with patchlevel 0
```

title: devtools' system.file() breaks citation()
description:
Hello,

When I ran unit tests for my package (with testthat), the tests crashed on the `citation("my_package_name")` function referenced in one of the modules, with an error message:

> $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors

and an additional warning:

> no package 'my_package_name' was found

I investigated it and it seems that the following code in `citation()` is the problem:

    dir <- system.file(package = package, lib.loc = lib.loc)
    # ...
    meta <- packageDescription(pkg = package, lib.loc = dirname(dir))
 
When a test is run, `system.file()` (overwritten by devtools) points to the `inst/` directory in the source location of the package, which is what `packageDescription()` can't handle, yielding NA and a warning message.

I don't know if this is a fault of devtools, testthat or R's base, but definitely it's an annoying bug rendering unit tests useless in this specific case.

Best regards,
Paweł

title: Multisession loading problems when using future

When using the `multisession` parallelization planning in the `future` package, `future` will try to load all the packages present in the master session. The problem is that when starting a new session, R will not be able to load the package under development since it has not been installed. What is the best approach for that? Does `devtools` implement something like`pip install -e .`, which is to install a package in editable mode?

I have engaged in a very fruitful discussion [here](https://github.com/HenrikBengtsson/future/issues/206#issuecomment-373249972) which might have to clarify the problem.

title: check() does not respect `document = FALSE`
description:
## Expected Behavior

Calling

``` r
check(pkg = "package.name", document = FALSE)
```

should **not** run `document()` on the package being checked.
## Actual Behavior

The `check()` function [currently ignores](https://github.com/hadley/devtools/blob/fa4d4f668c7a7674a48b45a39ada59be7655fa5e/R/check.r#L13-17) the value of `document` passed to it as an argument. Consequently, the `document()`function is always called on `pkg` no matter the input to the function:

``` r
check <- function(pkg = NULL, document = TRUE) {
  pkg <- as.package(pkg)

  document(pkg, clean = TRUE)
  message("Checking ", pkg$package)
```

In short, any time a user calls `check()` on a package that package will be forcibly documented, AND the `document()` function will always flush the roxygen cache, since it's called with `clean = TRUE`

title: Safeguards to avoid accidental nuking of project directories
description:
Say a user ill-advisedly runs `dev_mode('~/foo')` where `~/foo` is the same directory as given by the default function in `~/.Rpackages`, having misunderstood the `path` parameter … and then runs `install('bar')`.

The user's new `bar` package will be installed from `~/foo/bar/` — into `~/foo/bar`. This will replace his project directory … and, significantly, discard subdirectories such as, say, `.git`. You see where this is going.

If the user hasn't already run `git push` before this, then he's just lost a bunch of work. Just, you know, theoretically speaking. (I'm not at all in pain, and if I were, I would not admit it.)

To avoid such accidents:
- `dev_mode` could check whether its `path` parameter is the same as the directory given by the default function in `~/.Rpackages`, or the parent of any other directories mapped in that file, and raise an error.
- `install` could check whether the directory it's about to overwrite contains a VCS subdirectory like  `.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, etc., and raise an error (or maybe preserve such subdirectories).

install <- function (pkg = NULL, reload = TRUE, lib)               # <- this line changed
{
  pkg <- as.package(pkg)
  message("Installing ", pkg$package)
  install_deps(pkg)
  built_path <- build(pkg, tempdir())
  on.exit(unlink(built_path))
  install.packages(built_path, lib, repos = NULL, type = "source") # <- this line changed
  if (reload) 
    reload(pkg)
  invisible(TRUE)
}

install_github <- function (repo, username = "hadley", branch = "master", lib) # <- this line changed 
{
      message("Installing ", repo, " from ", username)
      name <- paste(username, "-", repo, sep = "")
      url <- paste("https://github.com/", username, "/", repo, 
              sep = "")
      zip_url <- paste("https://nodeload.github.com/", username, 
              "/", repo, "/zipball/", branch, sep = "")
      src <- file.path(tempdir(), paste(name, ".zip", sep = ""))
      content <- getBinaryURL(zip_url, .opts = list(followlocation = TRUE, 
                  ssl.verifypeer = FALSE))
      writeBin(content, src)
      on.exit(unlink(src), add = TRUE)
      pkg_name <- basename(as.character(unzip(src, list = TRUE)$Name[1]))
      out_path <- file.path(tempdir(), pkg_name)
      unzip(src, exdir = tempdir())
      on.exit(unlink(out_path), add = TRUE)
      if (!file.exists(file.path(out_path, "DESCRIPTION"))) {
    stop("Does not appear to be an R package", call. = FALSE)
      }
      install(out_path, lib)                                                   # <- this line changed
}
```

title: install fails when there are spaces in the path name
description:

```
R(paste("CMD INSTALL ", built_path, " --library=", .libPaths()[1], 
        sep = ""), tempdir())
```

If there are spaces in `.libPaths()[1]`, then this command fails.

op <- options(useFancyQuotes = FALSE)

        sep = ""), tempdir())

```

Another alternative, at least under Windows, might be to use shortPathName(.libPaths()[1]).

title: adding install_bitbucket
description:
Hi Hadley,

beside github I use bitbucket as my git host as it offers free private repos.
It would be nice to have this feature included as well.
Below is the slightly modified `github_install` code in case you want to add it.

```
#' Attempts to install a package directly from bitbucket
#'
#' This function is vectorised so you can install multiple packages in 
#' a single command.
#'
#' @param username  bitbucket username
#' @param repo      Repo name
#' @param branch    Desired branch or snapshot ID - defaults to \code{"master"}
#' @param ...       Other arguments passed on to \code{\link{install}}.
#' @family package installation
#' @export  
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{
#' install_bitbucket("testrepo")
#' install_bitbucket(c("testrepo", "testrepo2")
#' }
#' 
install_bitbucket <- function(repo, username = "markheckmann", branch = "master", ...) 
{  
  message("Installing github repo(s) ", 
          paste(repo, branch, sep = "/", collapse = ", "), 
          " from ", 
          paste(username, collapse = ", "))  

  url <- paste("https://bitbucket.org/", username, "/", repo,
               "/get/", branch, ".zip", sep = "")  
  install_url(url, paste0(branch, ".zip") , ...)
}
```

Cheers
Mark

title: Make packages loaded by load_all() children of global environment
description:
Objects loaded via `load_all()` behave somewhat differently from loading those loaded with `library()`.

With `load_all()`, the package environment is not a child of the global environment. But with `library()`, it is a child of the global environment.

This code will illustrate:

``` R
# This prints all parent environments, until it hits top (emptyenv)
printenvs <- function(e = parent.frame(), n = 100) {
  cat(str(e, give.attr=F))
  i <- 1
  while(i < n) {
    if (identical(e, emptyenv()))
      break

    e <- parent.env(e)
    cat(str(e, give.attr=F))
    i <- i+1
  }
  cat("\n")
  return(e)
}


library(ggplot2)
debugonce(qplot)
qplot()
printenvs()
# <environment: R_GlobalEnv> is a parent


# === Might need to restart R to do this ===
library(devtools)
load_all('.')
debugonce(qplot)
qplot()
printenvs()
# <environment: R_GlobalEnv> is not a parent
```

title: document() doesn't work properly with empty NAMESPACE file
description:
When you run `document()` on a package with an empty NAMESPACE file, as is the case for a new package made with `create()`, it gives a `?` prompt.

```
> create('testpackage')
 ... 
> document('testpackage')
Updating foo documentation
Loading foo
?
```

The problem is that `parseNamespaceFile()` calls `parse()`, which hangs. Possible solutions include:
- Don't create an empty NAMESPACE file.
- Have code in `parse_ns_file()` that will call `parseNamespaceFile()` on a non-existent directory, like this:  `parseNamespaceFile('xxxxx', 'xxxxx', mustExist=FALSE)`. This will return a list with the appropriate entries.

```
rds <- dir(file.path(pkg, "man"), full.names = TRUE)
```

Should be as in [R/run_examples, line 30-31](https://github.com/hadley/devtools/blob/master/R/run-examples.r#L30)

```
path_man <- file.path(pkg$path, "man")
rds <- dir(path_man, pattern = "\\.[Rr]d$", full.names = TRUE)

title: @aliases tag is mishandling S4 methods
description:
Hi guys, 

This is probably a roxygen thing, but I inherited the bug when I updated devtools. If I make an S4 method and then document it as an alias in the S4 class page, quotes get inserted around the alias. As a result, R doesn't recognize the link and thinks I have an undocumented S4 class. This then fails R CMD check. To recreate the error, put this in a file and document it:

```
#' ggsubplot class
#'
#' a ggsubplot object is a ggplot object that has been extended to include methods 
#' for embedding subplots when plotting. 
#'
#' @name ggsubplot-class
#' @rdname ggsubplot-class
#' @exportClass ggsubplot
#' @aliases show,ggsubplot-method
setClass("ggsubplot")

#' @export
setMethod("show", signature(object = "ggsubplot"), function(object){
    print(object)
})
```

The Rd file ends up containing

```
\alias{"show,ggsubplot-method"}
```

but what R wants is 

```
\alias{show,ggsubplot-method}
```

Cheers.

title: check_cran doesn't always install packages in the right order
description:
When there are many packages to install, `check_cran()` seems to not install them in the right order every time.

``` R
# This will download zillions of packages, so don't try it at home
revdep_check('ggplot2')

# Running again will install a few more, and so on
revdep_check('ggplot2')
```

I think the problem is that some packages require other packages to compile. For example a package that uses Rcpp to compile must have Rcpp installed first. (Other packages which only require an unzipping to install shouldn't have this problem.) So this is something that will probably happen on Linux, but not Windows and Mac OS X.

Update: It appears that the problem isn't the order, but that the `install.packages()` doesn't properly use `.libPaths()`.

title: Provide functionality to install binary from github
description:
Windows users sometimes have trouble installing from source. Package authors can provide binary versions of packages as github downloads. It would be nice to have a feature which will allow installation of the binary. 

A crude function that I cooked up is shown below.

``` r
install_github_binary <- function(repo, user, version){
  url = sprintf('https://github.com/downloads/%s/%s/%s_%s.zip', user, repo, repo, version')
  tf = tempfile(); on.exit(unlink(tf))
  message('Downloading binary from github')
  download.file(url, destfile = tf, method = 'curl'
  install.packages(tf)
}
```

If this is of interest, I could issue a pull request and also make the function more robust if the download file is not available. Ideally, it would be nice to weave this in to `install_github` or `install_url` both of which I believe only install from source.

title: has_devel() will complain if R tries to run i386 within RStudio on Mac
description:
There is a section on the 
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/bin/R
that _may_ read like:

```
# Since this script can be called recursively, we allow R_ARCH to 
# be overridden from the environment. 
# This script is shared by parallel installs, so nothing in it should 
# depend on the sub-architecture except the default here. 
: ${R_ARCH=`arch`}
```

this is unfortunate since `arch` will typically return `i386` even on modern Macs

This will generate problems if `has_devel()` is run within RStudio

```
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/bin/R --vanilla CMD SHLIB foo.c 

gcc -arch i386 -std=gnu99 -I/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/include -I/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/include/i386 -DNDEBUG  -I/usr/local/include    -fPIC  -g -O2  -c foo.c -o foo.o
gcc -arch i386 -std=gnu99 -dynamiclib -Wl,-headerpad_max_install_names -undefined dynamic_lookup -single_module -multiply_defined suppress -L/usr/local/lib -o foo.so foo.o -F/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/.. -framework R -Wl,-framework -Wl,CoreFoundation
Error in dyn.load(dylib) : 
  unable to load shared object '/var/folders/v1/wlzvt5ld0r56456kbf6lzj2h0000gn/T//RtmpGxFh6c/foo.so':
  dlopen(/var/folders/v1/wlzvt5ld0r56456kbf6lzj2h0000gn/T//RtmpGxFh6c/foo.so, 6): no suitable image found.  Did find:
    /var/folders/v1/wlzvt5ld0r56456kbf6lzj2h0000gn/T//RtmpGxFh6c/foo.so: mach-o, but wrong architecture
```

notice RStudio rightly thinks `x86_64` is the correct version

```
> version
               _                            
platform       x86_64-apple-darwin9.8.0     
arch           x86_64                       
os             darwin9.8.0                  
system         x86_64, darwin9.8.0          
status                                      
major          2                            
minor          15.1                         
year           2012                         
month          06                           
day            22                           
svn rev        59600                        
language       R                            
version.string R version 2.15.1 (2012-06-22)
nickname       Roasted Marshmallows     
```

I think the only solution is set `R_ARCH` to `/x86_64` in that script (as it appears oddly enough on my other machine)

```
: ${R_ARCH=/x86_64}
```

 or as an environment variable. I just wanted to alert others who might see this error.

Importing an S4 generic from an installed package and exporting a new implementation from your package doesn't work
description:
As the title says: imagine there is an S4 generic defined in a 3rd package, like `coef` from the package `stats4`. Now my package I'm `dev`-ing registers a method for `coef` for one of my classes and `exportMethods` it, this method is not "available".

The simple package/example is [here](https://github.com/lianos/devtools/tree/master/inst/tests/s4-mojo). I've made a dummy class `Model` with a `coef` slot. I've imported the `coef` generic from the `stats4` package, and have defined it for the `Model` class. Lastly, this method is exported via my package's `NAMESPACE`. 

OK, so:

```
library(devtools)
load_all('s4-mojo')
m <- new("Model")
coef(m)
## Error: $ operator not defined for this S4 class
```

The problem is that the `coef` generic isn't loaded, and a call to `coef` uses the the `stats::coef` S3 Generic. (Calling `load_all(..., export_all=TRUE)` doesn't change that.

I can fetch the method "from thin air" and use it:

```
f <- getMethod("coef", "Model")
f(m)
## numeric(0)
```

After installing the `s4-mojo` package and starting a fresh R session, everything works as expected:

```
library(s4mojo)
m <- new("Model")
coef(m)
f(m)
## numeric(0)
```

I'm pretty sure I've defined, imported/exported the generics correctly, so ... I think this should work?

title: Generate more detailed error message when error in load_code
description:
1. Take any preferred source/dev package
2. add `stop("some error)` somewhere in one of the source files
3. load_all => this -- correctly -- throws an error
4. traceback()

This will show something like:

```
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : some error
> traceback()
8: stop(e) at load-code.r#23
7: value[[3L]](cond)
6: tryCatchOne(expr, names, parentenv, handlers[[1L]])
5: tryCatchList(expr, classes, parentenv, handlers)
4: tryCatch(lapply(paths, sys.source, envir = env, chdir = TRUE, 
       keep.source = TRUE), error = function(e) {
       clear_cache()
       unload(pkg)
       stop(e)
   }) at load-code.r#17
3: load_code(pkg) at load.r#131
2: load_all(pkg, ...)
```

With this error, one cannot see where the error occurred. The least one could ask for is the filename where it happened, which is readily available in the argument passed to sys.source.
Putting `tryCatch` inside the `lapply` call would do the trick:

``` r
lapply(paths, function(file, ...){
    tryCatch(sys.source(file, ...), error = function(e) {
       clear_cache()
       unload(pkg)      
      e$message <- paste0(e$message, ' [in file: ', file, ']')
       stop(e)
   })
    }, envir = env, chdir = TRUE, keep.source = TRUE)
```

Would be great to get the error line number as well. I have just sent a request to r-devel to know how one can get this information (note that in this respect source and sys.source are not equivalent, see post: https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-devel/2013-March/066144.html).

title: Locale for R() shouldn't always be C
description:
I think the use of the C locale can lead to spurious warnings when checking packages, such as when the package uses UTF-8 or other. See the warnings here, for example: https://github.com/wch/ggplot2-checkresults/blob/master/00check-summary.txt

This message seems relevant:
https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-devel/2011-July/061661.html

Also, from [Writing R Extensions](http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html#Checking-packages):

> You do need to ensure that the package is checked in a suitable locale if it contains non-ASCII characters. Such packages are likely to fail some of the checks in a C locale, and R CMD check will warn if it spots the problem. You should be able to check any package in a UTF-8 locale (if one is available). Beware that although a C locale is rarely used at a console, it may be the default if logging in remotely or for batch jobs.

title: create defaults to GPL-3 license
description:
Opening this issue based on a comment from Stack Overflow: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/15789036/namespaces-without-packages#comment22524137_15794201

The default for `create` is to make a package GPL-3 licensed. This contrasts with `package.skeleton` which defines the license as "What license is it under?" (a value which will not pass `R CMD check`). 

I propose a compromise that the default license should be `file LICENSE`. This specification is allowable according to Writing R Extensions. If there is no `LICENSE` file, the check gives a warning

```
* checking DESCRIPTION meta-information ... WARNING
Invalid license file pointers: LICENSE
```

compared to

```
* checking DESCRIPTION meta-information ... WARNING
Non-standard license specification:
  What license is it under?
Standardizable: FALSE
```

Even this warning can be eliminated by adding a file `LICENSE` with the contents 

> None

This will allow building/installing without warning without assuming any licensing (in fact, assuming no licensing). For simple (or personal) use, this is fine. Prior to distribution, an appropriate license must be decided on, but that is a deliberate choice then. A check for this default `LICENSE` file can be added to `release`, since a non-redistributable package can't be hosted on CRAN.

The new default license should also be used for issue #281.

title: visual map of all functions in a package
description:
## Aim

Facilitate the understanding of complex packages with a visual overview of all the functions present in a package. Inspiration can be drawn from `foodweb` in the `mcbutils` package and `graphviz` (visualise dependencies between functions in graph from).
## Technical considerations
- arranging different pieces together could be automated using two
  kinds of meta-information: @family from roxygen2, and the network of
  dependencies (e.g using mvbutils::foodweb). A given family of pieces
  could be layout in a column, while inter-dependencies could be
  indicated by a common colour scheme, for example.
- there could be special markers (e.g a small asterisc) to indicate
  functions that are not exported.
- there should be a function that returns a grob describing a given
  function (with optional color and asterisk arguments). This grob would
  have widthDetails etc. methods so that it can be placed easily on a
  page.
- the gridSvg package could be used to animate the output
  interactively; for example highlighting dependencies on mouse-over, showing the function description as a tool-tip, etc.

title: Better support for R-Forge package layout
description:
Currently, it seems to be problematic to host a package on both GitHub and R-Forge.
- R-Forge expects the package to live in the `pkg` subdirectory, or even a subdirectory inside `pkg`
- `install_github` expects a `DESCRIPTION` file in the main directory of the repository

[GitHub supports SVN access](https://help.github.com/articles/support-for-subversion-clients) out of the box. R-Forge supports (or [used to support](http://r-forge.r-project.org/tracker/?func=detail&atid=194&aid=2111&group_id=34)) external SVN repositories. It would be favorable to use exactly the same layout in both GitHub and R-Forge, also to be able to host files not related to the R package (Makefiles, RStudio project files, ignore files, ...).

Options to resolve this include:
1. Optionally, search the directory tree recursively for `DESCRIPTION` files
2. Supporting a vector as `subdir` parameter

The first option is nice but will fail... for the `devtools` package in the first place, because of all the test packages. The second option is a simple solution which not yet supports the multi-package layout of R-Forge, but I'm not sure if this is necessary.

Even if using GitHub as external SVN repos won't work, this issue still makes sense: it should be possible to mirror the GitHub SVN to the R-Forge SVN, as a very last resort using some `svnrdump` hackery.

title: For check_cran, make sure that libpath is same as that specified in .Renviron
description:
See #180 and https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-devel/2012-October/065111.html.  Due to a bug in `install.packages`, `check_cran()` should have a check that the `R_LIB` specified in `.Renviron` matches the `libpath` passed to the function.

For example, compare this:

```
# ~/.Renviron contains:
# R_LIBS=/tmp/R-lib

revdep_check('ggplot2', libpath='/tmp/R-lib')
```

to this:

```
# ~/.Renviron contains:
# R_LIBS=/tmp/R-lib

revdep_check('ggplot2', libpath='/tmp/R-lib2')
```

In the first case, more of the reverse dependency packages will be successfully installed. The problem is that R gives no indication that these two scenarios give different results.

Edit: Need to do 2x3 experiment:

Variable A:
- `~/.Renviron` doesn't exist
- `~/.Renviron` contains `R_LIBS=/tmp/R-lib`

Variable B:
- `revdep_check('ggplot2')`
- `revdep_check('ggplot2', libpath='/tmp/R-lib')`
- `revdep_check('ggplot2', libpath='/tmp/R-lib2')`

In each condition of AxB, count the number of successul packages. Also see if subsequent runs add more installed packages.

title: package options, devtools.roclets

Since I don't like to have my DESCRIPTION file modified by "collate", I repeatedly have to specify the reduced `roclets` vector manually and unfortunately cannot use `check()` with default `document=TRUE` since this would apply the "collate" roclet (hard-coded default)...

Thinking about package options, I was also wondering how it comes that `devtools` defines its options using `base::options()` and not in an own environment. When I once tried to establish only two package-specific options via `options()`, CRAN maintainers requested that I adopt the `spatstat.options()` model. The concern was that with that many R packages one "cannot assume that all these will continue to interoperate smoothly by relying on loose conventions".
If you will adopt `devtools.options()` at some point (and I think that would be nice regarding the large number of options already available), you could seek inspiration in https://r-forge.r-project.org/scm/viewvc.php/pkg/R/options.R?view=markup&root=surveillance (`reset.surveillance.options()` is called in `.onLoad()`).

title: Permissions of binary files in install_github packages
description:
When calling install_github on a pkg that contains binary files, the call to unzip() does not keep the executable permissions for files in, for example, inst/bin/linux in

https://github.com/colinpmillar/FLa4a/archive/master.zip

utils::unzip uses the internal unzip, which does not seem to keep the permissions. If 

unzip("FLa4a-master.zip", unzip=getOption("unzip"))

is used on the file above in a Linux machine where getOption("unzip") returns

[1] "/usr/bin/unzip"

permissions are kept. So this seems to be an issue upstream with unzip in utils/libs/utils.so, but right now it affects devtools. Could maybe install_github have an **unzip** option?

``` R
# Example code

library(devtools)

## install_github
install.packages(c("copula", "triangle", "np", "latticeExtra"))
install_github("FLa4a", "colinpmillar")

system("ls -l $HOME/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.0/FLa4a/bin/linux/")

> system("ls -l $HOME/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.0/FLa4a/bin/linux/")
total 1772
> -rw-r--r-- 1 imosqueira imosqueira 1813664 Jul  9 14:19 a4a

## R's unzip

system("wget https://github.com/colinpmillar/FLa4a/archive/master.zip")
unzip("master.zip")
system("ls -l FLa4a-master/inst/bin/linux")

> system("ls -l FLa4a-master/inst/bin/linux")
total 1772
> -rw-rw-r-- 1 imosqueira imosqueira 1813664 Jul  9 14:20 a4a

## system's unzip
unzip("master.zip", overwrite=TRUE, unzip=getOption("unzip"))
system("ls -l FLa4a-master/inst/bin/linux")

title: Enable install_github to specify a subdir of github repo to use as package root
description:
Currently, `install_github` assumes the that the repository named in the params served as the root of the R package.

Adding support for a packge that looks like so would be helpful:

```
+ my-uber-project
`- C/
|   + C src files that are the core of my library
`- Python/
|  +- Python language bindings
`- R/
   +- DESCRIPTION
   +- NAMESPACE
   +- R/
   +- src/
    ...
```

Imagine that the `R` subfolder of `my-uber-project` repository is CRAN-stallable binding/part/whatever of `my-uber-project`.

You can imagine calling install_github something like:

```
install_github('my-uber-package', 'lianos', subdir=c('R''))
```

Where `subdir` might support a character vector, eg. c('path', 'to', 'subfolder', 'with', 'R-pkg').

title: Use install_github for private repository with OAuth2
description:
I would like to use `install_github` for continuous integration of private repositories. However I rather not hardcode my github username/password anywhere. Github says:

> _Personal Access Tokens function like ordinary OAuth access tokens. They can be used instead of a password for git over HTTPS, or can be used to authenticate to the API over Basic Authentication._

It seems like it would be relatively easy to add support for support authentication using either a `personal token` or a combination of `client_id` + `client_secret`? Both of these can be generated in [application settings](https://github.com/settings/applications), prevent from having to hardcode a password anywhere, and can easily be revoked when leaked.

title: run_examples() is unaware of /extdata
description:
According to the manual (http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Data-in-packages) package data in a format other than `.rda`, `.txt` or `.csv` should be stored in the folder `inst/extdata`.

During package building, these files are copied from `inst/extdata` to `extdata`.

Therefore, if one includes example code in the documentation to read these files, it could take this form:

`file <- system.file("extdata", "DellSurveyWave2.xlsx", package="tbgSurvey")`

This works in both `R CMD check package` and `devtools::check()`.

However, it fails with `run_examples()` since this file doesn't exist.

- compiling the attributes
- build and load the package

Some context here: https://github.com/RcppCore/attributes/issues/13

title: support for loaded but not attached packages: requests and bugs

Why it is important to me: my use case is to manage several inter-dependent source packages. So when loading a particular package, I will load myself the imports which are source packages using load_all() to be able to eventually load my package.

The problem is that this way all the dependent source packages are attached, which is not similar to the way imports are loaded by library().

I would like to be able to do: load_all(pkg, attach = FALSE). 
Is there a fundamental way that would make it unfeasible ? 

I tried to detach() the package after load_all(), but I got into trouble, because all devtools functions assume the package is attached. 
Examples:

loaded_packages() -> return "attached" packages
ns_env() -> return NULL if the package is loaded but not attached.

title: suggestion: devtools::create() should make some template test files in tests/testthat/
description:
Originally suggested by @sckott in this tweet: https://twitter.com/recology_/status/408695336970899456

Seems like a great idea to me: it would increase the discoverability of the testthat package (and testing in general) and would also imply that testing is an important part of the package that developers need to pay attention to.

title: Be more helpful on Mavericks
description: i.e. if on mavericks, and no `~/.R/makevars` exists, figure out if it should

title: Function to load default values for function parameters
description: When I'm developing functions in a package and there are a lot of parameters in the function, it's nice to be able to load all default parameter values without having to do so manually by executing one at a time. Any interest in a function in devtools that does this in a single function call for a function, many functions, or entire package?  Or, does this already exist?

title: install(dependencies = FALSE) installs dependencies
description: `devtools::install(...., dependencies = FALSE)` installs the package's dependencies via `install-deps`, whether or not dependency installation was requested. The `dependencies` flag appears to actually control whether dependencies _of dependencies_ are installed.

title: load_all error for package with RCs
description:
I've got a package, let's call it `PackageBlob`, that includes some Reference Classes (RCs hereafter). When running `load_all()` for the first time, everything works well (i.e. no warnings, load is successful etc). However, when running `load_all()` the second time (even if I haven't changed the package at all), I get the following warning:

```
load_all()
Loading PackageBlob
Error in FUN(X[[1L]], ...) : 
  (converted from warning) Created a package name, ‘2013-10-16 08:44:09’, when none found
```

I also get this warning in another package using RCs. I don't get any warnings when I run `check()` but do get one note about global bindings related to the use of `.self` and `<<-` in functions declared outside `setRefClass` that are then assigned to the RC in the `methods` argument to `setRefClass`.

I've tried to replicate this warning in a new dummy package where I define a RC and a simple method, but can't. 

Anyone experienced something like this? If not, tempted to bin RC and just use S4.

title: install_* requires user to have pdftex if package has a vignette
description:
This might be something you guys want to think about.  When a person runs `install_github` (and maybe other `install_`*'s), devtools retrieves a copy of the package, and then R builds and installs it on the user's machine.

If the package has an Sweave vignette, R build will try to find a program to compile the vignette and then error out if the user doesn't have one. 

I'm guessing that a lot of R users won't have latex installed and won't be able to figure out the error message, which may make it harder to use `install_github` and github.

Garrett

p.s. Also, I could be completely wrong about this :P

title: If pdflatex is not installed, it is impossible to generate vignettes
devtools should include pkgs in VignetteBuilder as dependencies to download
description:
For example, currently installing `Rcpp` from `GitHub` fails if `highlight` is not available:

``` r
install_github("Rcpp", "RcppCore")
```

gives me

``` r
* creating vignettes ... ERROR
Error in loadVignetteBuilder(vigns$pkgdir) : 
  vignette builder 'highlight' not found
```

Of course, the error is easy enough for the user to fix, but it would be nice if `devtools` could automatically grab the package from CRAN.

title: ChangeLog warning is nonsense
description:
When checking a package in RStudio, devtools is used even though I might prefer `R CMD check --as-cran`.

Worse, devtools appears to be drunk as it warn about 

```
   Non-standard files found:
     ChangeLog
```

A casual check on the CRAN site reveals that ~ 10% of all packages have such a file:

```
 edd@xmcorsairs:~/CRAN$ ls -1 */ChangeLog  | wc -l
 555
 edd@xmcorsairs:~/CRAN$ 
```

title: install_github is too popular; the R community has too much dependence on github
description:
The `install_github` function makes it very easy to use github as an R package repository. It has been so successful that I worry that the R community is now overly dependent on github.  Other people seem to [share my worry](http://bit.ly/1oj7Orv).

This could be mitigated by having equivalent `install_*` functions for other cloud code repositories. Bitbucket is probably the highest priority alternative worth developing for; Google Code is another possibility.
#### Initial thoughts on creating an install_bitbucket function

The basic structure of the code can be more or less copied and pasted from `install_github`:

```
install_bitbucket <- function(repo, username = getOption("bitbucket.user"), ref = "master", some_other_args)
{
  invisible(vapply(repo, install_bitbucket_single, logical(1), some_other_args))
}
```

`ref` can be either a branch name or a tag name.

In terms of what the `some_other_args` might constitute, Bitbucket [supports OAuth identification](https://confluence.atlassian.com/display/JIRA/Allowing+OAuth+Access), so eventually it would be worth adding an `auth_token` argument.

`install_bitbucket_single` can be more or less created by doing `str_replace(body(install_github_single), "github", "bitbucket")`.

For a `bitbucket_get_conn` function, the url is constructed as

```
url <- paste0("https://bitbucket.org/", username, "/", repo, "/get/", ref, ".zip")
```

For an equivalent of `github_parse_path`, punctuation characters are allowed in Bitbucket repository names, but those characters are replaced with a hyphen in the url.    

`github_extract_sha1` works on bitbucket bundles without any modifications.

The API for getting pull requests [isn't finalised](https://confluence.atlassian.com/display/BITBUCKET/Use+the+Bitbucket+REST+APIs), so an equivalent of `github_pull_info` probably isn't worth creating immediately.

`install_url_single` and `install_local_single` seem to work without modification, under my very limited testing.

title: install_github and omegahat?
description:
Hi @hadley ,

I was wondering if `install_github` could check omegahat for dependencies if they are not available on CRAN? If I've understood correctly, CRAN permits packages to depend on other packages available only in omegahat. Alternatively, I wonder if you might introduce convention whereby a package developer can put an install script at a designated location in an R repo on github that could simply be sourced by install_github to handle installing any non-CRAN dependencies (similar to what we do with .travis.yml) first, such that users can still just call install_github. title: Move auto_test_package into devtools
description:
Following a conversation from https://github.com/hadley/testthat/issues/145. When testing packages it would be useful if `testthat::auto_test_package` could apply proper build order to the package source. Currently `testthat::auto_test_package` builds source files in alphabetical order.

Much of the logic for building packages is encapsulated in `devtools::load_all`. Rather than making `devtools` a dependency of `testthat`, @hadley suggested moving `auto_test_package` into `devtools`.

The basic idea is to add a strategy for loading source files to `auto_test` through dependency injection. This will let the default strategy still be `testthat::source_dir`. `auto_test_package` can then define a new strategy based on `load_all` when it calls `auto_test`.

title: install_* requires non-source files under version control
description:
The `install_*` family of functions which install from a repository (`git`, `github`, `gitorious`, `bitbucket` …) require non-source files in that repository in order to work.

In particular, it requires a `NAMESPACE` file in the repository, even though said file is _generated_ from source (`#' @export` directives), and should therefore not be put under version control. The error I’m getting is

```

ERROR: a 'NAMESPACE' file is required
```

As a consequence, I cannot use it to install a GitHub hosted package without putting auto-generated files under version control.

title: Devtools should use Github API to find URLs of file downloads
description: This is useful because Github sometimes changes their download URLs for gists and repo zip files. As things stand now, we have the base URLs hard-coded, so we need to release a new version of devtools every time Github makes changes. If we use their API to find the download URL, we won't need to do this anymore.

title: Resolve install order based on dependency before vapply in install_*
description:
If you try to install package A which depends on package B by `install_*("A","B")`, the installation could fail if A specify a version of B that's not available on CRAN. Instead user should call `install_*("B","A")` instead.

However we could either resolve the dependency ahead to determine the appropriate installation order before calling vapply, or inject the list of to-be-installed packages to `install_deps` function so we call appropriate function instead of `install.packages`.

I'm happy to make an attempt if there's an actual demand for this. Part of me thinks R package dependency list is usually so short that it doesn't worth the trouble.

title: document not working for S4 generics
description:
I have a problem when documenting S4 generics in my package. The `devtools::document` function gives an error when using a S4 generic and it's methods with a `@describeIn` or `@rdname` tag (how I think it is usually done!?).

When I remove the `@describeIn` tag, the `devtools::document(clean = TRUE)` function doesn't raise an error, but of course the methods are not documented. If I add the `@describeIn` tag afterwards, `devtools::document(clean = FALSE)` works just fine.

Running `roxygen2::roxygenize(clean = TRUE)` directly also works with the `@describeIn` tag. 

If I create an empty project with just the file foo.R that contains following code the issue can be reproduced easily (I tried it with R 3.1.0 and 3.0.2 on Mac OS 10.9.2).

``` R
#' A generic method
#'
#' @param a parameter
#' @param b parameter
#' @param c parameter
setGeneric("foo", valueClass = "numeric", function(a, b, c) {
    standardGeneric("foo")
});

#' @describeIn foo
setMethod("foo", signature(a = "numeric", b = "numeric", c = "missing"),
function(a, b, c) {
    a + b;
});

#' @describeIn foo
setMethod("foo", signature(a = "numeric", b = "numeric", c = "integer"),
function(a, b, c) {
    (a + b) * c
});
```

Running `devtools::document(clean = TRUE)` gives following error:

```
Updating foo documentation
Loading foo
Error: Failure in roxygen block beginning foo.R:8
attempt to set an attribute on NULL
```

No .Rd file is generated and every subsequent call to `help` gives the error

```
Error in names(t1) <- rep(names(L), lapply(L, length)) : 
  attempt to set an attribute on NULL
```

title: `install_version` fails if `length(getOption("repos"))>1`
description:
```
options(repos=c(CRAN="http://probability.ca/cran/"))
library(devtools)
packageVersion("devtools")  ## 1.4
install_version("plotrix","3.4")  ## works
options(repos=c(getOption("repos"),"http://r-forge.r-project.org"))
install_version("plotrix","3.4")
## Error in url(sprintf("%s/src/contrib/Meta/archive.rds", repos), "rb") (from install-version.r#30) : 
##   invalid 'description' argument
```

In particular, this is likely to fail on Windows because `getOption("repos")` often includes the CRANextra repository.

Vanilla `install_version()` without a specified version number, or with the most up-to-date version number, works.

It might be slightly tricky to fix this because with multiple repositories you may have to figure out which one had the relevant version of the package available (you can't/shouldn't automatically assume it's the first one).

title: load_all needs be able to export imported objects
description:
When an imported object should be re-exported (without making a copy), `load_all` doesn't do it correctly. For example, ggvis should re-export `%>%`, `filter`, and `group_by`, but when the package is loaded via `load_all`, those functions aren't present:

``` R
load_all('ggvis')

group_by
# Error: object 'group_by' not found
```

When loaded via `library`, it works fine:

``` R
library(ggvis)
group_by
# [prints code]
```

title: DESCRIPTION file from create() shouldn't have Maintainer field
description:
When submitting a package to CRAN, the `Authors@R` field shouldn't contain a Maintainer field, if the Authors@R has `[aut, cre]`.

If both are present, `R CMD check --as-cran`, gives this NOTE:

```
* checking DESCRIPTION meta-information ... NOTE
Maintainer field differs from that derived from Authors@R
  Maintainer: 'First Last <first.last@example.com>'
  Authors@R:  '"First Last <first.last@example.com>'
```

The note doesn't come up when using `check()`, but it does come up when you use `with_envvar(c("_R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_"=TRUE), check())`.

title: RFC: automatically generating version numbers in DESCRIPTION
description:
This is coming from http://stackoverflow.com/questions/24209336/automating-version-increase-of-r-packages. I am not sure it belongs to `devtools`, so tell me what you think. 

I think in general it would be nice to have some control over the version number in developmental builds of R packages. What I am thinking about is having `build` and probably also `install` put/update the version number in `DESCIRPTION`, based on VCS revisions. E.g. for git you can simply do `git-describe --tags` and this will generate a good looking version string for the current revision. It looks like this: `0.7.0-132-gc66bb3a`, which means that the latest version was `0.7.0`, there were `132` commits since, and the last part is the hash of the last commit. (Of course in R you would need to leave out the last part, unfortunately.)

I would start supporting git first, and by adding a `set_version` option to `build` and/or `install`.
