title: Recursive package building fails for certain constellations
description:
I might have overlooked some "clean up" switch in `devtools::build()`, but as far as I can tell, the directory that is automatically created when building a Windows binary causes trouble in subsequent build processes once a binary-build is followed by a source-build.

Here's the walk through:
1. Create an empty package project in RStudio called `devtools.issue`
2. Build the package using the following code:
### Create repositories

```
repos_vec <- file.path(tempdir(), c("repos_1", "repos_2"))
## NOTE
## Suppose that these are two different package repositories following the 
## CRAN directory conventions for contributed packages (e.g. `bin` and `src` 
## subdirectories etc.). For each repository, we'd like to build a `zip` and a 
## `tar.gz` version or package 'devtools.issue'.

## Ensure existence of repository directories //
sapply(repos_vec, dir.create, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```
### Build into first repository

```
devtools::build(binary = TRUE, path = repos_vec[1]) 
## Status: ok
devtools::build(path = repos_vec[1])
## Status: ok
```
### Build into second repository

```
devtools::build(binary = TRUE, path = repos_vec[2])
## Status: error
```

This is the actual error I'm getting and I think it has to do with the fact that the directory `devtools.issue` that has been created when building the first binary is either not removed (should it be?) and/or "messed" up by the build process of the first `tar.gz`:

```
> devtools::build(binary = TRUE, path = repos_vec[2])
"Q:/home/apps/RAPPTO~1/apps/r/R-31~1.1/bin/x64/R" --vanilla CMD INSTALL  \
  "C:\Users\jat\Documents\devtools.issue" --build 

* installing to library 'C:/Users/jat/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpglqaO8'
* installing *source* package 'devtools.issue' ...
Warning in file.copy(f, instdir, TRUE) :
  problem copying .\NAMESPACE to C:\Users\jat\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpglqaO8\devtools.issue\NAMESPACE: No such file or directory
Warning in file(file, ifelse(append, "a", "w")) :
  cannot open file 'C:/Users/jat/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpglqaO8/devtools.issue/DESCRIPTION': No such file or directory
Error in file(file, ifelse(append, "a", "w")) : 
  cannot open the connection
ERROR: installing package DESCRIPTION failed for package 'devtools.issue'
* restoring previous 'C:/Users/jat/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpglqaO8/devtools.issue'
```

I'm guessing that creating the `devtools.issue` directory when building binaries is a must. But shouldn't it be removed afterwards? After all, I did say "build to `path`", so I wouldn't necessarily expect anything to be created **outside** of directory that I specified via `path`.

title: use_rcpp11
description:
This would be useful to have, and would definitely increase the potential exposure to Rcpp11. @romainfrancois, here's the actions that I think it should perform:
1. Add `SystemRequirements: C++11` to the package `DESCRIPTION` file (http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Using-C_002b_002b11-code),
2. Add `PKG_CXXFLAGS=$(PKG_CXXFLAGS) "../inst/include"` to `src/Makevars`, `src/Makevars.win` (or whatever the appropriate invocation is),
3. If possible, use git to clone the `inst/include/` directory of [Rcpp11](https://github.com/Rcpp11/Rcpp11/tree/master/inst/include) into the package's `inst/include` directory,
4. Otherwise, just download the latest Rcpp11 tarball, untar it, and move Rcpp11's `inst/include` into the package's `inst/include` directory.

For people using `git`, if we have a way of checking out a specific branch, e.g. `use_rcpp11(ref = "master")`, that would be great.

The other thing that would be useful for RStudio users -- maybe use `attributes::compileAttributes`, instead of `Rcpp::compileAttributes`, when building a package. Or we can just add back `#define RcppExport extern "C"` so that `Rcpp::compileAttributes` can work with `Rcpp11` projects.

Anything I'm missing?

title: Feature request: optionally treat "Imports" packages as "Depends" packages in `load_all()`
description:
I really came to love your package, awesome work!!

Do you think it'd be possible to implement a feature in `devtools::load_all()` that would optionally treat a package's _imported_ dependencies (as stated in the `Imports` section of `DESCRIPTION`) as if they were "_dependent_" dependencies, i.e. as if they'd been listed in the `Depends` section instead?

The reason I'm asking for this is the following: simply put, using `Imports` instead of `Depends` generally is a good idea for the **finished** package. But while still **developping** a package, you often end up working "inside" of your functions in a "line by line" or "step by step" manner instead of simply calling the finished version. However, for functions that rely on functions of imported packages, this currently implies that you'll have to manually make sure the imported packages are actually attached to the search path via `require()` in order to call them "interactively".

I hope you see the point and if so: thanks for considering this ;-)

title: CRAN rejects FTP uploads
description:
Several times I've submitted a package to CRAN via `devtools::release()` and the package has been successfully submitted via the web form. But twice the package has been uploaded by FTP instead (I think), and devtools has prompted me to send an e-mail to the maintainers. devtools seems to be doing everything in line with the CRAN policies for submission; I certainly wouldn't blame devtools for any mistakes. But a CRAN maintainer gets upset whenever the package is not submitted via the web form and the web form only (despite the policies allowing for an alternative method).

Is there a way of knowing why devtools sometimes uploads via a method other than the submission form, and is there an option to set to disable that method of uploading?

title: Make use_data generate documentation template
description:
I am digging the `use_data` function as it makes adding data to R packages super easy. I was wondering if it made sense to have an option, that would add an roxygen2 documentation template for the dataset. Here is a rough sketch of what the function could look like

``` r
#' Add roxygen2 documentation template for a dataset
#'
#' @param object data set to document
#'
#' @examples
#' document_data(iris)
document_data <- function(object){
  x1 <- "#' ~~ data name/kind ... \n#'"
  x1b <- "#' ~~ A concise (1-5 lines) description of the dataset. ~~\n#'"
  x2 <- "#' \\itemize{"
  x3 <- paste(paste0("#'    \\item ", names(object), "..."), collapse = "\n")
  x4 <- "#'  }\n#'"
  x5 <- "#' @docType data"
  x6 <- "#' @keywords ..."
  x7 <- paste("#' @name", deparse(substitute(object)))
  x8 <- paste0("#' @usage data(", deparse(substitute(object)), ")")
  x9 <- paste("#' @format A data frame with", NROW(object), "rows and",
    NCOL(object), "variables"
  )
  x = paste(c(x1, x1b, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x7, x8, x9), collapse = "\n")
  writeLines(x, con = file.path("R", paste0(deparse(substitute(object)), '.R'))
}
```

If you think this might be a good feature to add, I can contribute a PR.

``` R
showvars <- function(res) {
  pkg <- res$revdep_package
  desc <- packageDescription(pkg)
  rstatus <- if (grepl("devel", R.version$status)) "r-devel" else "r-release"

  pkgversion <- desc$Version
  if (!is.null(desc$GithubSHA1))

    RPKG=%s
    RPKGVERSION="%s"
    CHECKDIR="%s"\n',

}

title: Facilities for creating data files from data-raw
description:
I understand that `data-raw` is just a convention (#541). However, I think `devtools` could assist the user with building the data.

How about providing a function that looks at the scripts in `data-raw` and constructs a `Makefile`? Calls to `use_data` would define the targets, the script is the first dependency, and all strings that contain (or begin with) `data-raw` define additional dependencies. The recipe would be simply `R --vanilla -f @<`. Additional dependencies could be defined in an optional `Makefile.extra` file.

title: host argument for github utilities
description: Currently install_github (and the underlying github_remote) takes host and auth arguments.  This allows one to use it with Github Enterprise instances by specifying `host=ENTERPRISE-ADDRESS/api/v3` and providing an authentication token.  However, other useful utilities such as remote_metadata do not allow this--primarily because github_GET assumes a host of `https://api.github.com/`.  These tools will be useful for, e.g., creating something like `update_github` which compares installed `GithubSHA1` to that currently on the remote.

title: Git integration
description:
Some functions such as `document()`, `use_xxx()`, ... alter the state of the working copy. Such changes could be auto-committed, if and only if the working copy was clean before running those commands. (If the working copy is not clean, a warning would be issued.) I'm currently using different tools to achieve this, and I find this is a big time-saver.

Proposed API change:

`document <- function(..., auto_commit = getOption("devtools.autocommit"))`

Possible values for this option would be `never`, `if_clean`, and `always` (or `FALSE`, `NA` and `TRUE`).

Thoughts?

title: Capture package logs in revdep_check
description:
Similar to this code from rtravis:

``` sh
DumpLogsByExtension() {
    if [[ -z "$1" ]]; then
        echo "dump_logs_by_extension requires exactly one argument, got: $@"
        exit 1
    fi
    extension=$1
    shift
    package=$(find . -maxdepth 1 -name "*.Rcheck" -type d)
    if [[ ${#package[@]} -ne 1 ]]; then
        echo "Could not find package Rcheck directory, skipping log dump."
        exit 0
    fi
    for name in $(find "${package}" -type f -name "*${extension}"); do
        echo ">>> Filename: ${name} <<<"
        cat ${name}
    done
}

DumpLogs() {
    echo "Dumping test execution logs."
    DumpLogsByExtension "out"
    DumpLogsByExtension "log"
    DumpLogsByExtension "fail"
}
```

title: Using install_github() from behind a proxy
description:
I followed [this](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/17783686/solution-how-to-install-github-when-there-is-a-proxy) advice to use `install_github()` from behind a proxy.

However, there is the following problem: if we call `install_github()` with `dependencies = FALSE` then the installation will fail if the packages on which it is dependent have not yet been installed; but if we instead set `dependencies = TRUE` the call will hang as it falls back to `install.packages()` which does not seem to be aware that the proxy has been set via `httr::set_config(httr::use_proxy(...))`

title: Avoid Travis-CI time out from tests
description:
Hi Hadley,

I was wondering if it's possible to add an argument to the `check()` function which would allow a more verbose output for running tests with `testthat`. The reason is that Travis-CI will time out after a few minutes if there is no output being flushed to their console, so to avoid that I've usually just set up the `R CMD check` and `testthat` tests separately with a Makefile so that everything is printed on a continuous basis (e.g., https://travis-ci.org/philchalmers/mirt). In this way I have up to an hour of automated tests that can be run rather than just a few minutes. However, passing something like `check(package, verbose = TRUE)` would be a little more convenient and save from using a Makefile. Thanks for your time.

title: devtools::load_all() may fail when S4 class definitions are in different files
description:
Hi
This is similar to something I tried to raise in #550, but in the previous issue I confused two different aspects of my problem when I try to use the devtools package development sequence, so I am trying again, just concentrating on explaining the aspect that causes devtools to fail for me.

If I create a simple example project and add two files in the R directory as follows
a.r is 

``` r
#' @include b.r
Class2 <- setClass('Class2',contains='Class1')
```

and b.r is 

```
Class1 <- setClass('Class1')
```

then when I try to run load_all() on this package I get the following error messages

```
> library(devtools)
> load_all()
Loading loadallExample
Error in reconcilePropertiesAndPrototype(name, slots, prototype, superClasses,  (from a.r#2) : 
  no definition was found for superclass “Class1” in the specification of class “Class2”
> 
```

The problem arises because although I have the @include directive in my file a.r, it has not yet been processed, so load_all() attempts to read the code from the files in alphabetical order.

I still get an error if I try and run devtools::document('.'), as seen here

```
> document('.')
Updating loadallExample documentation
Loading loadallExample
Error in reconcilePropertiesAndPrototype(name, slots, prototype, superClasses,  (from a.r#2) : 
  no definition was found for superclass “Class1” in the specification of class “Class2”
> 
```

And because of the error while loading, the document('.') does not finish, and does not update the collate entry in the package DESCRIPTION file.

A solution is to run roxygen2::update_collate() before trying to load_all() or document() my package

```
> roxygen2::update_collate('.')
Updating collate directive in  ./DESCRIPTION 
> load_all()
Loading loadallExample
> 
```

The updated collate entry in the DESCRIPTION file created by roxygen2::update_collate tells load_all() (and all the other devtools machinery) the correct order to process the files in.

I can avoid this problem myself now I know what causes it, but as an absolute novice package creator it really confused me for ages. In my real life example the alphabetic order of the file names was not so obvious, and when I tried to pin the error down by commenting out bits of code, it enabled devtools::document to run successfully.  Then when I removed the commenting out, the original code would behave nicely, making the problem appear only intermittently and very frustratingly.  It would be nice if some fix of the type I have illustrated could be included in the official devtools.

Thanks

Geoff

 PS I'm still pretty much a novice package creator (waiting keenly for the book to be finished and published), just a little more informed about this particular problem.

PPS Because roxygen2::update_collate emits a message when it runs, I think simply adding a call to roxygen2::update_collate into the code for load_all may cause some of the testthat tests on devtools to fail (because they are not expecting that particular message to be there)

PPPS I have tried to write a testhat for devtools to check that the collate order is _correct_ and up to date.  The testthat code is

```
test_that("Collate sequence is uptodate, and @includes have been recognised", {
  # Make a temporary clean copy of the test package, in order to
  #   avoid (unwanted here but usually beneficial) side_effects
  #   namely that devtools::load_all may update the collate order in the
  #   DESCRIPTION file
  clean_testCollateOrder <- file.path(tempdir(),'testCollateOrder')
  dir.create(clean_testCollateOrder)
  test_pkg_files <- c('testCollateOrder/DESCRIPTION',
                      'testCollateOrder/NAMESPACE',
                      'testCollateOrder/R')
  file.copy(test_pkg_files,clean_testCollateOrder,recursive=TRUE)

  expect_message(load_all(clean_testCollateOrder), "Loading testCollateOrder")

  expect_equal(a, 1) #even though b.r set it to 2

  unload(clean_testCollateOrder)
  unlink(clean_testCollateOrder,recursive=TRUE)
})  
```

It requires a template project (which I have called testCollateOrder) with a plain vanilla DESCRIPTION file

```
Package: testCollateOrder
Title: Confirm that the collate order is uptodate
Version: 0.1
Authors@R: "Geoff Lee<geoff.lee99@bigpond.com> [aut, cre]"
Description: load_all fails with an error when S4 classes with inheritance
  are read in the wrong order.  This package checks that all @includes
  have been recognised and processed by roxygen2,
  so that the collate order in the DESCRIPTION file is uptodate
Depends: R (>= 3.1.1)
License: What license is it under?
LazyData: true
```

The key feature is that there is no collate entry in the file yet.

The two files in the R directory are 
a.r

```
#' @include b.r
a <- 1
```

and b.r

```
a <- 2
```

The test will succeed if the @include directive has been recognised so that a.r is read after b.r

title: load_all should not touch the DESCRIPTION file with roxygen2::update_collate
description:
Hi,

the recent change in `load_all` using `update_collate`  (PR #649) has a deep impact when loading the package on parallel jobs, has it simply creates a massively invalid `DESCRIPTION` file, with each job writing bits of the file in random places.

More generally, I think `load_all` should not touch any of the package files: it is meant to load the package as is, and by all means should honor what the user wrote in the DESCRIPTION file, even if it is incorrect.

If collate order must be updated, the user can call `collate_update`, and may be suggested to do so if a computed collate order is not as in the original file.

I would really stick to the rule: `load_all` emulates what library does, i.e., **read/load** package files without trying to fix things, roxygen2 helps **writing/generating** package files.

Thank you.

title: Working directory when preparing package for testing in test()
description:
When testing a package using `devtools::test()`, the current working directory for executing the _package's_ code ("installing" the package into a temporary environment) seems to be the `R` subdirectory of the package, whereas it's the package's root directory when using `devtools::check()`.

Test package: https://github.com/krlmlr/test.getwd

Output with `devtools::test()` (copied from RStudio's console):

```
In package: /home/muelleki/git/R/test.getwd/R
```

Output with `devtools::check()`: https://github.com/krlmlr/test.getwd/blob/master/test.getwd.Rcheck/00install.out#L4

Is this by design? Otherwise I'd like to take a look at this, so that the CWD is always the package's root.

title: Mysterious "Error: Command failed (1)"
description:
UPDATE, TL/DR: it would be nice to let the caller of `test()` choose between `load_all(pkg, quiet = TRUE))` or `load_all(pkg, quiet = FALSE))`.  Currently it's hard-coded to `quiet=TRUE`, which can make it hard to see what the problem is.

(Migrated from https://github.com/hadley/testthat/issues/199.)

Sometimes when I try to test a package in RStudio, I get the following response:

```
> test()
Testing AMGUtils
Error: Command failed (1)
```

I can get a stack trace like so:

```

8: force(code)

       ...))

5: RCMD("INSTALL", c(shQuote(pkg$path), paste("--library=", shQuote(dest), 
       sep = ""), no_args, "--no-multiarch", "--no-test-load", args), 
       quiet = quiet)
4: install_min(pkg, tempdir(), components = "libs", args = if (needs_clean(pkg)) "--preclean", 
       quiet = quiet)
3: compile_dll(pkg, quiet = quiet)
2: load_all(pkg, quiet = TRUE)
1: test()
```

I stepped through using the debugger, and in the `system_check()` call I see this:

```
Browse[2]> full
[1] "'/opt/R-3.1.1/lib64/R/bin/R' --vanilla CMD INSTALL '/home/kwilliams/git/AMGUtils' --library='/tmp/RtmpZdCcCw' --no-R --no-data --no-help --no-demo --no-inst --no-docs --no-exec --no-multiarch --no-test-load"
Browse[2]>

} else {

attr(,"status")
[1] 1

If I go look in the temp directory `/tmp/RtmpZdCcCw`, I only see a couple of `.rds` files, none of the package files.  If I try the INSTALL command manually in that directory, I get some errors about Rcpp:

```

Looks like it's picking up stuff in an old `~/R/library` directory.  So I moved that out of the way, tried again, and got this error again:

```

Testing AMGUtils
Error: Command failed (1)
```

Back in the shell, I see this:

title: install_git not working with ssh addresses copied from Github on Windows.
description:
I finally figured out why install_git hangs on Windows machines.

If I use

```
library(devtools)
install_github("hadley/memoise")
```

it works fine both on Windows and  Unix.

If I use

```
install_git("git@github.com:hadley/memoise.git")
```

it works fine on my Linux installations (Debian, Ubuntu and Arch), but it doesn't work on
Windows.

However if I modify slightly the address to be:

```
install_git("git://github.com/hadley/memoise.git")
```

it works just fine on both platforms.

For sharing code with people that are not used to git, I think this add an extra layer of difficulty,
and I guess it would be great to have a consistent behaviour on both platforms.

Cheers,
Luca

title: Query which versions R-release and R-oldrel refer to
description:
Code to do it:

``` r

library(magrittr)
library(RCurl)
library(XML)

## Get the tag info from SVN
xtags <- getURLContent(
  "http://svn.r-project.org/R/tags/",
  customrequest = "PROPFIND",
  httpheader=c("Depth"="1")
) %>%
  xmlParse() %>%
  xmlRoot() %>%      
  xmlChildren()

## Split a version number to major, minor, patch
split_versions <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    sub(pattern = "^([0-9]+-[0-9]+)$", replacement = "\\1-0") %>%
    strsplit(split = "-") %>%
    sapply(as.numeric)
}

## Sort version numbers
sort_tags <- function(x) {
  x_order <- x %>%
    split_versions() %>%
    apply(1, list) %>%
    lapply("[[", 1) %>%
    do.call(what = order)
  x [x_order]
}

## Extract versions numbers from XML and sort them
versions <- xtags %>%
  lapply(xpathApply, "*[local-name()='href']") %>%
  sapply("[[", 1) %>%
  sapply(xmlValue) %>%
  unname() %>%
  sub(pattern = "/R/tags/R-([^/]+)/", replacement = "\\1") %>%
  grep(pattern = "^[0-9]+-[0-9]+(-[0-9]+|)$", value = TRUE) %>%
  sort_tags()

## Relase is easy, most recent
release <- tail(versions, 1)

## Oldrel is latest from the previous minor
## (Careful with factors, they are ordered by default!)
oldrel <- versions %>%
  sub(pattern = "-[0-9]+$", replacement = "") %>%
  factor(levels = unique(.)) %>%
  tapply(X = versions, FUN = tail, 1) %>%
  tail(2) %>%
  head(1) %>%
  unname()
```

title: Update packages directly from github/bitbucket etc
description:
Rather than going through CRAN, it would be nice to be able to update packages that are available on public / private repos (with the usual authentication). 

Functionally this could mean writing a new function (say `update_packages()`) that is a wrapper for `update.packages()` plus another function that checks whether there are any newer commits on master branches of repos from which packages have previously been installed.

Okay, I created my package using devtools.

When I run devtools::check(), everything passes okay.

But, because I wanted to make sure that the generic R install approach would work, I ran  `R CMD check .`   My understanding was that it would test the package in the current directory, but it fails right away:

title: install_version issues with DCF/continuation lines
description:
Running R 3.1.2 on OS X 10.10.1. 

I've observed that on some packages, but not all, `install_version` gives me an error about continuation lines. An example that I ran into: 
- `install_version('RcppEigen', '0.3.2.1.2')` gives me an error `Error: Found continuation line starting '   The RcppEigen pac ...' at begin of record.`
- `install_version('BH', '1.54.0-2')` is no problem

It seems like an issue with `read.dcf` and continuation lines in DESCRIPTION that contain only a period, to indicate a blank line. The above version of RcppEigen happens to have two of these lines in DESCRIPTION, but BH does not. 

I debugged `read.dcf`. It's called 3 times during `install_version`, twice to an identical file in `/var/folders/...` that looks like a temp directory, and once to a nearly identical path but in `/private/var/folders/...` Weirdly, the version in `/private/var/folders/...` seems to have had the period lines replaced with total blank lines, and `.Internal(readDCF(...))` fails, presumably because it reads the next line as a start-of-record line. 

I can download and install the old version of RcppEigen with `R CMD INSTALL` just fine.

title: Why does devtools:::R use --vanilla?
description:
In another ticket I just opened (https://github.com/hadley/testthat/issues/199), I poked around in `devtools:::R()` version 1.6.1 and noticed that it calls R with the `--vanilla` flag.  This means it's not loading the site-wide Renviron, which is where we set our local `R_LIBS_USER` variable:

```
% cat /opt/R-3.1.1/lib64/R/etc/Renviron.site
R_LIBS_USER=/opt/R3.1-lib:~/R/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-library/3.1
```

title: Optionally roxygenize (or execute custom R code) before build
description:
As requested in https://github.com/hadley/devtools/issues/43#issuecomment-30662304.

In order to avoid having to manage `.Rd` files at GitHub, at lest the `install_github()` routine (probably also `build()`) should support roxygenization before build. Execution of custom R code is a plus, but not necessary for this feature.

To start, I'd suggest supporting a field `Devtools: list(document = TRUE)` in `DESCRIPTION`. During `build` this field is examined, and `devtools::document('.')` is executed after unpacking but before the call to `R CMD build`. As `devtools` already suggests `roxygen2`, no immediate action in terms of dependency management is needed.

Build-time dependencies could be supported by a new field `BuildDepends:` in `DESCRIPTION`, with the same syntax as `Depends:`. For the given use case this is probably overkill, but it could be useful for specifying generic pre-build code by e.g. `Devtools: list(pre_build = Rd2roxygen::rab('.'))`.

The `document` parameter to `check` could be made obsolete.

title: New argument create_if_missing to load_all
description:
If `load_all()` doesn't find a `DESCRIPTION` file in the package directory, it is created. As of #803, parent directories will not be scanned for a `DESCRIPTION` file. #816 explicitly documents and tests this behavior.

Now the behavior of `load_all()` is difficult to understand and communicate: If a directory happens to contain `R`, `src` or `data`, a `DESCRIPTION` is created -- if not (and no `DESCRIPTION` exists), an error is thrown:

``` r
> pkg <- tempfile(); dir.create(pkg); devtools::load_all(pkg)
Error: '/tmp/RtmpqMuf1p/file498b5f0c4c48' does not look like a package: no R/, src/ or data directories
No traceback available 
> pkg <- tempfile(); dir.create(pkg); dir.create(file.path(pkg, "R")); devtools::load_all(pkg)
No DESCRIPTION found. Creating with values:
```

I suggest a new argument `create_if_missing` that governs this behavior. If `TRUE`, always create (perhaps via `devtools::setup()`). If `FALSE`, never create (but use the usual `pkg <- as.package(pkg)` idiom). If `NULL` (the default), the user will be asked if in interactive mode (otherwise same as `FALSE`). 

@hadley: Is this sufficient for the use case you described in  [your comment](https://github.com/hadley/devtools/pull/816/files#r32617415)?

title: release() assumes package root is git repository root
description:
Current checks using `git2r` ensure that a package that is in a git repository doesn't have uncommitted changes and that the checkout is clean.  However, the checks in git.R in `git_uncommited()` and similar functions assume that the package is rooted in the top-level repository directory.  For packages that are in a subdirectory contained within a larger git repository, the call to `r <- git2r::repository(path)` returns an error that the directory is not a valid repository:

```
Error in validObject(.Object) : 
  invalid class “git_repository” object: Invalid repository
```

It seems to me that devtools should not require that the package root directory be the same as the git repository root directory. This is easily fixed by adding `discover=T` to the repository check in functions like `git_uncommitted()`, like this:

``` r
 r <- git2r::repository(path, discover=T)
```

Does this seem reasonable? I will add a pull request shortly.

title: Use system2 instead of system in system_check
description:
So, it looks `devtools::system_check()` originally used `system()` then switched to `system2()`, then switched back (here: https://github.com/hadley/devtools/commit/e11e949b1d92a9f097aaaf4318330d477b978708). Is there logic to this?

The reason I ask is [a StackOverflow question](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/31251544/how-can-i-send-the-output-of-r-cmd-check-to-a-file-or-variable) that came up today about redirecting the output of `check()` to a file. It doesn't seem like this is possible for two reasons:
1. `check_r_cmd()` has a `...` that is passed to `system()` via `R()`, but that `...` is not accessible from `check()`. The `...` in `check()` goes to provide access to the `manual`, `vignette`, and `binary` arguments to `build()`, while there is no `check_args` (or similar) argument to pass arguments to `check_r_cmd`.
2. The use of `system` means there's no way to redirect output, whereas there would be under `system2` (see my answer on SO).

That's two issues, but they're related. I would propose switching `system()` back to `system2()` and then either (1) adding an generic list-like argument to `check()` to pass arguments to `system()` or (2) explicitly exposing an output redirection option through the whole stack of check-related functions.

title: install_github syntax for github enterprise with organizations
description:
The institution where I work has a github enterprise installation with a number of sub-organizations set up. The R packages that we create and need to load live at URLs such as

https://github.myEnterprise.org/myOrganization/myPackage.git

I have tried a wide number of variants on the `install_github()` syntax but have been unable to figure out how to provide the organization name and my username for authentication. The `install_github()` help files indicate that username is deprecated and to provide that prior to the first slash in repo. (I'm using a token declared as GITHUB_PAT in .Renviron). I tried these:

```
install_github("myOrganization/myPackage.git", host="github.myEnterprise.org")
install_github("username/myPackage.git", host="github.myEnterprise.org/myOrganization")
install_github("username/myPackage.git", host="github.myEnterprise.org")
install_github("username/myOrganization/myPackage.git", host="github.myEnterprise.org")
install_github("username/myOrganization.git", host="github.myEnterprise.org")
```

In each case, I get these messages:

```
Using github PAT from envvar GITHUB_PAT
Downloading github repo _varies according to repo definition_
Error: Command failed (9)
In addition: Warning message:
Github repo contains submodules, may not function as expected! 
```

The github repo does not contain submodules. Here's the `traceback()`:

```
9: stop("Command failed (", status, ")", call. = FALSE)

Any ideas what I may be doing wrong?

description:
The `with_*` functions are useful outside of a package development context, so they should be split into their own small package.

One particular benefit is that if you have a package with `testthat` tests and translated messages, you want to run the tests with language fixed to (probably) US English.  So the `testthat.R` file now contains:

``` r
library(testthat)
library(devtools)
library(yourpackage)

with_envvar(
  c(LANG = "en_US"),
  test_check("yourpackage")
)
```

It feels a little cumbersome to have `devtools` as a suggested package just for this, but a smaller `withr` (?) package would be fine.

title: Incompatibility with shinyjs when loading a package containing definition of a reference class
description:
I have a simple Shiny app, using the latest version of R (3.2.2), RStudio (0.99.473), all packages up-to-date, tested in both Windows 7 and Ubuntu 14.04. The same thing happens in both SOs.

I created a small package with a properly created `DESCRIPTION` file called `RTEMP`. I use devtools to load this package. So, the first lines of code in the very simple Shiny app are

`library("devtools")`
`load_all("../../RTEMP");`

The folder structure where `RTEMP` is doesn't matter

This temporary package has one single file inside `RTEMP/R/`, `something.r`. This file contains one line of code:

`AA <- setRefClass("AA");`

It is creating a reference class with nothing but a name. Nothing else is done with this package in the Shiny app, it is only loaded and nothing more.

When running the Shiny app for the first time after opening RStudio, the app loads perfectly. If I close the app and open it again, I get the following error message:

`ERROR: shinyjs: you cannot mix named and unnamed arguments in the same function call`

The problem happens the second time the package is loaded.

If, instead, I define the `refClass` inside the app itself:

`#library("devtools")`
`#load_all("../../RTEMP");`
`AA <- setRefClass("AA");`

... everything works fine.

I wonder if devtools fails to properly unload the `refClass` before loading the package for the second time?

title: install_github() fails to install non-CRAN deps
description:
I have a package in Github that has a Bioconductor package (BiocCheck) in its Suggests field. I thought if I passed the bioconductor repos as the `repos` argument that I could install my package and the Bioconductor dependency in one go, but it doesn't work:

``` r
# in R-3.2.1
library(devtools)
install_github("dtenenba/anRpackage", build_vignettes=TRUE, 
  repos="http://bioconductor.org/packages/3.2/bioc", 
  dependencies=TRUE, type="source")
```

The output says `Skipping 1 packages not available: BiocCheck`. The package fails to build (and install) because its vignette requires that BiocCheck be present and is set to fail on error. The repos argument is supposed to be passed to `install.packages()` which is never called (I know this because I set `debug(install.packages)`). So something else is deciding that BiocCheck is not available, and that something else is not using the repos argument that I passed in.

title: Skipping package dependencies because of type mismatch.
description:
The problem is described and demonstrated [here](https://github.com/vladpetyuk/toypack)
It turned out that `devtools::package_deps` is forcing type to be "binary".

``` r
    if (identical(type, "both")) {

    }
```

However, some of the packages (e.g. `GO.db`) are not maintained as binary on Bioconductor.
Thus, the installation skips them.

title: `release()` checks for 'r_github_packages' in .travis.yml
description:
Would it be helpful if `release()` checks that the Travis (or AppVeyor or Wercker) builds are _not_ using a package version from GitHub?

I haven't run into this trouble (yet) but I could see it happening.  The builds could work perfectly on the local machine and Travis (which have the pre-release version of a package), but not on the CRAN farm (which is uses the old/release version of a package).

The rough steps for the new `release()` step would be:
- Search for .travis.yml (and appveyor.yml & wercker.yml) yaml files. 
- If found, determine if the `r_github_packages` section is populated. 
- If populated, list the packages, and then ask the user if that's intentional (in a no/yup/nope format).

If this feature sounds helpful, I'm happy to start coding it.

title: absence of hooks directory is not definitive test for git repo
description:
I confess: I created a git repo using [sourcetree](https://www.sourcetreeapp.com) instead of `git init` or RStudio. Apparently this can lead to a repo in which the `.git` directory does not contains a `hooks` subdirectory. Even after you've made a commit. So when I attempt to use `devtools::use_readme_rmd()`, I hit [this code](https://github.com/hadley/devtools/blob/0b122b24cead594b86d237eb6965205c8fd27c64/R/infrastructure-git.R#L81-L84) in `use_git_hook()` and get `Error: This project doesn't use git`. Apparently there are [other](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-ce/issues/1327) [ways](https://github.com/sprintly/Sprintly-GitHub/issues/17) to have a valid git repo and yet NOT have a `hooks` subdirectory.

I admit this maybe a rare phenomenon. Not sure if a different error message is the way to go or just outright creation of `hooks`.

title: Support for language string translation
description:
Internationalisation (I18n) is often left as an afterthought to software, added on once the "real code" is working, and only if there's some demand for it. If the mechanisms for I18n are included at the start, then it is easier to include translation string code as the package is developed.

I would propose a `use_translations(pkg)` function (or similar) that sets up the directories for string translation, and adds an example or two. It could also set up a string translation function for the domain of the package, perhaps `T`(because `_` - the conventional name in other languages -  needs quoting), although there's still T for TRUE lurking (but shouldn't ever get confused with a T function). T would not need to be exported.

I'm not sure what packages currently use I18n apart from Rcmdr if you need to find examplars of current practice.

title: Starting package version should be 0.0.0.9000
Package description must be title case
description:
Package `Title` field in `DESCRIPTION` file must be title case, and while CRAN checks this, devtools does not. E.g. "This is Title Case" passes CRAN, but "This is not title case" does not (at least, doesn't pass Uwe Ligges).

Not sure if this is devtools's responsibility, or that of R CMD check, but wanted to note it.

title: flagging links
description:
Dear All,

One of the things that CRAN does is check whether all the links can be followed. And as far as I can tell from the documentation and from using devtools, devtools doesn't currently check that. There are two aspects to the problem:
1. https links always raise errors, afaik
2. CRAN also catches stuff where header request is not honored.

For instance, Kurt Hornik noted: 
"curl http://www.freebase.com/ works fine"
but curl -I -L http://www.freebase.com/ doesn't

And the latter is what is used by CRAN.

title: Export and document check_dir
description:
Short version: 
Can you export `devtools:::check_dir` and rename it to `devtools::package_root`, and give it a default parameter of ".".

Long version:

Been using devtools at work to develop analysis packages.  One common thing I do is put extra scripts in what is a package directory.  These scripts usually need some awareness of their relative location to package root, but it occurred to me that `devtools::load_all()` has an ability to find package root no matter what the working directory is as long as it is a sub-directory of the package.  I inspected the source and noted it all came down to devtools::check_dir("."), and I thought this is wonderful...

Shouldn't _everything_ we code use that as a root directory?  This way a source file never needs to know where it is relative to the root of a package.  For example  I was modifying a colleagues data structure and wanted to save it in package_root/data.  A way to do that in devtools is:

```
save(tcga_ovarian_pepdata_bp, file = file.path(devtools:::check_dir("."), "data","ModifiedOvarianPepdataBP.Rdata"))
```

Now no matter where this script ends up in any sub-directory of the package the object will _always_ be saved in package_root/data.  I can put this save two nested directories deep and the script doesn't need to know. That is cool! But, it isn't exported and has a cryptic name.

title: Shared library is not reloaded instead of a compile error
description:
Hi Everyone,

Stumbled upon a weird issue that took a couple of hours of restarting R and loading packages to pinpoint. I've finally found what's causing this, but I'm confounded as to why, on two fronts. Not sure if this belongs in Rcpp forum, please let me know if I should repost there.

First a brief description of the problem: assigning an integer to an element of Rcpp::CharacterVector doesn't produce a compile time error. This is an issue number one. It's an issue with Rcpp, not devtools, and I can study the code and understand how it's allowed, although probably not why. The second issue is that doing so makes R not reload the shared library of my package when I re-install it using load_all(). This is the real puzzle to me.

Now to reproduce the problem. I'm running 64bit Ubuntu Linux Trusty 14.04 with 3.13.0-61-generic kernel. Start a new R session and do:

``` R
> library(devtools)
> library(Rcpp)
> session_info()
Session info -------------------------------------------------------------------
 setting  value                       
 version  R version 3.2.2 (2015-08-14)
 system   x86_64, linux-gnu           
 ui       X11                         
 language (EN)                        
 collate  en_US.UTF-8                 
 tz       <NA>                        
 date     2015-09-18                  

Packages -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 package    * version date       source        
 devtools   * 1.9.1   2015-09-11 CRAN (R 3.2.2)
 digest       0.6.8   2014-12-31 CRAN (R 3.2.2)
 memoise      0.2.1   2014-04-22 CRAN (R 3.2.2)
 Rcpp       * 0.12.1  2015-09-10 CRAN (R 3.2.2)
 rstudioapi   0.3.1   2015-04-07 CRAN (R 3.2.2)

> create("testpkg",rstudio=F)
```

This is my DESCRIPTION file:

```
Package: testpkg
Title: What the Package Does (one line, title case)
Version: 0.0.0.9000
Authors@R: person("First", "Last", email = "first.last@example.com", role = c("aut", "cre"))
Description: What the package does (one paragraph).
Depends: R (>= 3.2.2)
License: What license is it under?
LazyData: true
Imports: Rcpp
LinkingTo: Rcpp
```

This is my NAMESPACE file:

```
exportPattern("^[^\\.]")
useDynLib(testpkg)
importFrom(Rcpp, sourceCpp)
```

And this is my C++ code in testpkg/src/test.cpp:

``` C++
#include <Rcpp.h>
using namespace Rcpp;

// [[Rcpp::export]]
CharacterVector tptest() {
  return wrap("foo");
}

RObject some_test() {
  CharacterVector c(1);
  c[0] = 1;
  return c;
}
```

After this setup in R session load the package the first time:

``` R
> load_all("testpkg", quiet=T)
> tptest()
[1] "foo"
```

I then modify the function tptest() in test.cpp to return string "bar" and reload in R:

``` R
> load_all("testpkg", quiet=T)
> tptest()
[1] "foo"
```

The string didn't change, it's still "foo". It looks like the shared library is not reloaded. Any changes in test.cpp after this point will not be visible after the package is reloaded with load_all(). I've tried adding functions, removing them (after which I can still use .Call to call them), changing arguments... nothing works. R session now needs to be restarted and the package loaded anew for the changes to take effect.

If however the code `c[0] = 1;`, which is incorrect and should not even have compiled, is replaced with `c[0] = "aaa";` everything works. I can reload the package with load_all() and see my changes reflected right away. (Notice that the R session has to be restarted for the correct code to take effect.)

So my question is:
1. This is for Rcpp forum: how come the C++ code `c[0] = 1;` above compiles? If someone happens to know here for a reason, please point me in the right direction.
2. How come after inclusion of this incorrect code the shared library of a package is not reloaded with load_all()? I think this question belongs in this forum, but please tell me if I should post this to Rcpp.

Thanks.

title: Inconsistency in R version dependency
description:
Hi Hadley and Jim,

There is an inconsistency in the R version dependency:
- `devtools` requires  R (>= 3.0.2).
- However, `devtools` imports `withr` and `withr` requires R (>= 3.2.0).

So when one tries to install `devtools` in r-oldrel, it currently fails. 

See the CRAN tests: https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_results_devtools.html

Also, this configuration causes problem with Gabor's r-builder in Travis, when testing in r-oldrel. See this example (https://travis-ci.org/renkun-ken/formattable/jobs/103427303).

I think the way to go here would be to relax `withr` dependency, at least to r-oldrel. But if `withr` dependency can't be relaxed, maybe `devtools` dependency should be set to R (>= 3.2.0).

d <- tempdir()

    quiet=TRUE,
    check_dir = d
    )

check.dir <- file.path(
    d,

```

title: devtools::test when package Depends on data.table, but does not import it
description:
When a package Depends on data.table (and does not import it), sometimes using devtools::test on the package can break some functions that use data.table.  I filed a bug report for data.table, but it's not clear that is a data.table issue.  Here is the link to the data.table bug report: https://r-forge.r-project.org/tracker/?func=detail&atid=975&aid=2367&group_id=240

I don't see a way to attach files to this, but here is a link (that should be a direct download) to the package that I attached to the data.table bug report: https://r-forge.r-project.org/tracker/download.php/240/975/2367/275/anRpackage_1.0.tar.gz

The package has 2 functions: myFun assigns some values to a column of a data.table by reference.  myFun2() creates a data.table, and then calls myFun() to change the values of one of the columns of the data.table myFun2() created.

The package also has a testthat test that simply tests that myFun2 returns a data.table.

The package passes R CMD check, and test_dir.  However, if I use devtools::test, I get an error, and for the remainder of the R session, myFun() and myFun2() will fail with the same error.

Here is a link to the output from an interactive session (attached to the data.table bug report) showing the problem: https://r-forge.r-project.org/tracker/download.php/240/975/2367/276/interactive.txt

title: Honour _R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_ in install_deps
description:
I see mention of `_R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_` in #625 and #181 but I think this is a new use case: I want `install_deps` to (perhaps optionally, but by default) honour this environment variable. Right now, in Travis builds, `_R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_` is ignored, and Travis builds fails because unavailable suggested packages are attempted to be installed, and there is not a check for whether _all_ the dependencies were installed successfully.

This is probably an Travis R script bug, too, but I wonder what you think about `devtools` respecting arcane R environment variables.

title: Discrepancy between build_vignettes and document(roclets="vignettes")
description:
If I call `build_vignettes()`, the built vignette files get placed into inst/doc/.

If I call `document(roclets="vignette")`, the built vignette files stay in vignettes/.

There is a discrepancy here. It arises most because in current versions of Rstudio, the only way I can find to build vignettes from the interface (without running a full check or build) is to run Document, with the option for vignette selected (which adds `vignette` to the list of `roclets` in `document`).

Shouldn't `build_vignettes()` and `document(roclets="vignette")` function identically?

title: Add in `build_vignettes(, upgrade = FALSE)` argument
description:
When I run `build_vignettes()` in my package, the function tries to install some packages. But all the mentioned packages I already have, in the same path, but not in the most recent version.

``` r
> build_vignettes()
Installing 3 packages: evaluate, formatR, knitr
Installing packages into ‘/usr/local/lib/R/site-library’
(as ‘lib’ is unspecified)
Warning in utils::install.packages(pkgs, repos = repos, type = type, ...,  :
  'lib = "/usr/local/lib/R/site-library"' is not writable
Would you like to use a personal library instead?  (y/n)

> ip <- installed.packages()
> ip[rownames(ip) %in% c("evaluate", "formatR", "knitr"), 1:2]
         Package    LibPath                  
evaluate "evaluate" "/usr/lib/R/site-library"
formatR  "formatR"  "/usr/lib/R/site-library"
knitr    "knitr"    "/usr/lib/R/site-library"
```

The argument `dependencies = "VignetteBuilder` argument is passed down, `build_vignette() > install_deps() > dev_package_deps()`, the last check for updates.

```
> pkg <- dev_package_deps(pkg, repos = repos, dependencies = dependencies, type = type)
Needs update -----------------------------
 package  installed available
 evaluate 0.8       0.8.3    
 formatR  1.2.1     1.3      
 knitr    1.12      1.12.3   
```

New versions are always installed. But, why not add a argument in `build_vignettes()` to update or not packages, `upgrade = FALSE`, that is passed to `update()` inside `install_deps()`? With this, only non installed packages will be installed, but not those already installed.

Thanks in advance.

title: Let users choose default options for load_all
description:
I usually prefer to use `devtools::load_all(export_all=FALSE)`, especially if I'm doing package maintenance rather than new development. But as soon as I run `devtools::test()`, I get all my unexported internal functions dumped into the search path.

What if we replaced, e.g.

export_all = getOption("devtools.export_all", TRUE)

Then users could set their own defaults in their `.Rprofile`. These defaults would then apply even when `load_all()` is called from e.g. `test()`.

title: add host argument to use_github()?
description:
Hi,

The use-case for this is for people who use enterprise GitHub.

I have looked at the code, and I think this can be done, but it would involve (I think) also adding a host argument to:
- `github_GET()`
- `github_POST()`
- `use_github_links()`

The change to `use_github_links()` could be a bit hairy as it might have to map `api.github.com` to `https://github.com` and `github.foo.com/api/v3` to `https://github.foo.com`. 

I am happy to do a PR on this, if you think it is worthwhile to go forward. If so, a couple quick questions:
1. Are there other functions I would need to touch?
2. I also see a problem in testing the code, as it would require a public enterprise version of github to test against. Would it be enough to do private, informal testing, and also (of course) ensure that any changes do not break the existing behavior?

Overall, the "issue" is that in utils https://github.com/hadley/devtools/blob/master/R/utils.r#L155:

``` r
is_bioconductor <- function(x) {
  x$package != "BiocInstaller" && !is.null(x$biocviews)
}
```

Implies that if biocViews exists and the package is not `BiocInstaller`, then the package is assumed bioconductor package.  This is probably a good assumption or one of the only ways to distinguish the CRAN/bioC package distinction.  Thus, though not an `Imports` or `Suggests`, `BiocInstaller` seems to be a hidden/implicit dependency when installing using `devtools`.  This affects Travis builds.  

This may not be an "issue" exactly, and I may just add an install of `BiocInstaller` to the Travis to make it work, but figured I'd bring up the point here.

title: FR: Get rid of C code
description:
This would allow building/upgrading devtools on Windows without Rtools and perhaps without `build_github_devtools()`.

It's only the `nsreg()` function which is called by `ns_registry()`; to me it looks like it does the same as `.Internal(getNamespaceRegistry())`. Getting the latter past the CRAN checks is possible with some eval-bquote trickery. This is a CRAN-able version of `.Internal()`:

``` r
internal <- function(code) {
  Internal <- as.name(".Internal")
  code_sub <- substitute(code)

  eval(bquote(
    .(Internal)(.(code_sub))))
}
```

Putting `ns_registry()` into a separate package is also an option.

title: Installation with dependencies should first download, then install
description:
I think installation of packages + dependencies should be split in three stages:
1. Download all source packages, including their dependencies
2. Install them in the correct order
3. Apply devtools-specific post-installation steps

For 2., we can leverage `install.packages()` with a `repos` argument that points to a local path: All we need to do is to download the packages to some `contrib/src/` subdirectory and call `tools::write_PACKAGES()`. This would finally give us parallel installation with `options(Ncpus > 1)`.

It looks like this would be relatively easy to implement with the current codebase. @gaborcsardi: Do you have any plans for a separate "installer" package?

Motivation: `devtools` does _a lot_ when installing packages and their dependencies, especially if these packages are from different remotes (e.g., CRAN + Bioconductor + GitHub). When revdep-checking RSQLite (with `bioconductor = TRUE`), I observed twice that I need 2-3 passes to install all revdeps. (The process is single-threaded and takes a day, I'm not too keen to repeat it _again_.)

title: idea: github pages - using /docs folder in master branch
description:
GitHub made some changes recently to how they deal with GitHub pages - one of the new options is that pages can be served from a `/docs` folder in the master branch. I'm sure you saw the news - [here's the link](https://help.github.com/articles/configuring-a-publishing-source-for-github-pages/).

As you know, `/docs` is a non-standard top-level directory for an R package - it generates a note during `devtools::check()`.

On the other hand, it keeps public documentation closer to the source.

I guess my questions are:
1. Is there a reason you should not use `/docs` as a place to keep gh-pages for a package? In other words, is this a bad idea to begin with?
2. Assuming that you use `/docs` for gh-pages and that you want to avoid the note from being generated, could it be possible/advisable to modify `devtools::release()` to avoid including that directory from being sent to CRAN?

title: DESCRIPTION: space at the end of fields that start with \n
description:
This came up here: https://github.com/metacran/description/issues/14

It seems that in theory R requires a space after the colon for each key in DESCRIPTION, even if the value start with a newline. (The space is not part of the value, a newline immediately after the colon, is.)

Currently `devtools` does not add a space there, in fact if there was a space there originally, it removes it (this is only true for the most recent version AFAIR).

Handling this is somewhat tricky, because the space is not part of the value, so after we read in the file, we have no idea if there was a space there or not. Unless we store this as meta-information.

I am not sure what to do with this, and I don't think it is very important (`read.dcf` reads the file without the space), but it would be nice to handle it the same way. 

`description` currently adds a space there, even if it wasn't there originally, simply because it does not store meta-information, only the keys and the values.

title: Problems with encoding (latin1 vs. UTF-8) when running devtools:test()
description:
## TL;DR

UTF-8 encoded files with non-ASCII strings are not correctly represented when running devtools::test()
on Windows. There should be an option to get the encoding from the Description file or from e.g. devtools::test(encoding = "UTF-8")
## Description of issue

I am writing a package where strings containing non-ASCII characters need to be sent to a SQL server through RODBC.

By saving a query string with non-ASCII characters and running this in RStudio, R-terminal or using source from RStudio I am able to get the correct result.

However if I use devtools:test() my code fails since it seems that it does not source the functions using the correct encoding.

I have made a minimal example test functions (not using the SQL server). Here is the relevant code:

```
library(testthat)
context("Test encoding")

test_that("encoding works", {
  query <- "Test encoding: ó æ ø å  END TEST"
  print(query)
})

```

Running this code in RStudio (using Ctrl-R) returns:

> [1] "Test encoding: ó æ ø å  END TEST"
> Which is the correct and expected result.

Pressing the source button in RStudio runs:
`source('C:/Users/hahad/workspaces/bugreports/tests/testthat/test_encoding.R', encoding = 'UTF-8', echo=TRUE)`
and returns the correct, expected result:

```
> source('C:/Users/hahad/workspaces/bugreports/tests/testthat/test_encoding.R', echo=TRUE)

> library(testthat)

> context("Test encoding")

> test_that("encoding works", {
+   query <- "Test encoding: Ã³ Ã¦ Ã¸ Ã¥  END TEST"
+   print(query)
+ })
[1] "Test encoding: Ã³ Ã¦ Ã¸ Ã¥  END TEST"
```

From this I conclude that the files are saved as UTF-8 and should therefore be sourced as UTF-8 (also confirmed using external program and by inspecting the RStudio settings).

If I save this script in a testthat folder in an otherwise empty package and run

> devtools::test()

I get the following result:

```
devtools::test()
Loading bugreports
Testing bugreports
Test encoding: [1] "Test encoding: Ã³ Ã¦ Ã¸ Ã¥  END TEST"


DONE =========================================================================================
```

This means that devtools is sourcing the files as latin1 instead of the UTF-8 files that they are. This happens irrespective of the `Encoding: UTF-8` statement in the description file.

I have attempted to change to a UTF-8 encoding for my locale using

```
> Sys.setlocale("LC_ALL", 'UTF-8')
[1] ""
Warning message:
In Sys.setlocale("LC_ALL", "UTF-8") :
  OS reports request to set locale to "UTF-8" cannot be honored
```
## Summary

When using devtools::test() the encoding is not properly handled (at least on Windows). It is not possible to change to a UTF-8 encoding for the locale on Windows (as far as I can tell), even if this is the suggested encoding to use.
## Proposed solutions
1. Make devtools::test() respect the Encoding in the DESCRIPTION file.
2. Make optional argument to devtools:test() for encoding (as there is for source-function.
3. I should develop package entirely in latin1
4. Find a way to use UTF-8 compatible locale in Windows.

I would prefer solution 1
 :-)

description:
Running `devtools::check("somedir", document = FALSE)` can modify (without any notification) files `/R/RcppExports.R` and `/src/RcppExports.cpp`. I think this is a bug, since I cannot find it documented that modification of those files is a possible side effect of running `check`.

In the most inocuous cases, these leads to adding/removing spaces/newlines, which is annoying (as under version control things have changed, but trivially).

In more serious cases this might mean that a package that passes `R CMD check` fails `devtools::check`.

Even if these possible modifications were made explicit in the help, I do not think modifying these files would be a good idea. I'd suggest running the check **without** modifications, and adding the suggested modifications to the output).

**How can the behavior that leads to errors be triggered?**

Having commented arguments in the function calls.

a) Definitely if you have them in your C++ code, like

```
// [[Rcpp::export]]
void f(double x,
       //double y,
       double z) {
blablabla
```

The `y` leads to the spurious introduction of a `y` in RcppExports{R/cpp}.

b) I think also in some R code Suppose you have  `packagename.R` with a function
like

```
f <- function(x) {
  g(
  #y = oldy,
  x = x)
}
```

And in RcppExports you'll have

```
g < function(x) {
  .Call('packagename_g', PACKAGE = 'packagename', x)
}
```

And in RcppExporst.cpp

```
SEXP packagename_g(SEXP xSEXP);
blablabla
```

**How can this behavior that leads to removing newlines/whitspace be  triggered?**

Add newlines between entries for each function in `RcppExports.cpp`, add
extra whitespace between arguments in `RcppExports.cpp`, etc.

title: Example for Git Remotes Confusing
description:
Your example how to use `Remotes` for a git type dependency does not work. It shows a http git url, but in your implementation you use `git archive` which seems to be unsupported by the git http implementation.

Your example in `vignettes/dependencies.html`
```
Remotes: git::https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2.git
```
Devtool error if I'm actually use a git http url in `Remotes`:
```
Error in vapply(remote, remote_package_name, character(1)) : 
  values must be type 'character',
 but FUN(X[[1]]) result is type 'logical'
```

Caused by this error of the official git client:
```
git archive --remote http://server-name/git/gittest HEAD
fatal: Operation not supported by protocol.
Unexpected end of command stream
```

I think you should change the example to use ssh and no GitHub repository because GitHub does not support `git archive` at all:
```
Remotes: git::git@private-git-server.com:tidyverse/ggplot2.git
```

title: devtools::load_all() does not install packages (Bioconductor)
description:
Dear all,
I am wondering if it is the intended behavior that devtools::load_all() does not check whether package dependencies are fulfilled? The description says:

> load_all loads a package. It roughly simulates what happens when a package is installed and
loaded with library.

But if I don't have a dependency installed (in this case Biostrings), the following happens when running load_all():

> devtools::load_all()
Loading testPkg
Error in (function (dep_name, dep_ver = NA, dep_compare = NA)  : 
  Dependency package Biostrings not available.

If, however, I run the 'proper'
install command, Biostrings is installed successfully:

> devtools::install()
  Installing testPkg
  trying URL
  'https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.3/bioc/src/contrib/Biostrings_2.40.2.tar.gz

It would be nice if load_all() would install required packages directly rather than having to call devtools::install() beforehand, particularly if you do not want to actually install your development package (which is why you are using devtools). 

Additionally, if BiocInstaller is not available, the following happens for install():

> devtools::install()
Installing testPkg
‘BiocInstaller’ must be installed for this functionality.
Fehler in loadNamespace(name) : there is no package called ‘BiocInstaller’
package ‘BiocInstaller’ is not available (for R version 3.3.2) 

In this case, you have to manually load biocLite() to make it work.

Please find attached a minimal working example in terms of a test package.

Thanks and best regards
 Matthias

[testPkg.zip](https://github.com/hadley/devtools/files/816653/testPkg.zip)

title: Rscala: Java dir and jars not included in R package's installed directory
description:
Hi,

I'm trying to write a package which depends on [`rscala`][1].  I wrote a toy example [here][2].

In an R terminal, I did

```R
devtools::install_github("luiarthur/testRscalaPackage")
library(testRscalaPackage)
hello("Arthur")
```

The expected output is "Hello, Arthur!" This can be confirmed by starting scala with
```bash
scala -cp hello_2.11-0.1.0.jar
```
(the jar is included in the repo) and then in scala

```scala
Hello.hello("Arthur")
```

The problem is that the jar is not found. When I look in the directory where the library is installed, it is missing the `java` directory and the jar (which should be inside). If I manually add the `java/hello_2.11-0.1.0.jar` to the directory the package is installed at (in my case it is `~/lib/R_lib/testRscalaPackage`), everything works as expected.

Is there an easy way to include the `java` dir and the jars in the install dir?

title: Wish: build() should exclude git-ignored files
description:
Perhaps this is easiest to achieve with a fresh clone to a temporary directory:

```sh
git clone . $tempdir
R CMD build $tempdir
```

Rationale: By now I often have a considerable number of files and directories in `.git/inst/exclude`, such as IDE files, a package-local library (à la packrat), etc.. It's difficult to add these files to `.Rbuildignore` without committing them to the repository. On the other hand, I usually `build()` only for a CRAN release, and then I want a build from a clean state, just like on Travis.

title: functions for working with Docker
description:
Docker is all the rage amongst DevOps types and cloud service providers and seems to offer some concrete advantages for R users in managing dependencies, reproducibility and isolation of the computational environment (@cboettig has a nice paper on this: http://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.0846.pdf). And no doubt you've seen [rocker-org](https://github.com/rocker-org) by @eddelbuettel and @cboettig, which is a huge contribution to using R and RStudio with docker. 

What do you think about these functions being part of `devtools`:
- `add_dockerfile()`  writes a basic dockerfile to build a docker image that includes the R package and all its dependencies, and maybe edits other files in the package if necessary (maybe `.Rbuildignore`, cf. https://github.com/benmarwick/Steele_et_al_VR003_MSA_Pigments/blob/master/vignettes/Dockerfile and https://github.com/cboettig/nonparametric-bayes/blob/master/manuscripts/Dockerfile). 
- `add_circle()` writes a circle.yml file (analogous to travis.yml) for [circleci's](https://circleci.com/) continuous integration service of the docker image that the dockerfile generates (cf. https://github.com/benmarwick/Steele_et_al_VR003_MSA_Pigments/blob/master/circle.yml this also pushes the image to the docker hub when the tests pass)
- `build_docker()` builds the docker image from the dockerfile made by `add_dockerfile()`. This would require docker to be installed locally. Analogous to R package build tools in `devtools` and RStudio.
- `push_docker()` pushes the docker image to an online repository, the [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/) is the big one at the moment, but [Google have just announced one also](https://cloud.google.com/tools/container-registry/). This would require docker to be installed locally. Analogous to git push in RStudio.

This might be a bit of mission creep for `devtools` and overlap with the goals of `packrat`, but it would simplify the reproducible research workflow nicely (for Carl and I at least, not sure that Dirk is a `devtools` user ;) No doubt there are others using R and Docker that would benefit also. Anyway, what do you reckon?

title: `check(check_version = FALSE)` should use `_R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_REMOTE_`
description:
Currently the `check_version` option of `devtools::check()` defaults to `FALSE`.  When `FALSE`, it sets  `_R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_` to false, which does a lot more than just turning off the version checks:  it also turns off a bunch of style checks which can cause a package to be rejected by CRAN.  Those style checks are quick, unlike the version number check, which can be quite slow.

I've just added a new environment variable to R-devel (as of revision r70944) called  `_R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_REMOTE_` which is a more appropriate variable to set false by default.  It keeps the quick local checks, but turns off the remote ones, including the version check.  (The style checks will still only be run if `_R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_` is true, e.g. if `--as-cran` is given as a check option.)

It's not clear yet whether this will make it into R-patched, so for now it should only be used if

```
getRversion() >= "3.4.0" && as.numeric(R.version[["svn rev"]]) >= 70944
```

title: use_readme_rmd() not compatible with pkgdown::build_site()
description:
Say you've created a new package with R Studio (New Project -> R Package). If you then add a README.Rmd to it with `devtools::use_readme_rmd()`, `pkgdown::build_site()` fails with

```R
Updating README.md
Error in (function (variant = "markdown_strict", preserve_yaml = FALSE,  : 
  unused argument (html_preview = FALSE)
```

A [pkgdown issue](https://github.com/hadley/pkgdown/issues/286) was filed and closed with no fix except advising users to manually switch the README.Rmd YAML to

```R
output: rmarkdown::github_document
```

which fixes the problem and `pkgdown::build_site()` succeeds.

Although at core this is an issue with pkgdown requirements, there should be no reason to favor the incompatible devtools default YAML for README.Rmd. Could the default YAML be changed to the latter for automatic compatibility with pkgdown?

Thanks for the great software.

title: helper_ files don't have access to package's Imports when loaded with load_all
description:
When a test is run with `testthat::test_check`, the `helper_` files get sourced within a copy of the package's namespace environment which is a child of the package's "imports" environment. Therefore, when run with `testthat`, the functions defined in `helper_` files have access to the package's imports.
When `devtools::load_all` loads a package, it apparently runs the `helper_` files in the new package's "package:" environment and they don't have that access.
Apparently [a possible interpretation of load_all](https://github.com/hadley/devtools/issues/1202#issuecomment-230848112) is that it should recreate the environment in which tests are run, so I suggest to also evaluate `helper_` files with access to imports. The current behaviour also breaks `devtools::test` when the github version of `testthat` is installed and `load_helpers = FALSE` is passed to `testthat::test_dir`.

A way to reproduce this is to clone [mlr](https://github.com/mlr-org/mlr) and loading the current (4b9997d) commit with `devtools::load_all`. The `helper_helpers.R` file in the `tests/testthat` directory introduces a function "requirePackagesOrSkip", which fails when run, since it uses a function exported by `BBmisc`. Also, when the current github version of `testthat` (1.0.2.9000) is installed,
```R
devtools::test("mlr", filter = "cluster_kmeans")
```
(a test that uses `requirePackagesOrSkip`) fails.

However, going into the "tests" directory of mlr, run R and execute
```R
testthat::test_check("mlr", filter = "cluster_kmeans")
```
This executes `requirePackagesOrSkip` without any problems.

title: Don't include badges in README when preparing tarball for CRAN submission
description:
It seems that the README.md that gets uploaded on CRAN shouldn't include the badges that show code coverage, build status, etc.

These badges are obviously very useful when seen on GitHub, but they don't make sense when viewed on CRAN (or locally). Arguably, a lot less people read the README from CRAN than GitHub.

For instance, the repository might move (e.g., the links included in the README for dplyr 0.5.0 point to https://travis-ci.org/hadley/dplyr and https://codecov.io/github/hadley/dplyr?branch=master which are broken as the corresponding github repo has moved to tidyverse/dplyr) or the badges show the coverage/build status of the development version and not the version currently hosted on CRAN.

I am not sure what would be a reasonable technical solution to this, but it seems that devtools would be a natural place to handle it.

title: Feature Request: Find Minimum Version of Required Packages
description:
I've recently experienced an issue with my PKNCA package where I didn't know that a new feature I added had a minimum required version of a package in the Imports list.  I'd like to propose a new feature of devtools that will take a list of packages and install them to look for the version number of dependencies where tests fail.  It would then indicate that the next version is the required version.

A potential interface could be:
```r
find_required_dep_version(pkg=".", which_set=c("Depends", "Imports", "Suggests"), which_library, repo=getOption("repos"), ...)
```

It would then search on CRAN (or potentially other repository types) installing dependency packages one-by-one back in time until tests fail.

If this would be of interest, I can generate a pull request.

title: BUG: parse_check_results() fails to pick statuses when R CMD check reports on timings
description:
When forcing `R CMD check` to report on process times ("timings") for all tests;
```sh
export _R_CHECK_TIMINGS_=0
```
`devtools::revdep_check()` fails to detect ERRORs, WARNINGs, and NOTEs.

For example, I observe:

```
Checked doFuture            : 0 errors | 0 warnings | 0 notes
Checked fiery               : 0 errors | 0 warnings | 0 notes
Checked future.BatchJobs    : 0 errors | 0 warnings | 0 notes
```

although fiery's `00check.log` file contains:

```r
* checking tests ... [1s/11s] ERROR
  Running ‘testthat.R’ [1s/11s]
Running the tests in ‘tests/testthat.R’ failed.
Last 13 lines of output:
  5: lazy(expr = {
         message("test")
         10
     })
  6: .Defunct(msg = "Future strategy 'lazy' is deprecated. Instead, use f <- futur
e(..., lazy = TRUE) or v %<-% { ... } %lazy% TRUE.")
  7: stop(paste(msg, collapse = ""), call. = FALSE, domain = NA)
  
  testthat results ===============================================================
=
  OK: 152 SKIPPED: 0 FAILED: 3
  1. Error: futures can be added and called (@test-Fire.R#214) 
  2. Error: DelayStack works (@test-FutureStack.R#7) 
  3. Error: TimeStack works (@test-FutureStack.R#34) 
  
  Error: testthat unit tests failed
  Execution halted
* DONE
Status: 1 ERROR
```

# Troubleshooting

The reason for this is that [devtools:::parse_check_results()](https://github.com/hadley/devtools/blob/master/R/check-results.R#L12-L14) (master branch, but also in 1.13.1) assumes that `R CMD check` does not report on timings because it looks for fixed string patterns:
```r
      errors =   pieces[grepl("... ERROR", pieces, fixed = TRUE)],
      warnings = pieces[grepl("... WARN", pieces, fixed = TRUE)],
      notes =    pieces[grepl("... NOTE", pieces, fixed = TRUE)]
```
but those won't pick up `... [1s/11s] ERROR`.

When one don't do `export _R_CHECK_TIMINGS_=0`, then it works;
```r
Checked doFuture            : 0 errors | 0 warnings | 0 notes
Checked fiery               : 1 error  | 0 warnings | 0 notes
Checked future.BatchJobs    : 1 error  | 0 warnings | 0 notes
```

# Solution
Need to use a regular expression instead.

H/T @jimhester

title: Native calls fail after load_all ("not resolved from current namespace")
description:
`devtools::load_all` unloads previously loaded DLLs and therefore reorders the [`LoadedDLL`](https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/a1f8bde04bdbb0062964381efcbd79550c019e03/src/main/Rdynload.c#L138) array, but the `getCallingDLLe` result that [R relies upon when looking up DLL objects](https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/trunk/src/main/dotcode.c#L1406) does not change in the same way. This sometimes leads to `not resolved from current namespace` errors when an unlucky package calls a `.C` function.

In the following example, I have cloned the [ParamHelpers](https://github.com/berndbischl/ParamHelpers) package to a subdirectory, and I have the [lhs](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/lhs/index.html) package installed in my library. R needs to be run with the `--vanilla` option to prevent interference from a possible `.RData` file.
```R
$ R --vanilla
> devtools::load_all("ParamHelpers")
Loading ParamHelpers
Re-compiling ParamHelpers
'/usr/lib64/R/bin/R' CMD INSTALL '/home/user/ParamHelpers' --library='/tmp/RtmproDXbZ/devtools_install_588768c7107c' --no-R --no-data --no-help --no-demo --no-inst --no-docs --no-exec --no-multiarch --no-test-load
make: Nothing to be done for 'all'.
> lhs::maximinLHS(n=2, k=2)  # implicitly load the lhs DLL; works fine here.
          [,1]      [,2]
[1,] 0.6008410 0.9491948
[2,] 0.4723376 0.3303989
> devtools::load_all("ParamHelpers")
Loading ParamHelpers
Re-compiling ParamHelpers
'/usr/lib64/R/bin/R' CMD INSTALL '/home/user/master/ParamHelpers' --library='/tmp/RtmproDXbZ/devtools_install_58874478c51e' --no-R --no-data --no-help --no-demo --no-inst --no-docs --no-exec --no-multiarch --no-test-load
make: Nothing to be done for 'all'.
> lhs::maximinLHS(n=2, k=2)  # does not work                                                                                                                                                                                                               
Error in .C("maximinLHS_C", as.integer(n), as.integer(k), as.integer(dup),  : 
  "maximinLHS_C" not resolved from current namespace (lhs)
```

P.S.
* One could also argue this is R's fault, and `dyn.unload` should take care of this. [This looks like the same issue and was filed 1.5 years ago at the R project's bugzilla](https://bugs.r-project.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=16446). Someone with an account could add a back reference to here.
* [This was also an issue here](https://github.com/mlr-org/mlr/issues/1379), see [my comment](https://github.com/mlr-org/mlr/issues/1379#issuecomment-282179425).
* A possible workaround on the side of the package ('lhs' in this example) is to use the `PACKAGE` argument when calling `.C`.
* I'm running on a x86_64 linux system, Windows might very well be a different story.

title: install_github() exits with error when multiple packages are present in repository
description:
When using _install_github()_ to install packages from a repo that has multiple subfolders with packages in it:

```r
install_github("user/MyRepoName", ref = "release",  auth_token = Sys.getenv("GITHUB_PAT"), subdir = "Library/MyPackage1/", dependencies = TRUE)
```

will work only if _MyPackage1_ doesn't have dependencies within packages present in _"user/MyRepoName/Library"_

```r
install_github("user/MyRepoName", ref = "release",  auth_token = Sys.getenv("GITHUB_PAT"), subdir = "Library/MyPackage2/", dependencies = TRUE)
```

will fail if _MyPackage2_ depends on _MyPackage1_ until "dependencies = FALSE" is set:

```r
install_github("user/MyRepoName", ref = "release",  auth_token = Sys.getenv("GITHUB_PAT"), subdir = "Library/MyPackage2/", dependencies = FALSE)
```
However, this is not optimal for package deployment as it will also skip installing external CRAN dependencies.

The error returned is like this:

_Downloading GitHub user/MyRepoName@release
from URL https://api.github.com/repos/user/MyRepoName@release/zipball/release
Installing MyPackage2
Downloading GitHub repo user/MyRepoName@release
from URL https://api.github.com/repos/user/MyRepoName@release/zipball/release_
**Error in stop(github_error(request)) : Not Found (404)**

I have walked through the code and the error is happening when trying to pull the dependency package MyPackage1 from the same GitHub repo . The original remote$auth_token is not copied to subsequent calls to install_remote() for dependent packages. I have checked in debug mode and if I copy the remote$auth_token field from first call when downloading _MyPackage2_ to second install_remote() call for dependent package _MyPackage1_ it is working.

Also, there is a scope for optimization as these packages (MyPackage1, MyPackage2, MyPackage3,...) got downloaded in first zipball anyway as they reside in the same Library folder

title: Feature request: add -I"./inst/include" to devtools::test() ccflags

Note that the symlink does not fix problems with calling devtools::check(args = c('--as-cran')) as this probably calls testthat in a different environment.
