title: remote functions for private github repo
description:
Hi, 

I tried to used `Remotes` field in `DESCRIPTION` to manage dependencies for packages of my company hosted a private organisation.

I do not manage yet to make it works and I have notice some problems regarding private vs public repo. 

``` r
# with public repo
devtools:::remote_package_name.github_remote(devtools:::github_remote("hadley/lubridate"))
#> Using GitHub PAT from envvar GITHUB_PAT
#> [1] "lubridate"

# with private repo
devtools:::remote_package_name.github_remote(devtools:::github_remote("cderv/myprivaterepo"))
#> Using GitHub PAT from envvar GITHUB_PAT
#> [1] NA
```

In fact, the `GET` request in `remote_package_name.github_remote` has a result of an error 404. 
As there is no authentication sent with the `GET` using `devtools::github_auth(github_pat())`, it cannot found the page.

I tried first as it is done inside `remote_package_name.github_remote`
```r
httr::GET("https://github.com", 
                path = "cderv/myprivaterepo/raw/master/DESCRIPTION", 
                devtools:::github_auth(github_pat()))
```
but it did not worded. So I used, 
```r
httr::GET("https://raw.githubusercontent.com", 
                path = "cderv/myprivaterepo/master/DESCRIPTION", 
                devtools:::github_auth(github_pat()))
```
and it worked

Is it a known issue ? 
Is there a workaround to work with private repo ?

title: check_built, revdep_check require full path names
description: I don't know whether it's a structural issue or an oversight that full path names are needed for `check_built()` and (by extension) for `revdep_check()`, but it had me stumped for a while.  If it's not structural it would seem better to me to allow `check_built("./foo.tar.gz")` to work as well as `check_build("~/stuff/foo.tar.gz")` and similarly (`revdep_check(...,check_dir="local_path")`), but if you'd prefer either in the short or long term to leave the behaviour the way it is, I would be happy to provide a documentation patch as a PR.

title: Can't load downstream packages after load_all()
description:
In the working directory of a project based on a local fork of https://github.com/lme4/lme4:

``` r

Loading lme4
Loading required package: Matrix
> library(MEMSS)
Error: package ‘lme4’ required by ‘MEMSS’ could not be found
```

The error is thrown from `base::.getRequiredPackages2`, because it can't work out the version of the package loaded by `devtools::load_all`. The function `.findVersion` is defined inside `base::getRequiredPackages2`:

``` r
    .findVersion <- function(pkg, lib.loc = NULL) {
        pfile <- system.file("Meta", "package.rds", package = pkg, 
            lib.loc = lib.loc)
        if (nzchar(pfile)) 
            as.numeric_version(readRDS(pfile)$DESCRIPTION["Version"])
    }
```

It's not finding `package.rds`, so it's returning `NULL`. This triggers the error here:

``` r
        current <- .findVersion(pkg, lib.loc)
        if (is.null(current)) 
            stop(gettextf("package %s required by %s could not be found", 
                sQuote(pkg), sQuote(pkgname)), call. = FALSE, 
                domain = NA)
```

title: Multiple remotes in DESCRIPTION
description:
In `utils.R`, for `read_dcf`, the code is:

``` r
read_dcf <- function(path) {
  fields <- colnames(read.dcf(path))
  as.list(read.dcf(path, keep.white = fields)[1, ])
}
```

I wanted to know what the expected behavior would/should be for a DESCRIPTION with duplicated fields (for example Remotes): silent, warning, or error?  If `all = TRUE` on `read.dcf`, this may allow for this case to be parsed with all remotes (even conflicting), but it may be a bad case and needs an error
## Parsing DESCRIPTION with default `read.dcf`

``` r
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/muschellij2/freesurfer/7f336cddadfa1000f128db3341893f96af9eaf51/DESCRIPTION"
destfile = file.path(tempdir(), "DESCRIPTION")
download.file(url, destfile = destfile)
dcf = read.dcf(destfile)
colnames(dcf)
```

```
##  [1] "Package"            "Type"               "Title"             
##  [4] "Version"            "Author"             "Maintainer"        
##  [7] "Description"        "Imports"            "Depends"           
## [10] "License"            "Suggests"           "VignetteBuilder"   
## [13] "Remotes"            "BugReports"         "SystemRequirements"
## [16] "RoxygenNote"
```
### Only "last" Remotes section held

``` r
dcf[, "Remotes"]
```

```
##               Remotes 
## "neuroconductor/fslr"
```
## Parsing DESCRIPTION with default `read.dcf(all = TRUE)`

``` r
dcf_all = read.dcf(destfile, all = TRUE)
colnames(dcf_all)
```

```
##  [1] "Package"            "Type"               "Title"             
##  [4] "Version"            "Author"             "Maintainer"        
##  [7] "Description"        "Imports"            "Depends"
```

title: Moving of vignettes fails depending on access rights to folders
description:
I experienced a problem when building the vignettes. The error message when running 

``` r
devtools::build_vignettes()
```

was 
_Error in file.copy(out_mv, doc_dir, overwrite = TRUE) : 
  more 'from' files than 'to' files_

However, since the _vignettes_ folder contained the build vignettes, I didn't care about it until I wanted to release the package and noticed that the zipped file doesn't contain them.

Tracing down the cause of these issues, I narrowed it down to line 23-25 of vignette-r.r

``` r
if (!file.exists(doc_dir)) {
    dir.create(doc_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  }
```

In my case, the subfolder _doc_ in _inst/doc_ didn't exist yet. So the code tried to create it but did not succeed because I don't have writing access to some of the previous folders (e.g. if the package root is in p:/folder1/folder2/package I don't have writing access to p:/folder1). Setting `r recursive = FALSE` will solve the issue for me but certainly create new ones for people who don't have the _inst_ folder yet. 

I don't know why you set `r showWarnings = FALSE`, but if it was `TRUE`, I would have solved the access rights issue much faster. Actually I'm surprised that `dir.create` only creates a warning and not an error if it didn't succeed. Maybe adding something like

``` r
if (!file.exists(doc_dir)) {
    dir.create(doc_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    if (!file.exists(doc_dir)) stop(paste("Couldn't create folder ", doc_dir))
  }
```

would be a good idea

title: build() should call clean_vignettes by default if vignettes = TRUE
description:
## TL;DR
- [ ] new parameter `clean_vignettes = TRUE` to `build()`
- [ ] update docs for `build_vignettes()`, perhaps mention that adding `inst/doc` to `.Rbuildignore` doesn't work
## Details

The documentation of `build_vignette` [(code ref)](https://github.com/hadley/devtools/blob/d2bdbada3f8921978ab13dbcad5897a60cf5f965/R/vignettes.r#L5) mentions this:

> You need to ensure that these files are not included in the built package...

It would be best if `devtools` just did this:

```
build <- function(..., vignettes = TRUE, clean_vignettes = vignettes) {
  if (clean_vignettes)
    clean_vignettes()
  ...
}
```

Or, even better, move the stuff away during the `build` process and put it back when done.

Otherwise, if `build_vignettes` is called just once, all subsequent updates to the original vignette source will be ignored. (If `inst/doc` is in `.Rbuildignore`, vignettes are built but not included in the `.tar.gz`.) Build artifacts, if ignored by the VCS, should have no impact on the result of subsequent builds!

Per https://github.com/hadley/devtools/commit/9bb78f10ce750d2bd24ca655329e3cbf18cb3f37#commitcomment-11326492.

title: Too easy to forget junk in inst/doc/ and send a package with outdated vignettes to CRAN
description:
As `use_vignette()` adds "inst/doc/" to .gitignore, it's very easy to forget that you've left files in there from using `build_vignettes()` at some point in the past. Doing so causes package building to silently fail to update vignette files with the latest built vignettes (and can lead to a surprising embarrassment on CRAN when old versions with incomplete sentences or empty placeholder files get posted)

``` R
path <- file.path(tempdir(), "oldvignettes")
if (length(dir(path))) unlink(path, recursive = TRUE)
devtools::create(path)
devtools::use_vignette("example", path)
devtools::build_vignettes(path)
vfile <- file(file.path(path, "vignettes", "example.Rmd"), open = "a")
writeLines(c("", "Updated vignette text"), vfile)
close(vfile)
pkg <- devtools::build(path, vignettes = TRUE)
pkgfile <- gzfile(pkg, open = "rb")
untar(pkgfile, exdir = file.path(path, "..", "built"))
close(pkgfile)
built_vignette <- file(file.path(path, "..", "built", "oldvignettes", "inst",
                                 "doc", "example.Rmd"))
built_vignette_lines <- readLines(built_vignette)
close(built_vignette)
stopifnot(any(grepl("Updated vignette text", built_vignette_lines)))
```

Adding a check to `release()` for any files in inst/doc/ would save others from this mistake

title: Package S4 methods are sometimes not dispatched when using `load_all`
description:
I'm working on development of a few packages and we are using a number of S4 classes and methods. When using devtools' `load_all()` I've noticed that sometimes custom methods aren't being dispatched.

Here is a minimal example (I'm trying to write a new method for `write.csv`, and have that method pass all of it's arguments to another function, hence my use here.)
A package with the following in `./R/[anyfile].R`:
```
new_class <- setClass("new_class", slots = c(text = 'character'))
setGeneric("write.csv")
setMethod("write.csv", "new_class", function (...)  print("using new_class method") )
```
When loaded with `load_all()` and trying to run the following:
```
new_obj <- new_class(text = 'foo')
write.csv(new_obj, file = 'bar')
```
Errors with (presumably because the standard `write.csv` method is being used):
```
Error in as.data.frame.default(x[[i]], optional = TRUE) : 
  cannot coerce class "structure("new_class", package = "test")" to a data.frame
```

Whereas, if I (install and) load the package with `install()` and run the same lines, I get what I expect:
```
new_obj <- new_class(text = 'foo')
write.csv(new_obj, file = 'bar')
[1] "using new_class method"
```

If I _only_ provide `new_obj` and no other arguments my custom method is dispatched with both `load_all()` and `install()`, but I would like to be able to pass on arbitrary arguments with my custom method.
```
write.csv(new_obj)
[1] "using new_class method"
```

Because devtools' `test()` uses `load_all()`, I'm also seeing this behavior when I run tests through devtools as well. Running tests as part of `R CMD check` use the custom method just like if the package were installed / loaded with `install()`.

title: Avoid reloading packages
description:
More specifically, it would be great if a package request **not** to be unloaded/reloaded, or at least not its shared lib. 

This is because some packages cannot be reloaded properly. This includes all packages that depend on libglib on Linux. libgtk also depends on libglib, so libgtk dependent packages cannot be reloaded, either. If these packages are unloaded, they typically leave some extra threads behind. If they are then reloaded, then they probably crash R.

I am not sure what the best way would be to indicate this in the package.

title: Use BatchJobs instead of parallel::mclapply()
description:
Big advantages:
- Restartability: The job definitions are part of the cache, and set up during its creation. BatchJobs records which jobs haven't completed yet and can rerun only the failed ones in a revdep_check_resume() run
- Scalability: Works interactively, multicore, in a local network of machines via SSH, or on a HPC cluster; devtools doesn't need to care about configuration

title: Proposal of new function: build_manual()
description:
As far as I know, devtools do not offer possibility to easily and directly build pdf manual. Maybe something like the function below could be added?

```
#' Create package manual
#' 
#' @param pkg package description, can be path or package name.  See
#'   \code{\link{as.package}} for more information
#' @param path path in which to produce package.  If \code{NULL}, defaults to
#'   the parent directory of the package.
#' 
#' @seealso \code{\link{RdUtils}} 
#' @export

build_manual <- function(pkg = ".", path = NULL) {
  pkg <- as.package(pkg)
  if (is.null(path)) {
    path <- dirname(pkg$path)
  }
  name <- paste0(pkg$package, "_", pkg$version, ".pdf", collapse = " ")
  system(paste0("R CMD Rd2pdf --force --output=", path, "/", name, " ", shQuote(pkg$path), collapse = " "))
}
```

title: install_bitbucket() needs a default 'quiet' value
description:
Hi,

Using the example on the `install_bitbucket` help page:

```
install_bitbucket("sulab/mygene.r@default")
```

Fails with:

```
Error in value[[3L]](cond) : argument "quiet" is missing, with no default
```

I think the problem is that the arguments of `install_bitbucket` are passed to `try_install_remote`, which requires a value for `quiet`:

```
install_bitbucket(repo, username, ref = "master", subdir = NULL, auth_user = NULL, 
   password = NULL, ...) 
-> install_remotes(remotes, ...) 
-> try_install_remote(..., quiet = quiet)
```

If we add `quiet` to install_bitbucket, the problem is solved: 

```
install_bitbucket("sulab/mygene.r@default", quiet = FALSE)
## works as expected
```

Adding a default `quiet` value to the `install_bitbucket` definition, as is the case in `install_github`, would fix this.

Best,

Tyler

title: install_svn doesn't work with R-forge
description:
As mentioned in https://github.com/hadley/devtools/issues/684 last year, `install_svn` assumes all paths in Subversion repositories contain either "trunk" or "branches".  Those are just conventional names, they aren't requirements, and the repositories created on R-forge.r-project.org don't use those names.

I don't like the suggested fix from https://github.com/hadley/devtools/issues/684.  The proper fix is to drop the assumption that every repository must have a particular structure.  Allow users to specify something like `svn://svn.r-forge.r-project.org/svnroot/rgl/pkg/rgl` entirely in the `url` part of the name, or split up between the `url` and `subdir` parts.

Edited to add:  The same problem occurs in `remotes`, which got the code from here (or vice versa).  I've created a patch and sent the following pull request there:  https://github.com/MangoTheCat/remotes/pull/33.

description:

title: install_version doesn't leverage config values when fetching Meta/archive.rds
description:
First off: love this tool.  Unfortunately, when we are behind a CRAN mirror with self-signed certs (e.g. self-hosted mirror) and basic auth, obtaining the "Meta/archive.rds" files isn't done with any of the config values set in the install_version function call.

Example that fails
`install_version('slam', version='0.1-37', repos="https://self-hosted.repo", config = config( ssl_verifypeer = FALSE, userpwd='user:pass'))`

But, the following call to install_url works (which appears would be called if install_version got past the package_find_repo call)
`install_url("https://self-signed.repo/src/contrib/Archive/slam/slam_0.1-37.tar.gz", config = config(ssl_verifypeer = FALSE, userpwd='user:pass')))`

The line that appears to be failing is [this line in read_archive](https://github.com/hadley/devtools/blob/master/R/install-version.r#L50).

It looks like `curl()` could be used in place of `url()`, passing in a handle using the same config values passed in to install_version (if config is passed in, anyway)?  This is probably a huge edge case, but it would be a huge help.

title: install_github() failing on Windows due to long path names
description:
We have a package available for install in a sub directory `R Package/ffanalytics` at `dadrivr/FantasyFootballAnalyticsR`. Users are instructed to install this via `devtools::install_github(repo = "dadrivr/FantasyFootballAnalyticsR", subdir = "R Package/ffanalytics")`. However, Windows users are reporting that the install fails with following error

```
Error in utils::unzip(src, exdir = target) :
cannot open file ‘C:/Users/<username>/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpMZfFU0/devtools63c36d21285/dadrivr-FantasyFootballAnalyticsR-6c6c4a9/R Markdown/SubcriptionAccuracy/subscriptionAccuracy_cache/markdown_phpextra+backtick_code_blocks/unnamed-chunk-1_af5e2a896358b9ccbc8241e876b9ce5c.RData’: No such file or directory
```

The file mentioned is not part of the package directory, so I suspect that `devtools::install_github` is downloading the entire repo and then parsing it to find the subdir with the package. Since the repo files are extracted into a temp directory (`C:/Users/<username>/AppData/Local/Temp......`) the file names get rather long when it has to go through several levels of folders. 
The interesting thing is that you can get the command to complete after a number of tries - which may be when the file paths become short enough (<256 characters)

title: Let `install_version()` search for version in multiple repos
description:
TL;DR: I would like to change `install_version()` so that it will search for the requested version of the package in each of the repositories given, in sequence.

Motivation:  my company uses R internally, creating packages for various projects and publishing them to internal CRAN-alike servers for integration by other teams.  We have one “cran-stable” for official releases, and one CRAN-alike that updates with new snapshots every time someone pushes to a “develop” branch.

I would like our team to call `install_version(pkg, version, repos)`, which then iterates over each entry of `repos` until a suitable version is found.  

For instance, we might have the following:
-  http://myserver/cran-stable:
  - MyPackage_0.23.tar.gz
-  http://myserver/cran-dev:
  - MyPackage_0.24-283.tar.gz

```
repos <- c(Stable="http://myserver/cran-stable",
              Dev="http://myserver/cran-dev",
             CRAN="https://cran.revolutionanalytics.com")
install_version('MyPackage', '0.23', repos)  # Installs from ‘Stable’
install_version('MyPackage', '0.24', repos)  # Installs from ‘Dev’
```

Right now, it looks like `install_version()` expects exactly one version of a package to be officially published across all repositories, and it only knows how to look for alternate versions in `archive/` directories, under the assumption that the only alternate versions that could exist are previously-published versions.

Also, because packages in the “Dev” server may have versioned dependencies on packages from either repository, the same semantics would need to apply to the dependencies too, so `install_version()` would call itself recursively to handle them.

I would be happy to work this up as a pull request that keeps the existing semantics of finding packages in `archive/` directories too.

title: install_github forces remotes to branch tip
description:
I am trying to create a reproducible environment for document rendering. My intention was to lock `rmarkdown` and `bookdown`, for example, to specific commit SHAs.

```
R -e "devtools::install_github('rstudio/rmarkdown', ref = '70b9f1ec4ce71628d5d74f9a6287933a415fef9b')"
R -e "devtools::install_github('rstudio/bookdown', ref ='9f7dc0897c96c22f20f6cb69b757538fb7a0cf46')"
```

The `bookdown` package contains a `Remotes` specification:

```
Remotes: rstudio/rmarkdown, rstudio/htmltools, ramnathv/htmlwidgets
```

When `install_github` installs `bookdown`, the `rmarkdown` package is re-installed from the tip of its master branch (partial log from `bookdown` installation):

```
Downloading GitHub repo rstudio/rmarkdown@master
from URL https://api.github.com/repos/rstudio/rmarkdown/zipball/master
Installing rmarkdown
```

Is there a way to inform `install_github` that the `rmarkdown` remote is satisfied by the previously installed version? Is there more metadata that `bookdown` could include to specify the minimum version it needs from a particular remote?

I'm looking for recommendations for an installation technique that can let me and my teammates locally obtain the same package versions and thus the same rendering environment.

I am ignoring for the moment the fact that we are not locking all the dependencies; especially those that arrive from CRAN. I am focused right now on the dependencies that are rapidly changing. Locking versions for these GitHub dependencies means that we will all see the same behavior -- consistency of result is more important than some of us having the absolute latest code.

description:

Could we use an env var named GITHUB_API_URL for this? I suggest it because [`gh`](https://github.com/gaborcsardi/gh) already [does this](https://github.com/gaborcsardi/gh/blob/b7d3b8071ab24c67fd6db10f2997b3ab9d5f612d/R/package.R#L94). If GITHUB_API_URL is not defined, then use existing default `https://api.github.com`.

This makes it easier to define a user-level GITHUB_PAT for github.com and, for individual projects, store an alternative host and PAT for GitHub Enterprise in a project-level `.Renviron`.

title: `document` generates wrong S3 exports if NAMESPACE doesn’t exist yet
description:
My package ‹modules› has an [insidious bug](https://github.com/klmr/modules/issues/117) related to incorrect exports of S3 methods, generated via roxygen2. However, [the roxygen2 tags inside my package *are correct*](https://github.com/klmr/modules/blob/32e7404e9a4ed59e10a30e88e8b1970479d9edb8/R/export_roclet.r#L5-L7):

```r
#' @importFrom roxygen2 roclet_tags
#' @export
roclet_tags.roclet_export = function (x) {
```

The problem is that my deployment process (which generates the documentation) starts from a blank slate, i.e. no `NAMESPACE` file exists yet. As a consequence, even though the `Imports` are correctly listed in the `DESCRIPTION`, devtools fails to import the necessary S3 generic which my method extends. Subsequently roxygen2 fails to recognise that these methods are, indeed, S3 methods; and [it generates the following `NAMESPACE` entry](https://github.com/klmr/modules/blob/4dc6a9202b54a2ddd852ca9124854613d8815b7d/NAMESPACE#L19):

```r
export(roclet_tags.roclet_export)
```

---

### To reproduce this issue:

1. Generate an empty package using `Rscript -e 'dummy = 1; package.skeleton("foo", "dummy")'`
2. `cd foo`
3. Add imports: `echo 'Imports: roxygen2' >> DESCRIPTION`
4. `rm NAMESPACE`
5. Add a new file `R/test.r` with the contents

    ```r
    #' @importFrom roxygen2 roclet_tags
    #' @export
    roclet_tags.roclet_foobar = function (x) { list() }
    ```

6. Run `Rscript -e 'devtools::document()'`

### Expected output:

```r
# Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand

S3method(roclet_tags,roclet_foobar)
importFrom(roxygen2,roclet_tags)
```

### Actual output:

```r
# Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand

export(roclet_tags.roclet_foobar)
importFrom(roxygen2,roclet_tags)
```

Running `Rscript -e 'devtools::document()'` *a second time* yields a corrected `NAMESPACE` file.

---

I am reporting this bug here since using `roxygen2::roxygenize()` instead of `devtools::document()` actually *works*: `roxygen2::roxygenize` is “dumber” and performs less sophisticated loading. `devtools::load_all`, by contrast, is “too smart” and attempts to use the (non-existent) `NAMESPACE` as a hint for loading. This is fundamentally circular and, though a good heuristic, bound to produce false results on occasion.

Unfortunately devtools gives no indication of potential problems, and the result is very hard to debug failures (see linked bug report): I took several days of trial and error and going through roxygen2 and devtools internals to find the problem; if I hadn’t already known my way around both code bases this would have taken even longer.

At the very least `document` should produce a clear warning about potentially mis-classifying S3 methods; even better would be a way of controlling the behaviour so that a single pass of `document` produces the correct output.

title: Feature request: build some but not all vignettes
description:
It would be nice to have an argument to `build_vignettes` that lets you choose specific vignettes to build.

My specific use case is that I have 3 vignettes for my package. One of them requires a Spark connection, and takes several minutes to build. The others don't require Spark, and are likely to error out if it's present, in fact.

My current workaround for building the Spark vignette is to move the other 2 vignettes out of the /vignettes subdir, run `build_vignettes()`, and then move them back again. I do the same in reverse if I want to build the non-Spark vignettes. This isn't very automated, and prone to errors.

Something like `build_vignettes(pattern="regex")` would solve this nicely, where only files matching the supplied regex are built.

title: Option to prevent files opening with `use_vignette()` etc.
description:
Some functions to add useful infrastructure to a package also then open the files created. For example, `use_news_md()` will create and then open the news.md file, and similar behaviour is found in `use_readme_rmd()`, `use_package_docs()`, `use_vignette()` and possibly others.

I have written a wrapper function which initialises a new package with infrastructure and then switches to the new RStudio project in a new RStudio session. However, as a side-effect, all the files mentioned above get opened in my old RStudio session.

It would be nice to be able to pass an `open = FALSE` argument to the underlying code. For example, here is the code for `use_package_doc`:

```
function (pkg = ".") 
{
    pkg <- as.package(pkg)
    use_template("packagename-package.r", file.path("R", paste(pkg$package, 
        "-package.r", sep = "")), data = list(name = pkg$package), 
        open = TRUE, pkg = pkg)
}
<environment: namespace:devtools>
```

Note the `open = TRUE` on the fourth line of function body code, which seems to be an argument of the internal `{devtools}` function `devtools:::use_template`. Perhaps this argument could be exposed to users of the higher-level functions.

title: Chicken-and-egg NAMESPACE problem with Roxygen2, `devtools::check()`, and Rcpp
description:
Running `devtools::check()` on a project that uses Rcpp fails if the `NAMESPACE` file does not exist:

```
> devtools::check()
Updating wsim.lsm documentation
Loading wsim.lsm
Error in Rcpp::compileAttributes() : 
  pkgdir must refer to the directory containing an R package

```

To generate the `NAMESPACE` file, I need to run `devtools::document()`.  But this also invokes Rcpp, which in turn fails because the `NAMESPACE` file does not exist:

```
> devtools::document()
Updating wsim.lsm documentation
Loading wsim.lsm
Error in Rcpp::compileAttributes() : 
  pkgdir must refer to the directory containing an R package
```

It's not enough to run `touch NAMESPACE` before build, because Roxygen2 will only replace a NAMESPACE file that it generated.  For now, I papered this over with a hackish Makefile:

```
NAMESPACE:
	echo "# Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand" > NAMESPACE

check: NAMESPACE
	Rscript -e "devtools::check()"

```

But I wonder if devtools could take care of this somehow?  Since `NAMESPACE` is autogenerated by Roxygen2, I don't want to commit it to the repository.

description:

By the time I see this message the blah.Rcheck directory has already been deleted. However I found that if I run `devtools::check()` from the console it will run in a temporary directory (e.g.  ‘/tmp/RtmpsD063J/blah.Rcheck/00check.log’) which is around long enough to inspect. In the `00install.out` file there is some additional information on the error:

title: namespace does not delete old information when @importFrom changes
description:
Suppose I maintain two packages, call them `foo` and `bar`. `bar` exports a function `baz` and `foo` imports it in the help.R file using `@importFrom`, i.e., in foo/R/help.R there is a line `@importFrom bar baz`. When I `document` the namespace file is correctly created so it has `importFrom(bar,baz)`.

Now suppose, I change the name of `baz` to `bash` in the `bar` package. I update foo/R/help.R to `@importFrom bar bash`. When I `document` though, the namespace correctly adds `importFrom(bar,bash)` but it does not delete `importFrom(bar,baz)` so I get errors when running `install`. 

I am using the `clean = TRUE` argument thinking that would clean this as well, but it seems like that only goes to the man files. Am I missing something here? Or is this a bug?

Thanks!

``` r
#> Warning: running command 'cp -R . "C:/Users/user1/Documents/R/win-library/3.3/dlm" || ( internal cd - .| (cd "C:/Users/user1/Documents/R/win-library/3.3/dlm" && internal -xf -))' had status 1
#> ERROR: installing binary package failed
#> * removing 'C:/Users/user1/Documents/R/win-library/3.3/dlm'
#> Error: Command failed (1)
```

I've dived into the R source code. This code 

> Warning: running command 'cp -R . "C:/Users/user1/Documents/R/win-library/3.3/dlm" || ( internal cd - .| (cd "C:/Users/user1/Documents/R/win-library/3.3/dlm" && internal -xf -))' had status 1

is from around [here](https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/4f6493d96182944815e329bfa3a7dbeb2023b821/src/library/tools/R/install.R#L385-L387).

``` r
        res <- system(paste("cp -R .", shQuote(instdir),
                            "|| (", TAR, "cd - .| (cd", shQuote(instdir), "&&", TAR, "-xf -))"
                            ))
```

But it says this `do_install_binary()` is for [Unix only](https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/4f6493d96182944815e329bfa3a7dbeb2023b821/src/library/tools/R/install.R#L373). This means something is wrong that this part of code is executed on Windows platform.

The correct way of installing binary packages on Windows platform seems to be [using ZIP archive without decompressing](https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/4f6493d96182944815e329bfa3a7dbeb2023b821/src/library/tools/R/install.R#L247-L253). I suspect the problem is that `install_remote()` does not follow the way; it seems to ALWAYS `decompress()` package archives, around [here](https://github.com/hadley/devtools/blob/39222f8cbbc82cdc719a48746bc6b912a45a58a5/R/install-remote.R#L33)

Could you consider adding condition branch for Windows?

title: FR: Re-test only failing tests
description:
Often, I change some code, run the tests, just to notice failures. I then fix the code and re-run the tests until they pass. In this scenario I'm usually not interested in rerunning all tests, just the ones that failed.

Some GUIs for other environments offer a "re-run failing" button. For testthat, I need to use a filter, but I need to manually construct it, and I can't run the test in the "Build" pane of RStudio.

Can `devtools::test()` write a list with failing tests, and pick it up and use it as a filter on the next run of `devtools::test(filter = NULL)`? That file would be cleared once all tests are successful.

If we manage to output to the build pane (https://github.com/hadley/devtools/issues/1650#issuecomment-343465350), this could be done with an add-in too.

title: [install_github] GITHUB_PAT error for public R packages on GitLab Pages
description:
Hey,

I'm struggling to install R packages from Github inside a GitLab runner. 

This is my setup:
I'm trying to set up a GitLab Runner to display a gitbook generated using the **bookdown** package on a GitLab server.

Since GitLab doesn't work with a service like Travis but with Docker images, I created a Docker image containing both R-3.4.0 and loads of dependencies my package needs. Since I want to have the newest version of my package, I advice the script to install it using **devtools::install_github()**. My **.gitlab-ci.yml** looks like

```
image: thegreatwhiteshark/climex-r-ubuntu:1.0.0

pages:
  stage: deploy
  before_script:
    # - mkdir tmpBuild
    # - cd tmpBuild
    # - git clone https://github.com/theGreatWhiteShark/climex.git
    # - cd climex
    # - R -q -e 'devtools::install()'
    - R -q -e 'devtools::install_github("theGreatWhiteShark/climex" )'
  script:
    - R -q -e 'bookdown::render_book( "01-introduction.Rmd", "bookdown::gitbook()" )'
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - public
  only:
    - master
```

Now whenever the CI is running it already fails in the *before_script* part. The **install_github()** commands produces
```
> devtools::install_github( "theGreatWhiteShark/climex" )
Using bundled GitHub PAT. Please add your own PAT to the env var `GITHUB_PAT`
Downloading GitHub repo theGreatWhiteShark/climex@master
from URL https://api.github.com/repos/theGreatWhiteShark/climex/zipball/master
Installation failed: error in running command
```
The commented code unfortunately fails as well, since my package depends on two other R packages hosted on Github.

I'm using **devtools_1.13.4**

Reading [the github](https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/github.html) section of the bookdown book I understand one needs the GITHUB_PAT to access private repositories or to provide write permission for a service, e.g. like Travis.

But **all packages** I want to install are **public**. The repository I install the packages into is private, but I don't see how this would affect the package installation. 

So, can you explain to me why a personal access token is required here? And if it is really necessary, how would the encryption of the token looks like? `travis encrypt` is a Github-only solution.

Cheers 

P.S. The docker image is using Ubuntu 16.04 and both the installation from the repositories of the system and the installation of R packages using **install.packages()** works within it.

title: install_local() fails for package source files
description:
In **devtools** 1.13.4,

    example(install_local, run.dontrun = TRUE)

(which essentially tries to `install_local("testthat_1.0.2.tar.gz")`), fails with "Installation failed: cannot open the connection". This is because (at least) `remote_sha.local_remote()` and `remote_package_name.local_remote()` assume `remote$path` to point to a source directory, ignoring that the remote could be a compressed package source file (as documented).

Note that this issue does not occur in the implementation of the [**remotes**](https://github.com/r-lib/remotes) package, so one may simply use `remotes::install_local()` instead of the **devtools** version.

title: Provide advice for dealing with the diaspora
description:
I'd like some guidance on how the developers expect people to use *devtools* after the decomposition (into *remotes*, *usethis*, etc.) is complete. There are a few possible options.

### 1. Everyone still uses *devtools*

The business-as-usual option is that end users continue to use *devtools* just as before, and the decomposition into smaller packages is for the benefit of *devtools* developers only.

In this case, it would be useful to know how this is implemented. Would *devtools* attach the underlying packages (like *tidyverse* does)? Would it import and reexport everything (like *assertive* does)? Would it contain higher-level wrapper functions (like *rmarkdown* wraps *knitr*)?

### 2. Nobody uses *devtools*

The other extreme is that *devtools* is deprecated and everyone has to use the new packages for all tasks.

If this is the case, what's the timeline for deprecating the code? Are all the other packages ready for real-world use? That is, is it possible to completely ignore *devtools* yet?

### 3. *devtools* is used for some tasks

The in-between state is that devtools retains some functionality of its own, but other bits are farmed out exclusively to other packages.

In this case it would be useful to know which bits of functionality will stay in devtools and which bits will be fully outsourced.

----

The Diaspora section of the README states

> Generally, you should not need to worry about these different packages, because devtools installs them all automatically. You will need to care, however, if you're filing a bug because reporting it at the correct place will lead to a speedier resolution.

This suggests that (at least in the near future), it is expected that people are supposed to use *devtools*.

----

Contradicting this is that 

1. The `with_*` functions were deprecated and then removed once the *withr* was created.

2. The [`infrastructure.R`](https://github.com/hadley/devtools/blob/dcf77730da87ef7bdf45a5bd143c36c8e7490f11/R/infrastructure.R) file shows that the `use_*` functions are deprecated (and presumably will be removed shortly).

----

For context, DataCamp is making a course on creating R packages that features *devtools* quite heavily, and we need some guidance on what to tell students. Since video content is tricky to change, it would be helpful to know the long term plan.

Here is an example that may work. It has an extra parameter 'except_pkgs'
Only the code
```r
pkgs <- setdiff(pkgs, except_pkgs)
```

restricts the packages.

```r
update_packages <- function (pkgs = NULL, except_pkgs = NULL, dependencies = NA, repos = getOption("repos"), 
    type = getOption("pkgType"))
{
    if (isTRUE(pkgs)) {
        pkgs <- installed.packages()[, "Package"]
    }

    update(pkgs)
```

Run.

description:
Hi,

I know that the issue of `R CMD check` and the copious amounts of `no visible binding for global variable [variable name]` NOTES it produces has been raised in other forums (e.g., on StackOverflow: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/9439256/how-can-i-handle-r-cmd-check-no-visible-binding-for-global-variable-notes-when, or in the context of other packages: https://github.com/tidyverse/magrittr/issues/29), but the solutions provided therein are either not satisfactory or are actually problematic to the package since the solutions themselves introduce some additional notes/warnings, especially if this is your first time developing package and you are encountering this problem for the first time. 

So I was wondering if the future release of `devtools` can have some routines that automatically take the necessary steps to remove this particular breed of NOTES (e.g., automatically adding necessary variables via `globalVariables(c(...))` or setting them to `NULL`, etc.) since it seems like a very common problem that people encounter and is frustrating to get rid off.

title: `utils::help` and `dev_help` have incompatible behavior
description:
This is a bit of an edge case, but `devtools::help` and `utils::help` have different behavior when called with assignment. `utils::help` does not open the help viewer and returns an object that includes the path to the documentation database and some additional attributes:

```r
a <-utils::help("mean")    # does not open the help viewer
str(a)
# Class 'help_files_with_topic'  atomic [1:1] /usr/lib64/R/library/base/help/mean
#   ..- attr(*, "call")= language (function (topic, package = NULL, lib.loc = NULL, verbose = getOption("verbose"), try.all.packages = getOption("h| __truncated__ ...
#   ..- attr(*, "topic")= chr "mean"
#   ..- attr(*, "tried_all_packages")= logi FALSE
#   ..- attr(*, "type")= chr "text"
```

There are useful things once can do with that path (e.g. the [`gbRd` package](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/gbRd/index.html)).

On the other hand, `devtools::dev_help` returns `NULL` and, more importantly, _always_ opens the help viewer.

```r
devtools::load_all("/path/to/my_package")
b <- help("my_dev_function")    # still opens the help viewer
str(b)
# NULL
```

Returning `NULL` isn't a huge problem (though it would be nicer if the output more closely matched that of `utils::help`), but always opening the help viewer even in assignment is unexpected and can be rather disruptive. For instance, it led to a rather insidious bug in Nvim-R's vim completion functions (https://github.com/jalvesaq/Nvim-R/pull/292).

title: `load_all` handle namespace collision warnings
description:
# Problem

`devtools::load_all` does not propagate the warnings about namespace collisions nicely.  It returns `Warning: character(0)` instead of anything useful.  

# Desired behavior

The errors shown by R CMD CHECK would ideally be propagated back through the `devtools::load_all()` output when the namespace collision is identified.

# stack trace

```r
options(warn = 2)
devtools::load_all()
# Loading namespacecollision
#Error: (converted from warning) (converted from warning) character(0)
traceback()
#10: doWithOneRestart(return(expr), restart)
#9: withOneRestart(expr, restarts[[1L]])
#8: withRestarts({
#       .Internal(.signalCondition(cond, message, call))
#       .Internal(.dfltWarn(message, call))
#   }, muffleWarning = function() NULL)
#7: value[[3L]](cond)
#6: tryCatchOne(expr, names, parentenv, handlers[[1L]])
#5: tryCatchList(expr, classes, parentenv, handlers)
#4: tryCatch(error = warning, {
#       if (is.character(i)) 
#           namespaceImport(ns, loadNamespace(i, c(lib.loc, .libPaths()), 
#               versionCheck = vI[[i]]), from = package)
#       else if (!is.null(i$except)) 
#           namespaceImport(ns, loadNamespace(j <- i[[1L]], c(lib.loc, 
#               .libPaths()), versionCheck = vI[[j]]), from = package, 
#               except = i$except)
#       else namespaceImportFrom(ns, loadNamespace(j <- i[[1L]], 
#           c(lib.loc, .libPaths()), versionCheck = vI[[j]]), i[[2L]], 
#           from = package)
#   })
#3: process_imports(pkg)
#2: load_imports(pkg)
#1: devtools::load_all()
```

# To reprex

1. create a new package
2. Add a file with the following (`rlang` and `testthat` are lightweight-ish packages that have 3 namespace collisions at present):
```r
#' @import rlang
#' @import testthat
"_PACKAGE"
```

3. execute `roxygen2::roxygenize()`

Then we get:
```r
devtools::load_all("/path/to/namespacecollision")
#> Loading namespacecollision
#> Warning: character(0)

#> Warning: character(0)

#> Warning: character(0)
```

In `R CMD CHECK`, these warnings are handled a bit nicer:
```r
Warning: replacing previous import ‘rlang::is_null’ by ‘testthat::is_null’ when loading ‘namespacecollision’
  Warning: replacing previous import ‘rlang::is_true’ by ‘testthat::is_true’ when loading ‘namespacecollision’
  Warning: replacing previous import ‘rlang::is_false’ by ‘testthat::is_false’ when loading ‘namespacecollision’
```

title: Devtools encoding
description:
On my computer, Rstudio opens all file in UTF-8 by default. However, when I use devtools::load_all("."), it seems that the code is loaded using the system locale.

I've created a new package project in Rstudio and I only have one file: test.R. In this file I've put the following code:

    test_print <- function(){
        print("€")
    }

If I then save the file, use devtools::load_all(".") and execute the function, I see the following output:

    > test_print()
    â¬

However, I've explicitly used the save with encoding option in RStudio (in UTF-8). The mistake in encoding can be seen when I set a debug pointer on the print line. Suddenly I see the following code:

    test_print <- function(){
        print("â¬")
    }

But if I source the function straight from RStudio, then it works as expected and prints the euro sign: €.

The same behaviour is achieved when I build the package (using build and reload in Rstudio). Using mypackage:::test_print() also yields the desired normal euro sign.

I don't know if it can be specified anywhere, but it would be nice to source the files with load_all() using the UTF-8 encoding.
